stories.title: Celtics to extend guard Payton Pritchard on 2-year, $44.2M deal
stories.summary: Celtics guard Payton Pritchard has agreed to a two-year, $44.2 million extension with a mutual option for the 2029-30 season.
stories.detailText: Boston Celtics guard Payton Pritchard has agreed to a two-year, $44.2 million contract extension, plus a mutual option in the 2029-30 season, CAA co-head of basketball Austin Brown and agent Max Saidman told ESPN on Tuesday. Pritchard -- the 2024 NBA champion and 2025 Sixth Man of the Year -- cashes in on a fully guaranteed two-year max extension to keep him a key long-term member of the retooled Celtics after the 6-foot-1 guard averaged career highs in points (17), assists (5.2) and rebounds (3.9) last season. The deal keeps Pritchard for an additional season after his current deal ends in 2028. Pritchard will be set to make over $21 million for the 2028-29 season before a mutual option in 2029-30 worth nearly $23 million. That mutual option allows either side to opt in for the final season of Pritchard's contract in 2029-30, which also opens the window for extension conversations that summer. Pritchard is currently playing on a deal that pays him $7.8 million this season and $8.3 million next year. Pritchard blossomed last season while starting 50 games, helping to ease the loss of Jayson Tatum for most of last season by taking an increased role in the offense. His touches per game went from 51.8 in 2024-25 to nearly 70 last season, the second-largest increase among the 33 players to record at least 4,000 touches in each season. Pritchard, 28, is one of four players to make at least 200 3-pointers in multiple seasons in Celtics history, along with Tatum, Derrick White and Antoine Walker . He has also been incredibly durable in his six NBA seasons; his 241 games played over the last three years is tied for the third-most in the league during that span. The deal takes Pritchard, the No. 26 pick for the Celtics in the 2020 NBA draft, through at least his ninth season in Boston, and potentially Year 10 if the option is picked up.

stories.title: Payton Pritchard contract extension: What it means for Celtics, former Sixth Man of the Year
stories.summary: Payton Pritchard, a key scoring spark for the Boston Celtics, was just rewarded after he averaged career highs in points, assists and rebounds.
stories.detailText: A key piece of the revamped Boston Celtics secured his short-term future with the franchise. Guard Payton Pritchard, the 2024-25 Sixth Man of the Year, has agreed to a two-year, $44.2 million contract extension with the Celtics, with the 2029-30 season being a mutual option, according to ESPN . Messages left for Pritchard’s representatives were not immediately returned. As star forward Jayson Tatum missed much of last season, Pritchard took on more responsibility, becoming one of Boston’s primary shot makers; Pritchard averaged career highs in scoring (17.0 points per game), rebounding (3.9) and assists (5.2). Pritchard started 50 of his 79 games last season, but appears likely to resume his role as Boston’s sixth man. In the team’s preseason game against the 76ers Saturday, Oct. 10, which was something of a dress rehearsal for the Celtics, Pritchard came off the bench, before eventually leading the team with 25 points on 7-of-12 shooting. The Celtics are embarking on a new era after trading away former star Jaylen Brown to the 76ers. Boston will be incorporating Paul George, who scored 13 points on 3-of-10 shooting against his former team, into the lineup. Either way, Pritchard figures to remain a central scorer and one who often closes games on the floor because of his shooting and scoring. This article originally appeared on USA TODAY: Payton Pritchard contract extension: What it means for Celtics, former Sixth Man of the Year

stories.title: Celtics reportedly reach contract extension with Payton Pritchard for two years, $44.2 million
stories.summary: The former Sixth Man of the Year stays with the only franchise he's ever played for.
stories.detailText: It's tough to envision Payton Pritchard in any uniform other than Boston Celtics green. Now, nobody will have to, at least for a few more years. The Celtics and Pritchard have agreed to a two-year, $44.2 million contract extension that keeps him in Boston, his agent told Shams Charania of ESPN . Pritchard has two more years on what is a steal of a contract ($7.2 million this season, $7.8 million in 2027-28) then he will get a massive raise starting in 2028-29 to likely $21.3 million. The deal includes a mutual option for the 2029-30 season. This is the max extension the Celtics can give Pritchard under the CBA, and it rewards his years of quality play. That said, this is a good deal for both sides. Pritchard — a key part of the 2024 championship Celtics and the 2025 Sixth Man of the Year — somewhat quietly had his best season as a pro last season, when stepping up to fill in with Jayson Tatum injured and Jrue Holiday traded. Pitchard, 28, started 50 games for the Celtics and averaged 17 points, 5.2 assists and 3.9 rebounds per game — all career highs — while shooting 37.7% from beyond the arc. Boston has locked up a couple of other key role players this offseason, Neemias Queta (four years, $56 million) and Jordan Walsh (three years, $15.75 million).

Windhorst on the growth of the NBA around the world: "I think the flow of international players into the NBA is even going to grow because of two things. One, the NBA is expanding to Europe. The ramifications of the Hukporti injury for Philadelphia The season ending Achilles injury to Ariel Hukporti has roster ramifications for the 76ers. Philadelphia is $1.8 million below the first apron, so they are not allowed to sign a player with their open roster spot until Dec. 4. The 76ers could create financial flexibility but at the cost of Jabari Walker , whose $2.6 million salary is guaranteed for only $250,000. Walker scored 11 points and grabbed 11 rebounds in their pre-season opener. The 76ers do have an open two-way spot and can sign a player with three years or less in service. Beyond starter Joel Embiid , Philadelphia's frontcourt depth is Dean Wade , Adem Bona , Dominick Barlow and Walker. -- Bobby Marks Charania: Hukporti sustained a season-ending ruptured Achilles An MRI confirm Tuesday that Philadelphia 76ers ' center Ariel Hukporti sustained a season-ending torn right Achilles, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania. Hukporti will undergo surgery for the injury later today. Doncic, who 'worked his butt off all summer,' lights up Kings A lighter Luka Doncic scored an easy 21 first-half points in the Los Angeles Lakers ' preseason opener over the Sacramento Kings on Monday night, needing only 16 minutes to sharpen up his game in a 127-103 blowout in Sacramento. Doncic was listed at 244 pounds prior to the 2025-26 season. That dipped to 230 pounds entering training camp. The difference in physique from his heavier days is obvious. "The guy worked his butt off all summer staying in shape and actually ran this summer," coach JJ Redick said. "He actually did like sprints and stuff. Came into camp in fantastic shape." The Lakers were without Austin Reaves and Walker Kessler in the preseason opener. Reaves tweaked his ankle recently, and Kessler jammed a finger on the backboard. Both are listed as day-to-day. Without either, the Lakers still rolled through the Kings. Doncic scored all 21 of his points in a 73-point Lakers first half, resting while the backups finished the job. He made three 3s, four shots in the paint and got to the line for nine free throws. "For someone who normally plays a ton of live basketball [in the summer], he didn't do as much of that by design," Redick said. "We've seen him literally every day in camp incrementally get more and more in rhythm." Doncic badly strained his hamstring in early April and missed the entire Lakers playoff run while rehabbing the injury. He said he felt "great" against the Kings but downplayed any larger changes to his training regimen. "I feel probably a little more rested," Doncic said. "I didn't play [on the Slovenian] national team." -- Anthony Slater Hoop Collective: Biggest questions in the NBA's Southwest Division Brian is joined by ESPN's Tim MacMahon and Michael C. Wright to preview the NBA's Southwest Division, including the biggest questions facing each team heading into the 2026-27 season. Knicks' Karl-Anthony Towns not expecting extension soon New York Knicks center Karl-Anthony Towns said Monday that, "It don't look good" in regards to him and the franchise agreeing to a contract extension before the start of the season. "Simply put, I want to do something that can keep the team together and work with the Knicks and also values me," Towns said. "None of those things have come close to happening." "So far, these sides are not close" Oct. 2 Hawkins, Grizzlies mutually agree to part ways The Memphis Grizzlies and guard Jordan Hawkins have agreed to part ways via waivers, allowing the 2023 lottery pick to find a new home in free agency, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania. The move comes three weeks after arriving as part of a four-player trade with the New Orleans Pelicans for AJ Johnson and Taj Gibson . Hawkins, 24, averaged 5.1 points in 51 games last season and struggled to find consistent playing time in New Orleans' crowded backcourt rotation. The former UConn star played just 13.6 minutes per game, a significant decrease from the 2024-25 season, when he played 23.6 minutes per game and averaged 10.8 points per game. With Draymond and Steph Curry on the floor together, it was still plus-105 last year, still a good offensive rating,117.7, but the moment Steph's been off the floor, and last year he was off the floor a lot, their offense cratered when Draymond was on the floor and was actually OK when it was no Draymond and no Steph. "I've had these conversations with Steve [Kerr] and again I think you're going to hear it a lot publicly in their messaging, they're going to adapt the offense at times away from Draymond. They're going to try to make him more of a spot-up shooter at times instead of giving him the ball. They're trying to limit his turnovers." Mitch Johnson excited about Billy Donovan's role with Spurs San Antonio Spurs coach Mitch Johnson likes what he's seen so far at training camp from new lead assistant coach Billy Donovan. "I don't want to be naive enough to think I'm going to tell you what a 61-year old Hall of Fame coach like Billy Donovan and his resume can bring to the table," Johnson said. "I'm excited he's here. He's a tremendous person, great personality, fits in seamlessly. He's got worlds of experience and he's an extremely hard worker. He's not kicking up his feet and telling stories. He's rolling his sleeves up and getting his hands dirty. He's going to help all of us and probably me, specifically, a ton this year." Donovan joined the staff in July, replacing former lead assistant Sean Sweeney, who left San Antonio to take the head coaching job in Orlando. Sweeney ran the Spurs' defense last season, helping it improve from 25th to third in the NBA in defensive rating (110.4). Donovan won't be tasked with taking on Sweeney's responsibilities, according to sources, however. San Antonio brought in Donovan to lean on his experience on both ends of the floor, as well as his vast knowledge of the NBA and college games. A member of the Naismith Basketball Hall of Fame class of 2025, Donovan joined the Spurs after 11 seasons as an NBA coach with the Chicago Bulls and Oklahoma City Thunder , after capturing two college basketball national titles in 2006 and 2007 with the Florida Gators. -- Michael C. Sept. 30 Nuggets add Nembhard on two-way deal Guard Ryan Nembhard has agreed to a two-way contract with the Denver Nuggets , sources told ESPN's Shams Charania . Nembhard, 23, played 60 games (27 starts) for the Dallas Mavericks in 2025-26 after signing as an undrafted free agent. He was traded to the Atlanta Hawks then to the Charlotte Hornets this offseason before being waived. Sept. 29 Charania: NBA reviewing finalists' bids for Vegas team ESPN's Shams Charania reported that the NBA is currently reviewing finalist bids for a new expansion team in Las Vegas. The price range is currently speculated at $12-13 billion with a new arena factored into the cost. The three final groups are Nancy Walton Laurie and Bill Laurie; Steve Apostolopoulos and Marc Lasry; Bill Foley and Jerry Colangelo, sources told ESPN. Will KAT take a pay cut in next Knicks deal? On "NBA Today," ESPN's Malika Andrews detailed Karl-Anthony Towns ' mindset toward contract negotiations with the defending champion New York Knicks . "Towns, from what I have been told, is willing -- similarly to what Jalen Brunson did [but the] numbers aren't the same -- to take a pay cut," Andrews said. "But the pay cut that the Knicks are asking him to take, he views as unreasonable." Towns, 30, is eligible to sign a four-year, $276 million extension through June 30. Embiid "full participant" in first Sixers' practice Joel Embiid was a "full participant all the way through" for the Philadelphia 76ers first practice of training camp, Sixers coach Nick Nurse said Tuesday. "He looked great," Nurse said of Embiid. "Very, very good news from the standpoint of where it's been the last couple years, last couple summers leading into today. ... It's great to see." After being named the league MVP in 2023, the 32-year-old center has missed 150 games over the last three seasons because of various injuries. He also sat out four of the Sixers' 11 playoff games in the spring because of appendicitis, right hip soreness and a right ankle sprain. The only Sixers player who did not participate in Tuesday's practice according to a team spokesperson was backup big man Adem Bona , who is dealing with a sprained left foot. Anfernee Simons , who signed a two-year, $12.3 million contract to join Philadelphia in July, said Embiid's presence in the gym was already notable leading up to the start of camp. "Everybody's been impressed around here about how he's come in and worked," Simons said. "Joel is going to be Joel. He's going to be a dominant player always. We just want to continue for him to be himself, as well, and I think everybody's going to be able to work around that." Despite the injuries, the 10-year veteran still averaged 26.9 points, 7.7 rebounds, 3.9 assists and 1.2 blocks per game last season. Embiid's inclusion only added to what several Sixers players described as an "exciting" opening day with LeBron James and Jaylen Brown completing their first official practice with the franchise. "With any team, we got to start somewhere, and then we got to get better and better, and just keep trying to reach our ceiling, right?" Nurse said. "That happens day-to-day. Can we get up tomorrow, like, 98% as excited as we did today? It's going to be hard to get as excited as we all were today, right? "But we need to come back, and we need to keep climbing that mountain. That's a daily process. I just want them to reach their potential. If they do, great things are going to happen." -- Dave McMenamin Hoop Collective: The 2026 NBA Media Day reaction special Brian Windhorst is joined by ESPN reporters from around the league to check in on Monday's Media Days. Tim MacMahon, Dave McMenamin, Vince Goodwill, Jamal Collier, Anthony Slater and Michael C. Wright all hop on the podcast to discuss the biggest storylines throughout the NBA ahead of training camp. Latest episodes of the 'Hoop Collective' podcast Top NBA media day headlines LeBron says he envisioned joining Knicks as free agent | Philly stars ready to 'sacrifice' Clippers apologize to fans, vow to move past investigation | Ingram (Achilles) out Edwards happy to cede Wolves' PG duties to Ball Wizards, AD to wait until summer for extension talks Karl-Anthony Towns wants extension to stay with Knicks Jokic on his next Nuggets deal: 'I'm going to sign next year' Bronny on LeBron James' Lakers exit: 'He's got his own path' Sept. 28 Bronny on LeBron James' Lakers exit: 'He's got his own path' When LeBron James chose to leave the Los Angeles Lakers in free agency over the summer, he consulted his family on the decision to sign with the Philadelphia 76ers . But when it came to his son/teammate Bronny, much was apparently left unsaid . "We're men of very little words when it comes to talking about business and what we're going to do and how we feel about each other. So it wasn't really much [discussion] to be honest with you," Bronny James said Monday at Lakers media day. "He's got his own path and I got my own. He knows that I want to make a name for myself and I want to continue my career and keep growing as a player. And he knows that I want to focus on that. So he decided to do that." LeBron and Bronny have routinely been in unique situations in league history, whether it was opening night two years ago, when the father and son entered the game together, or last year in the playoffs, where they combined to deliver a 10-0 run during a victory over the Houston Rockets . Navigating a complex free agency in which the father leaves and the son stays is another one for the books. Tatum 'comfortable' leading new-look Celtics post-Brown trade Jayson Tatum 's one constant during his development into a star with the Boston Celtics was having Jaylen Brown as a teammate. That partnership ended this offseason when the Celtics' front office decided to trade Brown -- the 2024 NBA Finals MVP -- to the Philadelphia 76ers in what was largely a cost-cutting move that broke up the duo most responsible for leading Boston to the 2024 NBA championship. "The business of the NBA comes and plays a part at some point. And I've seen it in my almost 10 years in this league," Tatum said during Celtics media day on Monday . "For me it's more so being grateful for what we accomplished and what he means for this city and to this organization. Just the ups and downs in our career that we were able to grow and learn from and made us the players that we are today. So really just being thankful for those nine years." Suns owner Ishbia says mortgage company woes won't hurt team It's well-known at this point that billionaire Mat Ishbia's mortgage company has had a rough financial stretch. The owner of the Phoenix Suns said Monday that will have "zero" effect on his spending habits when it comes to basketball. In fact, the 46-year-old said he's working on purchasing 14% more of the team, bringing his total to roughly 80%. Ishbia's company -- United Wholesale Mortgage -- suffered a reported $450 million net loss in the second quarter this year, calling into question if the sizable dip would affect his basketball business. The outspoken Ishbia was adamant that nothing would change for the NBA franchise when it comes to spending on players or the fan experience. Williamson not where he wants to be New Orleans Pelicans forward Zion Williamson kept his answer brief when asked how he would summarize his first seven years as an NBA player. "I'm not where I want to be," said Williamson, whom the Pelicans drafted with the No. 1 pick out of Duke in 2019. "I'm not where I need to be." Butler indicates he is 'ahead' in his knee rehab Nearing the eight-month mark since his right ACL surgery , Jimmy Butler III is hesitant to put a specific target date on his eventual NBA return, but he did express optimism in advance of Golden State Warriors training camp. "I promise you I'm coming back, and it's going to be -- I think it's going to be, like, real eye-popping for everybody how I'm still going to be nice," Butler said. "Probably nicer, honestly." Butler has only recently advanced to running, and he will be limited to light on-court individual work when the team begins practice in Hawaii on Tuesday afternoon. It will be several weeks before Butler is expected to advance to a more rigorous stage of his rehab, and the team's lead medical decision-maker, Rick Celebrini, is known for his cautiousness in the later stages of the rehab process. A January or February return can be considered on the optimistic side for Butler, who turned 37 earlier this month. But Butler did say that the strengthening tests on the knee indicate he is ahead of schedule. "My numbers are staggering," Butler said. "They're off the charts. I'm ahead, so they say. So, I just know that all the work that I've been doing, whether it be at home, in L.A., in Europe, in South America, wherever the case may be, I've been doing all the right things. So, I am confident that whenever I come back, I'll be more than ready, I'll be more than healthy and I'll be a better all-around player than I was whenever I went down." -- Anthony Slater Pistons eye "better version" of Cunningham Detroit Pistons coach J.B. Bickerstaff has held many offseason conversations with All-NBA guard Cade Cunningham about seizing greatness and the necessary steps toward improving after last year's playoff run that stretched to Game 7 of the Eastern Conference semifinals. Bickerstaff has guaranteed "a better version" Cunningham this season, which could be a scary sight after he averaged 23.9 points, 9.9 assists, 5.5 rebounds and 1.4 steals in 33.9 minutes during 2025-26. But Cunningham also led the East in turnovers per game after finishing with the second most in 2024-25. "I don't have to challenge Cade, and that's why he is who he is," Bickerstaff said. "Because he's pulling. He's not being pushed." Cunningham showed up in a fresh pair of Nike S.T. Charge "Detroit Tough" sneakers in Pistons colors. He will also receive his own signature Nike shoe, which is expected to debut during the second half of the season. "I'm thankful to be in these shoes. I'm thankful to have the opportunity to represent my family in this way," Cunningham said. "Represent where I come from, but then to represent the city of Detroit. "In a city like this, it's a blessing. I'm thankful for it, I don't take it for granted and I'm trying to make the most out of it." -- Eric Woodyard Hornets waive former No. 8 pick Dillingham The Charlotte Hornets are waiving guard Rob Dillingham , sources told ESPN's Shams Charania . Dillingham was traded from the Chicago Bulls on Saturday for Buddy Hield and cash. The Hornets created a $9.6 million trade exception with the move. Dillingham, 21, appeared in 30 games for the Bulls last season, averaging 9.6 points and 2.8 assists. SGA on chance at historic third straight MVP At Oklahoma City Thunder media day, guard Shai Gilgeous-Alexander discussed the possibility of winning a third straight NBA MVP award and whether that's something he ponders going into this season. "No different than any other year: Try to be the best player I can be, try to implement the things I just worked on," Gilgeous-Alexander said. "The decision for MVP is literally 82 games away. I'm not going to win the award in the first week of the season. ... That kind of recipe for me in the past has kind of worked, and I've been fortunate to win two in a row. "We need to be laser focused on ourselves. We need to take the lessons from that [Western Conference finals] series, for sure, and we did. But it's certainly not something that we overcorrect for, because you end up chasing your shadow, and it prevents you from being your best as you move forward." ESPN's Summer Forecast gave Gilgeous-Alexander the fourth-best chance at the 2027 MVP, behind Victor Wembanyama , Nikola Jokic and Luka Doncic . No player has won three consecutive MVPs since Larry Bird in 1984, 1985 and 1986. -- Baxter Holmes Doncic talks LeBron exit, Lakers "championship" ceiling Speaking to ESPN's Brian Windhorst during Los Angeles Lakers media day, guard Luka Doncic detailed his reaction to LeBron James leaving for the Philadelphia 76ers this past summer and why he thinks a successful 2026-27 includes a Lakers run to the title: "It was kind of sad. Playing with LeBron was amazing. There's a lot of things I learned from him. ... We all know who LeBron James is." Shams: Duren's relationship with Pistons "has fractures" Simmons "didn't touch a ball for a year" During Sacramento Kings media day, guard Ben Simmons laid out the reasons he chose the Kings and why he's excited for the 2026-27 season. "The expectations are low. I feel like that's been something on me too, so we can relate in that way," Simmons told reporters. "I think we have a chip on our shoulder." Simmons last played in 2024-25, appearing in 51 games for the Brooklyn Nets and LA Clippers . The three-time All-Star said the time away gave him the chance to focus on "getting my body right and my mind right." Pistons GM hasn't spoken with Duren all summer Jalen Duren and the Detroit Pistons have a decision to make as the clock ticks closer to Oct. 1 -- the deadline to sign a one-year, $9.6 million qualifying offer. For Duren, he can accept the five-year, $200 million contract that has been offered by Detroit or he can become the first player named All-NBA or All-Star to sign the qualifying offer. If he chooses the latter, Duren will hold veto power on any trade this season and be an unrestricted free agent next summer. For the Pistons, weighing the risk of having an All-NBA player on a one-year contract and, more importantly, the likelihood he will depart next summer as a free agent is key. There are eight projected teams that have significant cap space to sign Duren to a four-year, $189 million max contract. "I can't control the different things that he does or his group does," Pistons president of basketball operations Trajan Langdon said at media day. "For me, it's control what we can and letting him know he is a big part of what we do." Langdon also said he hasn't spoken with Duren all summer during Pistons media day. -- Bobby Marks Mitchell: LeBron to Cavs made sense "for a lot of reasons" At Cavaliers media day, Donovan Mitchell said that in his mind, he thought LeBron James would return to Cleveland because "for a lot of reasons it made sense." "I didn't think Philly. I thought if he didn't come here, it'd be Golden State," Mitchell said. After being swept in the Eastern Conference finals by the eventual champion New York Knicks then missing out on James in free agency, Cleveland kept its core intact. The Cavs signed Mitchell to a four-year, $273 million maximum extension and re-signed James Harden to a three-year, $97 million contract. Cleveland did make one major addition by acquiring Peyton Watson from the Denver Nuggets in a multiteam trade then signing the restricted free agent to a four-year, $88 million deal. Speaking for the first time since their extensions, Mitchell and Harden both said their approaches to their new deals -- Mitchell signing as soon as he was eligible with Harden opting out to give Cleveland more flexibility to make moves -- reflected a team-first mindset. "This is something that I want to do, and I want to win a championship," Harden said. "So, what does that look like? Making the team better, making the team whole to where we give ourselves a chance. By the way, you can have the best talented team, which I've been on before, and still not win. "We waited, waited, waited until the front office called me, made sure that we got everything that we can get, and then we signed. We got a long way to go, but I love the direction and steps that we're taking here as a unit from top to bottom." -- Daniel Oyefusi MacMahon: Thunder adjusting to roster changes The departures of three championship-winning teammates doesn't yet feel like reality for Thunder superstar Shai Gilgeous-Alexander , who kidded that he still expected Luguentz Dort , Isaiah Joe and Aaron Wiggins to show up for Oklahoma City's team picture Monday afternoon. "It's the business of the NBA, right?" Gilgeous-Alexander said, referring to the series of financially motivated trades. "I don't think anybody has played with all 12 guys their whole career. It sucks a little bit. "My mind never even went to what we were going to be like on the court. It was more like the brotherhood." As fellow OKC guard Jalen Williams added, "It's the weirdest thing ever." -- Tim MacMahon Clippers announce Ingram has partially torn Achilles The LA Clippers announced they found a partially torn Achilles tendon in Brandon Ingram 's foot after his recent heel surgery. He will miss the start of the 2026-27 season. Jokic: "I'm gonna sign next year" Denver Nuggets center Nikola Jokic reiterated his commitment to the franchise at Monday's media day. "I'm gonna sign next year," Jokic said. "If they want me." Curry said knee is ready to go for the season Golden State Warriors superstar guard Stephen Curry addressed the media Monday in offering positive updates on his injured knee. "Knee's feeling great. Ready to go. No issues," Curry said. "I feel a lot stronger and understanding of what I'm dealing with." Curry did acknowledge a "management element" but said there are currently no restrictions. Nuggets confident in Jokic's future with franchise Members of the Denver Nuggets ' front office, general manager Jon Wallace and executive vice president of basketball Ben Tenzer addressed the media on Monday and answered questions regarding Nikola Jokic 's future with the franchise. The three-time MVP didn't sign an extension this offseason. "We feel very comfortable with the relation and trust there," Tenzer said. "We have no concerns." LeBron: I wanted to finish my career with the Knicks New Philadelphia 76er LeBron James said his decision came down to five teams this offseason and that he envisioned going to the New York Knicks before they won the 2026 title. "I had visions of playing in [Madison Square] Garden and finishing my career in the Garden," James told ESPN on Monday during the 76ers' media day. "One of the best places I've ever played. "I think it's the No. 1 arena in the world, as far as for a basketball player. But after they beat San Antonio, I was like, 'Hey, I can't.' I couldn't do it." James and the 76ers will play the Knicks at the Garden on opening night, Oct. 20. No update on Gary Trent Jr. investigation Milwaukee Bucks governor Wes Edens did not provide an update on the league investigation into Gary Trent Jr. 's contract. "I don't have any update," Edens said. "We're working with the league and fully cooperating with them. But I don't have any insight beyond that." The NBA is looking into a potential cap-circumvention violation by the Bucks around Trent's deal this offseason. Cronin: Blazers have "belief" in Ja Morant Portland Trail Blazers ' general manager Joe Cronin addressed why the franchise decided to trade for Ja Morant this offseason during Portland's media day on Monday. "Just straight belief in Ja," Cronin said. "Our view of Ja as still a very high-level player. "I'm sure there will be questions about fit, but we're very focused on talent." Cronin also said veteran guard Jrue Holiday could play some minutes on the wing for Portland this season, while adding that Holiday and veteran guard Damian Lillard will have a positive influence on Morant. Kerr: Rookie Lendeborg going to "play a ton" Golden State Warriors coach Steve Kerr said during Monday's media day that he expects rookie Yaxel Lendeborg to "play a ton" this season. "He's clearly going to play a ton," Kerr said. "He gives us the size and the versatility that we need. "Whether he's a starter or coming off the bench, that will be determined the next couple of weeks." Lendeborg was the No. 11 pick in the 2026 NBA draft and averaged 15.1 points per game at Michigan last season. Embiid: 'Extremely excited' about this year's team Philadelphia 76ers center Joel Embiid said Monday that he feels like the team finally has the right mix of players, after an offseason in which the franchise traded for Jaylen Brown and signed LeBron James to join the young guard tandem of VJ Edgecombe and Tyrese Maxey . "It's hard to win when you get a group of guys together for one year, two years, maybe," he said. "I'm extremely excited about this team because we have the right mix of veteran leadership and younger guys. We might have some ups and downs, but we're gonna get there." Wembanyama addresses last year's Finals loss After leading by double digits in each of the five games in last season's NBA Finals, San Antonio Spurs center Victor Wembanyama said his memories of it will fuel the team this season. "I couldn't imagine a better motivation," he said. Harper addresses role for coming season After offseason chatter about his role, San Antonio Spurs guard Dylan Harper said he'd follow the coaches' lead this season. "Everyone has a competitive edge to them. But the biggest thing for me is whatever I can do, just like last year, to help the team win," he said. "Whatever position the coaches think is best for me to be in, that's the position I'll happily go in." First look at LeBron in a 76ers uniform New Philadelphia 76ers forward LeBron James is taking questions from reporters on Monday. Here's what he had to say when asked about his initial impressions of his team: "Everybody is on the same page," James said. "We are all speaking the same language." LeBron addressed his role too, saying he's open to whatever the team needs from him to win. "Whatever they need me to do," he said. "The luxury of my game is I can do everything. ... Literally, I can do everything" Kawhi: I was a distraction, ready to move forward In his first public appearance with the Toronto Raptors after a controversy-filled summer, Kawhi Leonard addressed the NBA's investigation into him and his business dealings. "I know why some of you guys came. You want to hear about the investigation. But in talking with the NBA and PA, I think the best decision is to move forward and focus on my time being a Toronto Raptor," he said. "I already was a distraction for the past 70 days and wasn't able to meet my teammates or do any of that stuff, minicamp stuff, so, moving forward, I just want to talk about the Toronto Raptors." Haliburton: I am 100% healthy Indiana Pacers guard Tyrese Haliburton said Monday that he is healthy and ready for the season. "I am healthy. I am 100%," he said. "There will be no restrictions. That is not news. There is no source. I am the source. I am ready to go for the year." Porzingis out indefinitely in blow to Warriors Golden State Warriors big man Kristaps Porzingis is out indefinitely to open training camp with a health issue, according to the team. In late July, Porzingis agreed to a two-year, $40 million contract with a player option on the second season to return to the Warriors. Brown: KAT, Hart extension talks won't be a distraction After reports surfaced last week that negotiations between the New York Knicks and center Karl-Anthony Towns had hit a stalemate, coach Mike Brown said Monday neither Towns' situation nor Hart's would linger in the locker room. "We talk about everything [with the team]," Brown said. "We don't want to have any elephants in the room." "I'm not involved in it. They'll figure it out. Control what you can control." And here's what Towns said about a potential extension: "I've made it known I want to play here. Been a fan since I was a kid. I'd like to get it done." Hornets GM: Brandon Miller to be ready for training camp After undergoing offseason surgery on his left shoulder, Hornets wing Brandon Miller should be a full participant in training camp and "ready to roll" for opening night, Hornets general manager Jeff Peterson said Monday. Miller, 23, is entering his fourth NBA season after being the No. 2 pick in the 2023 draft. Duren won't be at Pistons media day, start of camp Detroit Pistons All-Star center Jalen Duren is not attending the team's media day on Monday or the start of training camp as his contract standoff continues, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania on Monday. Duren, a restricted free agent, is declining the team's five-year, $200 million fully guaranteed offer as both sides remain at a stalemate ahead of the Thursday deadline on a one-year, $9.6 million qualifying offer, sources said. Sept. 26 Bulls trade Dillingham to Hornets for Hield, cash The Chicago Bulls and Charlotte Hornets agreed to a trade sending Rob Dillingham to Charlotte for Buddy Hield and cash, the teams announced Saturday. 2026 NBA offseason trade grades Sept. 25 What's next for Curry and the Warriors? Stephen Curry 's two-year, $116 million extension made him the first player in NBA history to amass $600 million in career on-court earnings. The deal has also put the Golden State Warriors in position to have extra spending power next summer. By Curry taking $10 million less than the maximum allowed, the Warriors project to have nearly $38 million in cap space in 2027. Golden State could increase its projection to $55 million if center Kristaps Porzingis is waived in the offseason. Porzingis' $20 million salary for next season is guaranteed for $3 million. For Golden State to have ample room, forwards Draymond Green and Jimmy Butler III would need to sign elsewhere or at a significantly lesser salary. They will be free agents next summer. Both salary projections include the $17 million free agent hold of guard Brandin Podziemski . The 2023 first-round pick is eligible until Oct. 19 to extend his contract. -- Bobby Marks Grading the Curry deal: Why Warriors don't get an A Hornets star Knueppel sidelined by hamstring injury The Charlotte Hornets announced that Kon Knueppel will be out for at least the entire preseason because of a left hamstring injury. James: Maxey, Embiid were factors in joining 76ers LeBron James said his longstanding friendship with All-Star Tyrese Maxey and a desire to help Joel Embiid win his first NBA title played significant roles in his decision to sign a two-year, $8 million contract with the Philadelphia 76ers in July. "[Embiid has] done everything in our league, and the only thing he has not done is win a championship. And I want to try to help him get that first one," James said. "He has a city on his back. He's been 'The Process' for 10 years, 12 years, however long he's been there. But I think it's time we even get you deeper into the process. And I hope that I can be, kind of, that final little piece that can help him get over the hump." Grizzlies waive Russell The Memphis Grizzlies have waived D'Angelo Russell , sources told ESPN's Shams Charania. Russell has made one All-Star team during his career and was selected No. 2 in the 2015 NBA draft.

stories.title: Payton Pritchard: Lands contract extension Tuesday
stories.summary: Pritchard signed a two-year, $44.2 million contract extension with the Celtics on Tuesday, Shams Charania of ESPN reports. Visit RotoWire.com for more analysis on this update.

stories.title: Celtics reportedly sign G Payton Pritchard to 2-year, $44.2 million extension, with a mutual option
stories.summary: Pritchard was in the second year of his 4-year rookie extension signed ahead of the 2024-2025 season.
stories.detailText: The Boston Celtics are reportedly signing guard Payton Pritchard to a two-year, $44.2 million extension, according to ESPN's Shams Charania . The deal also includes a mutual option for the 2029-2030 season, and it is fully guaranteed. The Celtics selected Pritchard with the 26th overall pick in the 2020 NBA Draft. He helped them win the 2024 NBA championship and was named the NBA's Sixth Man of the Year in 2025. Join or create a Yahoo Fantasy Basketball league for the 2026-27 NBA season The Boston guard has been used off the bench throughout his career, but he started 50 games last year, a significant increase from three the year before. Pritchard averaged a career-high 17 points per game last year. He also averaged 3.9 rebounds, 5.2 assists and 32.4 minutes per game. Pritchard is once again projected to come off the bench this season. Derrick White is expected to start at point guard, with Baylor Scheierman at shooting guard. The Celtics will likely rely more on Pritchard off the bench this season, because former guard Jaylen Brown now plays for the Philadelphia 76ers. Despite being a first-round pick, the guard has carved out a role as a depth player. He tended to fly under the radar, but had his first breakout game on April 9, 2023, against the Atlanta Hawks. Pritchard finished with 30 points and hit nine 3-pointers. He added 14 rebounds and 11 assists for his first triple-double. The guard's best scoring output came on March 5, 2025, when he drilled 10 3-pointers and finished with 43 points. Pritchard also grabbed 10 rebounds. He has 16 games in which he has made at least five 3-pointers. Pritchard is shooting 39.4% from beyond the arc in his career. Last year, he averaged 7.1 3-point attempts per game, the 18th most in the league. The Boston guard's 37.7% 3-point percentage ranked 11th-highest among players who attempted that many shots from beyond the arc. Pritchard and the Celtics will open the 2026-2027 NBA season on Oct. 20 on the road against the Detroit Pistons.

stories.title: Which NBA deals will get done? Bobby Marks' biggest extension decisions to watch
stories.summary: With Monday's extension deadline looming, Bobby Marks breaks down the biggest decisions around the league.
stories.detailText: The NBA season starts in one week, but that isn't the only thing on the minds of league executives. The deadline for rookie extensions is Monday, a day before the 2026-27 regular season tips off. Since the start of the offseason, five players -- Victor Wembanyama , Amen and Ausar Thompson , Keyonte George and Brandin Podziemski -- have signed rookie extensions. That's currently far below the average of 11 rookie extensions signed per year since 2023, but expect that number to rise in the coming days. Of the 34 players to land rookie extensions in the past three seasons, 17 signed on deadline day. What deals will the next week bring? We broke down what to expect for six of the 16 eligible players. Rookie extension decisions aren't the only things we're watching. Oct. 19 is also the deadline to extend veterans with two years remaining on their contract -- not including an option year -- and the deadline to reduce rosters to 15 players on standard contracts. Let's examine the league's most important extension decisions and what Monday's deadline could bring for teams around the league. Jump to a section: Six big rookie extension decisions KAT, Giannis among vets to watch Moves coming for Lakers, Knicks? Rookie extension candidates to watch Brandon Miller , Charlotte Hornets Why an extension could get done: Following offseason trades of LaMelo Ball and Miles Bridges , the Hornets view Miller and Kon Knueppel as the franchise's new foundation. An injury-plagued sophomore 2024-25 season limited Miller to 27 games, but he rebounded last season to post career highs in 3-pointers made, 3-point percentage and free throw attempts and averaged more than 20 points per game for the second straight season. Why it might not: Miller views Amen Thompson's five-year, $208 million extension with Houston as a comparable salary. The main difference: Thompson played at least 60 games in each of his first three seasons and was selected for the All-Defensive First Team in 2025. What I would offer: Five years, $175 million. The contract can either start at $30.2 million and increase each year, ending at $39.8 million, or start high and decline each season. ( Coby White 's latest contract with the Hornets declines in Years 2 and 3.) With no player earning more than $25 million in 2027-28, Charlotte has the flexibility to increase Miller's offer. Not including new contracts for Miller and center Moussa Diabate , who is eligible for an extension in February, Charlotte projects to be $80 million under the luxury tax next season. Dereck Lively II , Dallas Mavericks Why an extension could get done: The Mavericks would need to bypass injury concerns and look at his impact when healthy. Despite playing only 36 games in 2024-25, Lively ranked 17th out of 138 players in offensive rebounding percentage and fourth in defensive rebounding percentage. During that season, Lively held opponents to 56.3% of shooting at the rim, ranking 20th out of 165 players. In 21 postseason games as a rookie, Lively averaged 7.4 rebounds in 22 minutes per game. Why it might not: What else? Injuries and durability. Lively has played a total of 98 games in his first three seasons, including 55 his rookie year, and missed all but seven games last season. He had right foot surgery in July 2025 before another surgery on the same foot four months later. Lively continues to ramp up his recovery but was not cleared to play 5-on-5 during training camp. What I would offer: Three years, $35 million. The first-year, $10.8 million salary is comparable to the one-year qualifying offer Lively is eligible for next summer if an extension is not reached. The second year is guaranteed, but the third is contingent on Lively playing at least 41 games in the first or second season of the contract. Jaime Jaquez Jr ., Milwaukee Bucks Why an extension could get done: If we are evaluating Jaquez off last season with Miami, then discussions for a new contract are warranted. With the Heat, Jaquez became one of four players to average at least 15 points, five rebounds and four assists off the bench since the 1982-83 season. The forward shot a career-high 50.7% last season and saw his assists nearly double from 2.5 to 4.7. Considering Kyle Kuzma is on an expiring contract and Nate Ament is in his rookie season, having Jaquez under contract should be a priority. Why it might not: Other than failing to reach a compromise, Milwaukee could pause extension talks to evaluate how Jaquez fits in with new Bucks coach Taylor Jenkins. What I would offer: Four years, $78.8 million. Comparable to Jaquez's free agent hold, the contract starts at $17.8 million and ends with a player option. Cason Wallace , Oklahoma City Thunder Why an extension could get done: If there ever was an indication, it was the trade sending Lu Dort to Atlanta. "I would just say Cason is someone we think very highly of and has done a great job for us," Thunder general manager Sam Presti said before training camp. "I think the greatest sign of respect we could have shown Cason is moving Lu [Dort] in that trade. We potentially could have looked at a series of other options, but it's a bit of a gesture to him to say, 'We think you can have a great role on this team. We believe in you as a player.'" Named All-Defense for the first time in his career, Wallace led all players in steals last season. He finished seventh in Defensive Player of the Year voting and was one of five guards (Dyson Daniels, Derrick White, Andrew Nembhard, Amen Thompson) over the past two seasons to win Defensive Player of the Month. Why it might not: Second apron concerns. With Year 1 of Shai Gilgeous-Alexander's supermax extension beginning, Oklahoma City is $1.9 million over the second apron. A contract for Wallace starting at $25 million not only puts the Thunder deeper into the apron but will cost them an additional $150 million in luxury taxes. As this past offseason proved with the trades of Dort, Aaron Wiggins and Isaiah Joe , Oklahoma City is not afraid to make difficult choices to keep its core intact. What I would offer: Five years, $145 million. The contract starts at $25 million and increases to $33 million in the final year. You can make a case that Wallace should get more in guaranteed money than Keyonte George and Ausar Thompson, but Oklahoma City is in a different bracket financially than Utah and Detroit. Anthony Black , Orlando Magic Why an extension could get done: Past precedent. The Magic have been aggressive in signing former draft picks to rookie extensions. In the past three offseasons, Orlando has extended Cole Anthony , Jalen Suggs , Franz Wagner and Paolo Banchero . If not for injuring his back in early March, Black would have been a candidate for 2026 Most Improved Player; his scoring increased from 9.4 to 15.3 points per game and he shot a career-high 44.7% from the field. Defensively, Black had 25 games with multiple steals. Why it might not: Finances. A new contract would likely put Orlando over the luxury tax for consecutive seasons and over the first apron. The Magic are a projected $20 million under the tax threshold. Next season and in 2028-29, they will have four players (Wagner, Banchero, Desmond Bane , Jalen Suggs ) earning more than $26 million. Considering Orlando has failed to advance past the first round with this roster, is it prudent to pay a significant penalty once again? What I would offer: There are two ways to look at Black's next contract: the deal Orlando should offer because of its financial constraints, and what Black deserves. If the goal is to remain below the luxury tax, the starting salary cannot exceed $13 million -- below the $16 million non-tax midlevel exception for next season. There is also the question of whether Orlando views him as a starter or a sixth man. The starting backcourt of Suggs and Bane is under contract through at least the 2028-29 season. Scoot Henderson , Portland Trail Blazers Why an extension could get done: The Trail Blazers view Henderson's production in the first round of the playoffs as a reason to lock up the former No. 3 pick to a long-term contract. In the first three games against the Spurs, Henderson scored 70 points. Over the past 30 seasons, only Brandon Roy (82 points in 2009) and Damian Lillard (79 points in 2014) scored more through their first three playoﬀ games as a Blazer. Why it might not: Other than a small sample in the playoffs, what has Henderson done in his first three seasons to show he is worthy of a lucrative contract? Henderson's career field goal percentage (40.4%) is the second worst of any player in the past three seasons. And on defense, Henderson allowed 51.4% shooting from the field as the closest defender last season. Also, how does Henderson fit with new coach Micah Nori and a crowded backcourt of Lillard, Jrue Holiday and Ja Morant ? What I would offer: Three years, $51.8 million. The first-year salary of $16 million is comparable to the non-tax midlevel exception. Other players eligible for rookie extensions: Noah Clowney (Brooklyn), Julian Strawther (Denver), Marcus Sasser (Dallas), Ben Sheppard (Indiana), Jarace Walker (Indiana), Gradey Dick ( LA Clippers ), Taylor Hendricks (Memphis), Kris Murray (Memphis), Brice Sensabaugh (Utah), Bilal Coulibaly (Washington) Veteran extension candidates Recent extensions for Kawhi Leonard and Stephen Curry have continued the trend of stars choosing guaranteed money over hitting free agency. Since the offseason started in July, 11 potential free agents extended their contracts, including Leonard, Curry and Donovan Mitchell . There are two sets of deadlines for players who are extension-eligible. For players with two years or more remaining on their contract, such as the Celtics' Payton Pritchard, Monday is the deadline to extend. Players with one year remaining on their contract have until June 30 to extend. If a player has two years left on his contract but with an option in the last season, however, he is also eligible to extend up to June 30. This group includes Nikola Jokic , Karl-Anthony Towns , Giannis Antetokounmpo and Anthony Davis . For each of the four players to extend after Oct. 19, the player option must be eliminated and replaced with the first year of the extension. Here are where things stand ahead of that Oct. 19 deadline: Nikola Jokic , Denver Nuggets For the second consecutive offseason, Jokic will not sign an extension in Denver. The lack of long-term security has nothing to do with his unhappiness in Denver, but rather his ability to maximize finances next offseason. By waiting until the 2027 offseason, Jokic is eligible to sign a five-year, $359.5 million contract as a free agent. That contract would be the largest in NBA history and see his career on-court earnings reach $724 million. Karl-Anthony Towns , New York Knicks Towns has repeatedly said the goal is to get a new contract done with New York. "Simply put, I want to do something that can keep the team together and work with the Knicks and also values me," Towns said on Oct. 5 . The Knicks are thinking differently, stating they will not negotiate any extensions until later in the season. Since the NBA Finals concluded in mid-June, Towns has been eligible to sign up to a four-year, $276 million extension. Talks have reached an impasse, per Towns, however. "None of those things have come close to happening," he said. The holdup on why New York is not writing a blank check comes down to second apron concerns over the foreseeable future. With Towns' $61 million player option in 2027-28, New York is likely to exceed the second apron. They are currently $9 million below the threshold and have five open roster spots. The purse strings get even tighter in the summer of 2028. Not including new contracts for Towns and Josh Hart and a significant raise for Jalen Brunson (his salary will likely increase from $43.3 to $64.7 million), New York will project to be $104 million below the second apron. For example, if New York signed Towns to a four-year, $227 million extension ($53 million, $57.4 million, $61.5 million and $65.7 million), extended Hart starting at $20 million and signed Brunson to a max contract, it guarantees New York as a second apron team for the 2028-29 season. Knicks owner James Dolan said after the Finals that New York will not exceed the second apron . Giannis Antetokounmpo , Miami Heat Antetokounmpo has been extension-eligible since Oct. 1 but at considerably less money because he was traded on July 6. The extension would be either three years, $194 million or two years, $135.1 million. But waiting until Jan. 6 (six months after the trade) would make Antetokounmpo eligible to sign a four-year, $276 million extension. The $62.8 million player option would be replaced with Year 1 of the extension. One scenario not to be overlooked: Antetokounmpo mirroring Jokic and re-signing with Miami as a free agent in the 2027 offseason. By not extending in January, Antetokounmpo would then become eligible for a five-year, $357 million contract. His potential $754 million in career on court earnings would be the most in NBA history. Anthony Davis , Washington Wizards Do not expect a Davis extension in the near future. "[I'll decide] when the season is over," Davis said on media day. "We're going to go through the season and try to do what I do at a high level. ... And then when it's over, sit down and have those conversations again with the front office." Davis became eligible to sign an extension in early August for up to four years and $275 million. He holds a player option for $62 million next season, the final year of a three-year, $175 million deal he signed with the Lakers. The first year of an extension would replace that player option. Davis, 33, did not play with Washington after he was acquired at last season's trade deadline, and he has failed to reach 60 games in five of the past six seasons. Jaden McDaniels , Minnesota Timberwolves McDaniels is eligible to extend for two years and $87 million. (Because he has three years remaining on his current contract, the first year of the extension would not start until 2029-30.) Last season, McDaniels increased his scoring from 14.8 points per game in the regular season to 16.5 in the playoffs and scored a season-high 32 points in the Game 6 clincher against Denver. In that series, McDaniels also held All-Star Jamal Murray to 32% shooting as the closest defender. More players to watch Oct. 19 deadline: Onyeka Okongwu (Atlanta), Terance Mann (Brooklyn), Royce O'Neale (Charlotte), Nicolas Claxton (Chicago), Moses Moody (Golden State), Pascal Siakam (Indiana), Obi Toppin (Indiana), Andrew Nembhard (Indiana), Tyrese Haliburton (Indiana), Ivica Zubac (Indiana), Darius Garland (LA Clippers), Anthony Edwards (Minnesota), LaMelo Ball (Minnesota), Jaden McDaniels (Minnesota), Karlo Matkovic (New Orleans), Zion Williamson (New Orleans), Desmond Bane (Orlando), Jaylen Brown (Philadelphia), Deni Avdija (Portland), Ja Morant (Portland), Domantas Sabonis (Sacramento), Devin Vassell (San Antonio). June 30 deadline: Lu Dort (Atlanta), Mouhamed Gueye (Atlanta), Paul George (Boston), Michael Porter Jr . (Brooklyn), Grant Williams (Charlotte), Leonard Miller (Chicago), Jalen Smith (Chicago), Isaac Okoro (Chicago), Buddy Hield (Chicago), Craig Porter Jr . (Cleveland), Max Christie (Dallas), Caleb Martin (Dallas), Cameron Johnson (Denver), Zeke Nnaji (Denver), Johnny Furphy (Indiana), Jay Huff (Indiana), Kris Dunn (LA Clippers), Derrick Jones Jr . (LA Clippers), Cam Christie (LA Clippers), Max Strus (LA Clippers), Jarred Vanderbilt (LA Lakers), Bronny James (LA Lakers), Jaden Hardy (LA Lakers), Isaiah Stewart (Memphis), Jaylen Wells (Memphis), Scotty Pippen Jr . (Memphis), Jerami Grant (Memphis), Giannis Antetokounmpo (Miami), Kyle Kuzma (Milwaukee), Tyler Herro (Milwaukee), Donte DiVincenzo (Minnesota), Rudy Gobert (Minnesota), Jordan Poole (New Orleans), Dejounte Murray (New Orleans), Josh Hart (New York), Tyler Kolek (New York), Miles McBride (New York), Goga Bitadze (Orlando), Adem Bona (Philadelphia), Jalen Green (Phoenix), Oso Ighodaro (Phoenix), Miles Bridges (Phoenix), Vit Krejci (Portland), Zach LaVine (Sacramento), De'Andre Hunter (Sacramento), Malik Monk (Sacramento), Keldon Johnson (San Antonio), Kyle Filopowski (Utah), Svi Mykhailiuk (Utah). Key roster decisions around the league Nearly 80 players will hit waivers Saturday night in anticipation of Monday's deadline to cut rosters to 15 players. Teams will incur a per-day cap hit if a player signed to a non-guaranteed contract is not waived by 5 p.m. ET on Saturday. For example, the Knicks would be charged $17,622 per day against the cap if James Wiseman is not waived by Saturday. New York is currently over the luxury tax and first apron. The full salary counts against the apron. Here are three more teams to watch as the Monday roster deadline approaches: Los Angeles Lakers Is there a trade on the horizon to consolidate the Lakers' roster? With 16 players currently on guaranteed contracts, Los Angeles will need to open up a roster spot either in a trade or by releasing a player. "Behind that evaluation of who's emerging in camp, there's also consolidation trades that could still be looked at -- trading two guys out, bringing one in," Lakers president of basketball operations Rob Pelinka said last month. "There's a number of ways that could be addressed." Memphis Grizzlies The Grizzlies have already made two roster decisions by waiving veteran D'Angelo Russell and former first-round pick Jordan Hawkins . Memphis has 16 guaranteed contracts but needs to release two players because the $2.3 million salary of Jaylen Wells is set to become guaranteed on Oct. 19. Possible candidates include Kris Murray and Micah Peavy . New York Knicks New York loaded up on depth this summer by signing veterans Bruce Brown , Ochai Agbaji , Drew Eubanks , James Wiseman and Tony Bradley . But due to a self-imposed second apron hard cap, the Knicks are likely to keep just one of the five players despite having two open roster spots. They are currently $3.2 million below the second apron. Other options: Keep two players and then cut one during the season, or make a minor trade to clear out salary. Other decisions to watch The Hornets made a series of transactions in the offseason, trading Dorian Finney-Smith , Buddy Hield and waiving Ryan Nembhard . They have 16 players on standard contracts, including the non-guaranteed contract of veteran Pat Connaughton . With Moussa Cisse 's contract becoming guaranteed on Oct. 1, Dallas has 15 players on guaranteed deals. The Mavericks signed center Dwight Powell before training camp and need to waive the veteran or make another move to get their roster to 15 players. The Warriors have a decision with their final two roster spots. They are hard-capped at the second apron and allowed to keep only three of these four players: Brandon Williams , Dalen Terry , Georges Niang and Charles Bassey . Terry, whose contract is not guaranteed, had a team-high 23 points in a preseason loss to the Trail Blazers on Oct. 7. Bassey ($1.4 million) and Niang's ($1.8 million) salaries are partially guaranteed, while Williams' salary increases from no protection to $1.4 million if he is not waived on the first day of the regular season. The Clippers and Cam Christie agreed to move back his guaranteed date twice during the offseason. Now with a Thursday deadline looming, LA can guarantee the former second-round pick and waive a player on a guaranteed deal -- newly acquired Gradey Dick , for example -- or cut bait with Christie. The four-for-one trade that sent Antetokounmpo to Miami has Milwaukee with 16 guaranteed contracts. Pete Nance 's deal becomes guaranteed if he is not waived by Monday.

stories.title: JJ Redick is a big fan of Chris Mañon: ‘We’re invested in his development’
stories.summary: Mañon is on a two-way deal with the Lakers for the second consecutive year
stories.detailText: SACRAMENTO, CA - OCTOBER 5: Chris Manon #30 of the Los Angeles Lakers looks on during the game against the Sacramento Kings during a 2026 NBA Preseason game on October 5, 2026 at Golden 1 Center in Sacramento, California. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images Agreement. Mandatory Copyright Notice: Copyright 2026 NBAE (Photo by Rocky Widner/NBAE via Getty Images) | NBAE via Getty Images During his Summer League debut in 2025, while playing for the Golden State Warriors, Chris Mañon recorded eight points, three rebounds, three steals, two blocks and one assist in 19 minutes against the Los Angeles Lakers. Although Mañon spent the entirety of his 2025 Summer League stint with the Warriors, his play in that opening game caught the eye of the Lakers organization, which ultimately signed him to a two-way contract for 2025-26 and did so again this summer for 2026-27. Mañon has appeared in all three of Los Angeles’ preseason games thus far, headlined by a 12-point, five-rebound, one-block, one-steal performance against the Sacramento Kings on Oct. 5. “I really like Chris. We had him in for a draft workout. I think we maybe had him in for two draft workouts,” Redick told reporters. “Then he was with Golden State during the California Classic and really popped against us. So we started working that pretty much immediately with his agent because he wasn’t on a two-way. So, we’re invested in him and we’re invested in his development, in his career. I thought he played really well against Sacramento. I don’t think any of our guards played well against Golden State.” Mañon only played in nine games with the Lakers last season but logged 46 G League appearances for the South Bay Lakers, where he averaged 11.6 points, 6.0 rebounds, 2.4 assists and 2.1 steals. His defensive playmaking, perhaps the standout trait of his game, has seemingly translated across every context. He posted a 5.6% steal rate in four years collegiately, posted a 3.8% steal rate in the G League last season, picked up five steals in 46 NBA minutes a year ago, and has four steals in 40 preseason minutes this season. Redick has emphasized defensive disruption during training camp and preseason play, an area Mañon could clearly help boost with his knack for occupying the passing lanes. He’s also been a highly effective interior scorer, shooting 60.5% on 2-pointers for his collegiate career and 59.6% (155-of-260) in the G League. It’s doubtful the 24-year-old factors into Los Angeles’ rotation this year but he owns a collection of skills the Lakers are intrigued by, so his development will be worth monitoring wherever he receives the majority of his playing time in 2026-27. You can follow Jackson on Twitter at @jackfrank_jjf .
