stories.title: Welcome to Malu-Watch, where the numbers tell part of the story
stories.summary: A weekly look at rebounds, blocks and steals per 36 minutes offers one way to track Maluach’s defensive development.
stories.detailText: DETROIT, MICHIGAN - OCTOBER 05: John Collins #20 of the Detroit Pistons drives to the basket against Khaman Maluach #10 of the Phoenix Suns in the second half during a pre season game at Little Caesars Arena on October 05, 2026 in Detroit, Michigan. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Gregory Shamus/Getty Images) | Getty Images Plenty of eyes will be on second-year center Khaman Maluach throughout this season as he looks to receive his first real opportunity to play consistent minutes in the NBA following the injury to Mark Williams. You could essentially call last season a redshirt year for Maluach, considering how little he played. Sure, he appeared in 46 games, but he averaged only 8.9 minutes per contest. It’s difficult to draw many meaningful conclusions from a sample size like that, especially when you’re talking about a young player still learning the nuances of the NBA game. Add in the fact that he’s entering his second season following a full summer of what we hope was growth and development, and projecting what to expect from the 20-year-old big man becomes even more challenging. That said, I came across an interesting statistic that could serve as the foundation for a weekly update tracking his progress throughout the season. A “Malu-Watch”, if you will. It’s certainly a flawed metric, but one that could serve as a useful reference point for evaluating his impact on the defensive end. Because at the end of the day, that’s where I’m hoping Maluach makes his greatest contribution. Whoever starts at center for the Phoenix Suns isn’t going to be somebody the team relies upon to score 20 points every night. Perhaps there will be occasional performances where that happens, but with Devin Booker, Jalen Green, Dillon Brooks, and Miles Bridges occupying the other four starting positions, the expectation is that those players will dominate the shot diet. The center position will primarily serve a complementary role offensively. But defensively? That’s where the opportunity truly lies, and it’s where I’m hoping Maluach can establish his value. So what’s the statistic I’m referring to? Rebounds + blocks + steals per 36 minutes. It’s not a perfect representation of defensive impact, and there are certainly limitations to evaluating a player through those three categories alone. But I came across an interesting little nugget that caught my attention. Based on that measurement from last season, Maluach ranked among the top five centers in the NBA. And considering how limited his opportunities were a season ago, that’s an intriguing starting point as we prepare to evaluate what he can become with a more consistent role. Just sayin': https://t.co/tN48nHBx6L pic.twitter.com/mQRZIXku9n — Suns Uniform Tracker (@SunsUniTracker) October 10, 2026 Again, I recognize how flawed this statistic is. Maluach played only 8.9 minutes per game last season, and per 36 numbers are much like single-game plus-minus. They tell part of the story, not the entire story. When you’re extrapolating production across 36 minutes, you’re assuming a player can maintain the same level of effectiveness and energy over that extended period. That’s not necessarily realistic, especially for a young center still developing his conditioning and understanding of the game. But the advantage of using per-36 is that it provides a consistent baseline for comparison. Rather than relying solely on counting stats from game to game, where minutes can fluctuate due to rotations, injuries, and foul trouble, it provides a standardized metric for evaluating a player’s production relative to his time on the floor. And I think that could be an interesting way to monitor Maluach throughout the season, tracking his defensive production as his role evolves and his minutes potentially increase. It won’t tell us everything about his impact, but it could provide another layer of context as we evaluate his development. What does that look like through the first three preseason games? When you look at his performances through the first two preseason games against the Pistons and Bulls, I think the numbers reflect much of what we witnessed. Defensively, Maluach looked out of sorts. From a rebounding perspective, he wasn’t consistently securing the basketball, often tipping rebounds around rather than grabbing them with authority. His positioning seemed off, and he didn’t appear entirely comfortable with what was happening around him. It almost felt like he was thinking too much rather than reacting instinctively. But one thing I’ve noticed about Maluach throughout his young career, whether it’s been in Summer League, the G League, or playing against NBA competition, is his ability to adjust. Whether those adjustments happen within a game or from one game to the next, he’s consistently demonstrated an ability to process what went wrong and execute more effectively following difficult performances. And we saw that in his third preseason appearance. His positioning on the glass was noticeably better, and he attacked rebounds with much more conviction. He looked more comfortable, more decisive, and more confident in where he needed to be defensively. Perhaps my favorite play of the game came when he picked Jordan McLaughlin’s pocket, showcasing the kind of defensive instincts that make his development so intriguing. View Link Last season, Maluach’s per-36-minute numbers in rebounds + blocks + steals came in at 15.0. Thus far this preseason, considering he’s played 21.8 minutes with 8.0 rebounds, 0.7 blocks, and 0.3 steals, he finds himself at 14.9. Initial analysis says the trend he set last season, albeit in a very limited role, is continuing. As the season progresses, feel free to check in with Bright Side each week as we track Maluach’s development, how his defensive impact manifests itself statistically, and whether those numbers align with what we’re seeing on the court.

stories.title: Jake LaRavia’s improved mindset, reworked jumper is paying big dividends early this preseason
stories.summary: LaRavia spent the summer reflecting on last season’s struggles and is off to a strong start this preseason
stories.detailText: LOS ANGELES, CALIFORNIA - OCTOBER 08: Jake LaRavia #12 of the Los Angeles Lakers reacts against the Sacramento Kings in a preseason game at Crypto.com Arena on October 08, 2026 in Los Angeles, California. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, user is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Luke Hales/Getty Images) | Getty Images Through three preseason outings , Jake LaRavia is shooting 6-of-11 (54.6%) beyond the arc. While an 11-shot sample is far too small to project any future success, LaRavia’s willingness to shoot is encouraging. Per 36 minutes, he’s attempting 5.9 3-pointers, an uptick from last preseason’s 3.8 and a jump from last regular season’s 4.2. In the playoffs, as his playing time dwindled and jumper cratered, he averaged just 2.2 3-point attempts per 36 minutes. LaRavia’s head coach, JJ Redick, notices him operating with a level of belief necessary to be a good shooter. “I think Jake had a like a really nice base and foundation to shoot with. So it wasn’t like he was completely revamping his shot on those small tweaks. Ultimately, the tweaks don’t matter if they don’t give you confidence,” Redick told reporters after Thursday’s game against the Sacramento Kings. “I feel like he’s shooting the ball with a lot of confidence right now and he feels confident in the shot. [He had] a great summer shooting the ball, has had a great training camp of practices shooting the ball and that’s carried over to games.” LaRavia’s playing time dipped last postseason for numerous reasons, largely because his outside shot abandoned him and derailed much of his decision-making offensively. After shooting 35.3% from deep through Jan. 15, he made just 27.9% of his 3s over the final 43 regular-season games before netting just 2-of-7 triples (28.6%) in the playoffs. “I think the response has been great. Obviously, he’s played really good so far. He was big for what we wanted to do last year,” Austin Reaves told reporters postgame on Thursday. “I think he has spoken about it, not shooting the ball the way he knows he can and wants to. But he told me, I think it was one of the last games of the regular season, we were just [having a] casual conversation and he just told me he was like, I’m going to get the in the gym. I’m going to be one of the best shooters on this team.” Before struggling over the second half of the season, LaRavia was a key cog in the Lakers’ rotation behind his defense, viable floor-spacing, quick decision-making and offensive rebounding. An extended cold spell from deep interfered with many of those traits. This season, following a summer of reflection , he’s altered his mindset to be less worried about whether each specific hot goes in and is instead harping on the controllable aspects to be the best version of himself. “I think the one thing that kind of changed for me this year was focusing more on the input rather than the output,” LaRavia said. “So not really focused on my makes or my misses, but am I doing everything in my control to give myself the best opportunity to make the shot. So as far as the output goes, I’m not really concerned about how many shots I’m making right now because at some point, I’m going to also miss shots. But as long as the input stays the same, then I’ll be consistent.” You can follow Jackson on Twitter at @jackfrank_jjf .

stories.title: Tyrese Haliburton's return brings hope and expectations in Indiana
stories.summary: Nearly 16 months ago, a torn Achilles cost Tyrese Haliburton -- and the Pacers -- the 2025-26 season. Now, he returns to help them reclaim their spot in the East.
stories.detailText: THE SWEAT FROM Tyrese Haliburton 's Indiana Pacers jersey almost immediately began to seep into his blue warmup shirt. For 16 months, the two-time All-Star guard had been patiently -- and then not so patiently -- and then practically champing at the bit to leave his seat on the sideline and play minutes in an NBA game. On Oct. 7, he finally did. The Pacers were playing in Ames, Iowa, at Iowa State University, Haliburton's alma mater, where it was a two-part homecoming. It was his first game at his college arena in six years. Students began lining up the night before the game to get into the student section and grab a yellow shirt with Haliburton's face on it over the moniker "Cyclone Hali." And it was also Haliburton's first seven minutes in a game since tearing his right Achilles during Game 7 of the 2025 NBA Finals. With 4:27 remaining in the first quarter of the Pacers' preseason opener against the Minnesota Timberwolves on Oct. 7, Haliburton relished a different moment: his first break. "I was tired as hell," Haliburton said with a laugh after the game. "But even through that, I just kept feeling like, 'Man, I'm playing again .'" On Indiana's first possession of the game, an antsy Haliburton fired a no-look pass, intended for Andrew Nembhard , out of bounds. But with that out of the way, on the next possession, Haliburton ran a 2-on-1 with Pascal Siakam that Haliburton finished with a crossover into a 15-foot jumper for his first basket in more than a year. The adrenaline of the night carried him through 16 minutes of action . Haliburton finished with seven points and six assists in the Pacers' 123-112 win. "I have my own internal expectations," Haliburton told ESPN. "But our goal is to win a championship. That has never wavered." The Pacers' season -- and Indiana's road back to contention -- depends on those expectations . The last time Haliburton was healthy, he electrified the NBA with one of the greatest clutch postseason runs in NBA history, with a game-tying or winning shot in each of the four rounds of the 2025 playoffs. Indiana led in the first quarter of Game 7 in Oklahoma City before Haliburton tore his Achilles , and the Thunder marched their way to the record books. While Haliburton spent the 2025-26 season recovering, the Pacers won 19 games. It makes Indiana one of the most perplexing teams coming into the 2026-27 NBA season. Despite making the conference finals in 2024 and the conference finals in 2025, the Pacers are projected to win a modest 42 games and ranked 10th in the Eastern Conference, according to ESPN's Basketball Power Index . "I don't look too much into it," Haliburton told ESPN. "Our whole team can relate to that. We've all felt that way one way or another." The Pacers are the last team to beat the champion New York Knicks in a playoff series. But in a more competitive East than the last one he left, Haliburton is out to prove that the Pacers can reclaim their spot at the top. "Finding that magic again, that's no guarantee," Pacers general manager Chad Buchanan told ESPN. "But our core guys believe in each other. They feel like people have written them off already. That's what's happened those two years we made runs -- people just kind of discarded us. That's what fuels them." THE ZERO IN the middle of the jersey was orange, matching the trim on a jersey that had been shaded with blue in the middle. As Haliburton picked up the sheet of paper, he scoffed. "Who drew this one?" he asked. "Orange and blue on a Pacers jersey?" "Knicks colors," his wife, Jade, said with a knowing smile. With training camp still a few weeks away, the Haliburtons visited children at the Peyton Manning Children's Hospital in Indianapolis. Haliburton was there as a spokesperson for the Indiana Donor Network to raise awareness for organ donation. The five kids in attendance are recipients of kidney transplants. Sitting around a table, Haliburton and the children, some as young as 6, gathered sheets of paper to color. A raucous debate immediately ensued. "What's your favorite color?" Haliburton asked his tablemates, launching an animated discussion. "Red!" one kid said. "Blue!" said another. "Yellow!" "Rainbow!" another said, inciting another debate as to whether all the colors can be considered one color. He insisted it could. "But is there a rainbow marker ?" Haliburton prods, presenting the question as a color-form of checkmate. When Haliburton suggests his favorite color is grey, the kids recoil. "You never hear that , huh?" he says with a smile. Haliburton spent much of the past year in Indianapolis launching himself into projects such as these. He helped the Pacers revitalize their charity softball game earlier this summer, featuring players from the Indianapolis Colts and Indiana Fever. Fans packed Victory Field, a 12,000-seat Triple-A baseball stadium in downtown Indianapolis. Haliburton's connection to the Midwest is deep. He was born in Wisconsin and met and eventually proposed to his wife in Ames. His bond to the region has only deepened since he was traded to Indiana in 2022. It's why he has poured so much into the community. "It's a different perspective on life now," Haliburton told ESPN. "I'm just thankful to be playing basketball again and to be doing all the different things that I can do in the community because when something like that happens, it's like your life flashes before your eyes." During his first vacation a few months after surgery, he could barely walk down the stairs at a house they had rented and needed assistance getting around when they left. His surgeon had warned him, but the reality had set in. He wept in the shower. "Just having to come to terms with going from being on top of the world to the complete opposite of that in an instance," Haliburton told ESPN. "It's such a crazy thing to say because it's a basketball injury that no matter what ... there's a time put on it. You know you're going to be good in that amount of time. We have the best doctors in the world, the best therapists, all those things. You know you're going to be good, but it's a scary thing." He spent most of his recovery in Indianapolis, finding a spot on the bench for game nights, home and road, even as the season went south. But in the middle of his rehab, he dealt with a bad case of the shingles , too, gaining 30 pounds and suffering from severe face swelling as a side effect of the heavy medication. The illness, which is highly contagious, kept him away from his teammates on the sidelines. It was another blow in a long season. "In the league, especially when a star player like that is injured, what that means for the next year, sometimes they're on their own little schedule, 'Hey, I just got to do what's right for me,'" Buchanan said. "That's not how Ty's wired. Ty is wired to know what does the team need from me, rather than what I need to do for the team." During his lonely, arduous recovery, he would occasionally fire up some of his old highlights. "Just to feel something," he said. "I once could do that. I miss that feeling." At one point, he even rewatched the 2025 Finals, he said. His focus remained on Game 4. The Pacers were leading 2-1, but the Thunder rallied from down double-digits in the second half as Shai Gilgeous-Alexander scored 15 of his 35 points in the final 4:38 of the game. "Game 4 will forever live in my brain," Haliburton said. "You win that game, the whole series changes." The thought sat with him as he watched his team go through its worst season in franchise history, realizing so much of the conversation around the Pacers' struggles centered on him, his injury, his recovery and his eventual return. "Everybody always feels the summer is really long," Haliburton said. "Well, I've had that for double, triple the amount of time everybody else." HALIBURTON DOESN'T WANT the Pacers to forget last season. Indiana finished with its fewest wins in franchise history. The team was decimated by injuries early, and started to position itself for a better draft pick by the second half. By the end of the season, the team looked like a shell of the one that went to the Finals. "You can take [our preseason rankings] as disrespect, but at the same time, you got to understand we put ourselves in that position by the way we played last year," Haliburton said. "There's standards that we didn't meet that we got to get back to. And there's no secret that there was a drop-off last year." Training camp has been focused on rebuilding those habits. The night before the first day of practice, the team gathered at Buchanan's house on the floor at his indoor basketball court. It has become an annual tradition for the past four years, a moment when the Pacers can iron out their priorities heading into the season. Coach Rick Carlisle lamented how long the summer had been. It had been 5½ months since their last game in April, and even longer since their last game with anything on the line. "Reclaim" ended up being the key word during the meeting. Carlisle acknowledged how important it was to have Haliburton back, but cautioned against looking at Haliburton as a savior. "We're a team that's very reliant on one another," Carlisle said before the game in Ames last week. "One of the things that when we had a really, really good two-year run, it made us a special team, our connectivity, our ecosystem, dependence on one another. "We're always going to be better as the sum of all the parts." Most of the Pacers' core is the same -- Haliburton, Siakam, Nembhard and Aaron Nesmith -- but Ivica Zubac was brought in to replace the departed Myles Turner in a trade deadline deal that ended up costing Indiana the No. 5 pick in the draft . Team sources say the Pacers are confident that the deal will help reopen their championship window. They also acknowledge Zubac, who plays closer to the basket, will provide different strengths than Turner, a center who stretches the floor from 3-point range. "We have a great coach who figures things out," Buchanan told ESPN. "That's a strength of his. If things aren't going well, and we aren't playing well -- or [Zubac's] not fitting well, he adapts." The fit with Zubac could take time. His individual fit with Haliburton could, too. They've struggled with their timing in pick-and-rolls early in the preseason, with Haliburton often rounding the corner before his new center has an opportunity to roll. "He's so anxious to prove to people. He hates that people say he'll have to be patient. He hates that," Buchanan told ESPN. "He's like, 'I've been out 16 effing months. I'm ready to play.' He's obviously very confident, but I still think there's going to be a ramp-up for him as just getting his feet, groove and rhythm back." HALIBURTON MOVED LIKE his former self at times, but the growing pains were evident in his first game back. He compared himself to a rookie, playing too fast and needing to slow down to let the offense find its rhythm. He tweaked his right ankle during the game, and sat out the next preseason game, but an MRI confirmed his Achilles was unaffected. "I was hyped to be out there, excited, but I just got to slow down a little bit," he said. "There's a ton of improvement to be made on my end and on our team's end. But I'm just excited to be back on the floor." Multiple moments in the gym this summer gave him reason for the confidence. One afternoon in late July, 13 months after his surgery, he took one dribble and tossed the ball into the air toward the basket. As he raced after it, the ball bounced just short of the basket inside the Pacers' practice facility, its upward trajectory almost carrying him higher toward the rim than he has been in years. Midair, he crossed the ball between his legs, and rose toward the hoop, dunking the ball with his right hand as various members of the Pacers' staff let out a collective scream. But it was Haliburton who screamed the loudest, releasing more than a year of pent-up angst. He had a running bet with Justin Tallard, one of Indiana's physical therapists, that if he completed the dunk, named an Eastbay, Haliburton could skip his post-practice workout. It's a dunk Haliburton hadn't regularly made since he was a 20-year-old rookie. Later, Haliburton posted a video of the dunk to his social media accounts, and the message to the rest of the league was obvious. I'm back . The dunk signified Haliburton's flashy arrival, but it was a quieter moment a month later that sent an even louder signal. Before the start of the season, Pacers players held a minicamp in Los Angeles. At one point during a scrimmage, Haliburton fell to the floor. A few months before, everyone in the gym would have gone hush, waiting for him to get back to his feet, similar to what happened that night in Oklahoma City. But this time, nothing happened. He got up. The game continued. "That," he said, "makes me feel normal again."

stories.title: NBA unveils NBA Cup courts: Bold colors are back, fans will know it's a Cup game
stories.summary: The NBA wants its NBA Cup games to have a distinctive look. These courts accomplish that.
stories.detailText: When fans tune in to an NBA Cup tournament game, the league wants them to instantly recognize something is different — this isn't just another regular-season NBA game. One key way to do that: Distinctive, vibrant NBA Cup courts, and they are back this season. ALL 30 TEAM COURTS FOR @EMIRATES NBA CUP 2026 pic.twitter.com/RgBqe1VJCB — NBA (@NBA) October 13, 2026 These courts will be used for the group play, quarterfinals and semifinals of the NBA Cup (in a change this year, the semifinal games will be played on the higher-seeded team's home court, with the two teams in the Cup Finals traveling to the iconic Hinkle Fieldhouse in Indianapolis, home of the Butler Bulldogs, for that game). This year's court design is inspired by Nike’s “End of Ordinary” NBA Standard Issue Collection , with the collection's designs extending onto the court. At center court is the team's logo as well as the NBA Cup trophy, and there are oversized "woodmarks" featuring the team's name in the style of the Nike Standard Collection jackets. Teams also will wear their statement edition uniforms for all NBA Cup games, to help those games stand out. NBA Cup games will start on Oct. 30 and run on selected NBA Cup nights through Nov. 27. The 30 NBA teams have been drawn into three five-team groups within their conference, and each team will play at least four NBA Cup games against the others in its group. The winner of each group — with point differential as the tiebreaker — and one wild card team from each conference will enter an eight-team tournament (four East teams, four West) and play a single-elimination tournament to reach the NBA Cup Finals. Last season, the New York Knicks beat the San Antonio Spurs in the NBA Cup Finals, previewing what would happen in the NBA Finals in June. Whether we get another NBA Finals preview in the Cup remains to be seen, but we fans will know when the NBA Cup games hit, with these courts it will be hard to miss.

stories.title: 4-star SG Devin Cleveland down to 3 schools, sets commitment date
stories.summary: Four-star Devin Cleveland is down to three schools: Michigan, Missouri, and TCU. He’ll announce his college commitment on October 16th.
stories.detailText: Four-star shooting guard Devin Cleveland has narrowed his list of schools under consideration to three, a source told Rivals. Moving forward, the 6-foot-3 rising senior out of La Lumiere School (IN) will consider Michigan , Missouri , and TCU . Cleveland will announce his college commitment on Friday, Oct. 16, and has visited each of his three finalists. [ $19.99 gets you a FULL year of On3 | Rivals national coverage ] Cleveland, a Chicago native, is ranked as the No. 32 overall recruit in the 2027 class and the No. 5 ranked shooting guard, according to the Rivals Industry Rankings , an average of all three major recruiting media companies (Rivals, ESPN, 247Sports). In late July, Cleveland announced a top seven that also included Alabama, Arkansas, Marquette, and Syracuse. More on Devin Cleveland Playing on the EYBL Circuit this summer, Cleveland averaged 16.6 points, 2.9 rebounds, and 2.5 assists per game for Brad Beal Elite. “I feel like I’m a winner,” Cleveland previously told Rivals in an interview. “That’s what I’ve been trying to prove this EYBL season. You know, the past couple of years, I haven’t really had much success in winning games, so just coming over here with Bradley Beal, their identity is to win. So, I’m just trying to be a leader. I can score the basketball, and I’m a willing passer. I try to get my teammates involved every game. “I watch a lot of Devin Booker, Jeremiah Fears, my brother Fred Cleveland, who is a pro overseason. Watching how they score the ball, create contact on the offensive end so I can draw fouls and little things like that.” Cleveland also discussed what he’s looking for in a program. “I’m going to be looking a lot at the fit. I want to play for a coach who believes in me and believes in my game, and that it will fit in with their system. Really, I just want to win. That’s all I want to do at the end of the day.”

stories.title: Kyshawn George shows added muscle in 21-point showing vs. Nets
stories.summary: WASHINGTON — Kyshawn George added eight pounds on lean muscle this offseason to become a more versatile defender. What he didn’t expect was how much it would help his offensive game as well. Namely, bodying his way into the paint for easy layups or kick-outs to open teammates. The 22-year-old wing tallied used that mu…
stories.detailText: WASHINGTON, DC - OCTOBER 12: Kyshawn George #18 of the Washington Wizards drives to the basket during the game against the Brooklyn Nets on October 12, 2026 at Capital One Arena in Washington, DC. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this Photograph, user is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. Mandatory Copyright Notice: Copyright 2026 NBAE (Photo by Stephen Gosling/NBAE via Getty Images) | NBAE via Getty Images WASHINGTON — Kyshawn George added eight pounds on lean muscle this offseason to become a more versatile defender. What he didn’t expect was how much it would help his offensive game as well. Namely, bodying his way into the paint for easy layups or kick-outs to open teammates. The 22-year-old wing tallied used that muscle to tally 21 points and four assists in the Wizards’ 131-122 loss to the Brooklyn Nets on Monday. It’s a sign of things to come for George, who’s entering a possible breakout campaign in Year 3. “Just more durability, being more confident in my body, what I could do out there,” George said of his added muscle. “I think I always had the skill set, just having the strength and the athleticism to just put it on display on an hourly basis. So having that work being done over the offseason gave me more confidence to go do it in the game.” George opened the game with a patient step-through move into a mid-range jumper and later skied in for a put-back layup. Isolated on the wing, George drove left and used his added strength to fend off Michael Porter Jr. with his off-arm before drawing contact and making the ensuing free throws. That ability to muscle inside and draw contact is one of the many perks of added weight, especially against NBA competition. “My first intention was to be able to add on weight to guard multiple positions, keep that same ability, but guard you know bigger players. And offensively, it’s the same thing,” George said. “I’d be able to get in the paint, draw contact, and then find the open man.” Then came George’s playmaking — an area the Wizards want him to expand this season. The 6-foot-9 wing received a pass from Alex Sarr before throwing a transition lob to AJ Dybantsa that ignited Capital One Arena. Alex ➡️ Ky ➡️ AJ pic.twitter.com/2TeGrS5DfZ — Washington Wizards (@WashWizards) October 12, 2026 “I think it’s just getting comfortable [playing point guard],” George said. “I’ve been the point guard for most of my life. It’s just being able to do at this level, and we got a whole ton of support outside of this. So I’m gonna just go out and do it. “ George finished his impressive opening quarter with a 3-point barrage. The Miami product ran the baseline and found space on the wing before drilling his first triple. He followed with another three on the ensuing possession to give him 12 first-quarter points on 4-for-5 shooting.

stories.title: Adou Thiero says Matisse Thybulle has been helping him improve defensively
stories.summary: The young, athletic wing is learning from his accomplished veteran teammate
stories.detailText: LOS ANGELES, CALIFORNIA - OCTOBER 08: Darius Acuff Jr. #5 of the Sacramento Kings dribbles the ball against Adou Thiero #1 of the Los Angeles Lakers in a preseason game at Crypto.com Arena on October 08, 2026 in Los Angeles, California. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, user is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Luke Hales/Getty Images) | Getty Images Throughout his eight-year NBA career, Matisse Thybulle has been tasked with guarding all sorts of stars and offensive archetypes. His foremost traits defensively are his anticipation, timing and ability to cause havoc, which helped him earn consecutive All-Defensive Second Team accolades in 2020-21 and 2021-22 as a member of the Philadelphia 76ers. For his career, he’s averaged a staggering 2.8 steals and 1.4 blocks per 36 minutes, underscoring his knack for disrupting opposing offenses. Since signing with the Los Angeles Lakers this summer, Thybulle has seemingly been imparting whatever wisdom he can upon second-year wing Adou Thiero, whose tremendous athletic gifts suggest significant defensive upside. “We [were] talking about defense,” Thiero told reporters following an Oct. 6 loss to the Golden State Warriors. “That’s what he’s been helping me with the whole time. Just letting me know to pick my spots when I want to be aggressive, when not to, ways to keep the ball in front and just telling me different things defensively.” In 55 minutes this preseason, Thiero has collected four steals and two blocks, four of which (two steals, two blocks) came Thursday against the Sacramento Kings. During that game, he authored a handful of eye-popping plays defensively, including a rotation to deflect and steal a Maxime Raynaud short-roll pass, fighting around a screen to stay attached to Darius Acuff Jr. and get a hand on his jumper, and containing a Precious Achiuwa drive before blocking his shot. Here’s the block on Acuff: Adou picking up full court -> chase over back pressure -> blocks jumper pic.twitter.com/X9SqP4vWgN — Raj C. (@RajChipalu) October 10, 2026 After the Lakers’ preseason opener against the Sacramento Kings on Oct. 5, when they forced Sacramento into 27 turnovers, head coach JJ Redick said “clearly, that disruption we talked about carried over.” Across the two ensuing games, the Lakers have forced 51 more turnovers. The generally sloppy, experimental and shake-off-the-rust nature of preseason presumably inflates turnover numbers across the league. But the Lakers, with plenty of full-court pressure, are clearly trying to be a disruptive group defensively . Thiero’s size and athleticism can help amplify this identity, and it appears the veteran Thybulle is offering his own insights to accelerate the young forward’s development on that end. You can follow Jackson on Twitter at @jackfrank_jjf .

stories.title: Cooper Flagg poised to be one of the greats? Kyrie Irving thinks so
stories.summary: Irving had high praise for his young running mate, even comparing him to modern-day stars
stories.detailText: MACAO, CHINA - OCTOBER 6: Cooper Flagg #32 and Kyrie Irving #11 of the Dallas Mavericks pose for a photo as part of 2026 NBA China Games on October 6, 2026 in Macao, China. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and/or using this Photograph, user is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. Mandatory Copyright Notice: Copyright 2026 NBAE (Photo by Juan Ocampo/NBAE via Getty Images) | NBAE via Getty Images The Dallas Mavericks are working their way through their preseason schedule in anticipation of the 2026-2027 season tipping off later this month. Fresh off a two-game set in Macau, China, where they split wins and losses with the Houston Rockets, Kyrie Irving was asked about rising star Cooper Flagg. This led Irving to show respect to two former teammates, LeBron James and Kevin Durant, while drawing parallels to Flagg. “I think Coop falls in line in terms of having that competitive nature at a very young age” Irving’s choice of comps is well thought out. He has played with Durant, James and now Flagg throughout his career, affording him unique insight beyond what a more casual observer could glean. Also, all three of those players are versatile two-way types and all three were drafted into the NBA at the age of 18. Flagg, of course, is at the beginning of his NBA career, while Durant and James are nearer to the end of theirs, but to be grouped with such company is high praise indeed. If Flagg can grow into that caliber of player, it would make him a sure-fire Hall of Famer and NBA Champion, so let’s hope Irving is correct in what he is seeing. Already we have seen Flagg develop at a rapid rate across his Rookie of the Year campaign last season, and despite some struggles from the floor in the second game in Macau, Flagg nonetheless showcased the hard work he put in this offseason. Irving echoes this notion when discussing Flagg’s development going into his second year in the league. “I love that he’s a two-way player… I love that he cares about using his voice as he’s grown into year two” As viewers, a player growing into a vocal leader can be a bit more difficult to pick up on, but that seems to be part of Flagg’s evolution according to Irving. Flagg certainly led the way with his play last season, especially in the second half, so this next logical step in becoming a leader is a great sign. Joining a team with established veterans means there is a more clearly defined pecking order. Flagg wasn’t necessarily a leader until he earned it with his play, then witnessed a roster overhaul that put him firmly in the spotlight. Now in year two, he is set to be a vocal leader as well. That’s not easy for any player, especially one that is 19 years old, but accordingly to Irving, that time has arrived. “My first few years in the league were pretty tough on me… I struggled in certain areas, I needed veteran leadership… so now that I’m in this seat…” While Flagg develops into the player and leader he will one day become, Irving has his back. Encapsulated in Irving’s comments are why it is important to not abandon all veteran presence for the sake of a youth movement. Some are proponents of jettisoning Irving while others want to see him retire a Maverick. The stance of the latter is supported by Irving’s comments simply because you can’t replace experience the likes of which he has. A fellow Duke alum, Irving was also Rookie of the Year and has been through some ups and downs on his road to winning a championship and beyond. Both on the court and off, Irving appears more and more like an ideal running mate and veteran mentor for Flagg. "I give my respect to KD and Bron and they are on their own separate categories and trajectories and careers but I would say this, I think Coop falls in line in terms of having that competitive nature at a very young age… he's displaying in front of you guys what's capable of… https://t.co/JMoXET2V3S pic.twitter.com/uoNDZKiTDw — NBA (@NBA) October 11, 2026 I invite you to follow me @_80MPH on X, and check back often at Mavs Moneyball for all the latest on the Dallas Mavericks.

stories.title: Celtics, Pritchard agree to 2-year, $44.2 million contract extension (Report)
stories.summary: Pritchard is getting a well-deserved raise.
stories.detailText: Celtics, Pritchard agree to 2-year, $44.2 million contract extension (Report) originally appeared on NBC Sports Boston The Boston Celtics are extending the contract of one of their most important players through the end of the decade. The C’s and point guard Payton Pritchard have agreed to a two-year, $44.2 million contract extension with a mutual option for the 2029-30 campaign, ESPN’s Shams Charania reported Tuesday . Good security for Pritchard; another great value extension for Celtics. $22 million at start of deal is 12% of the cap. Pritchard had said this summer he wasn't in a rush for extension, but offseason market might have nudged him. https://t.co/QSiWjWDm2U — Chris Forsberg (@ChrisForsberg_) October 13, 2026 Pritchard’s current contract runs through the 2027-28 season. Breakdown of the Payton Pritchard extension: Existing contract 2026/27: $7.8M 2027/28: $8.3M Extension 2028/29: $21.2M 2029/30: $22.9M (Mutual Option) The first year of the extension is the maximum allowed (140% of the average player salary) Pritchard will be eligible to… — Bobby Marks (@BobbyMarks42) October 13, 2026 The Celtics acquired Pritchard with the No. 26 pick in the 2020 NBA Draft. stories.title: What's next in Karl-Anthony Towns, Knicks contract drama: Will he pick up his player option?
stories.summary: The deadline is Oct. 19 and most likely he turns down the option, but that can make him free agent.
stories.detailText: Contract extension talks between Karl-Anthony Towns and the Knicks are paused. New York management hit that pause button, and while it surprised Towns and he doesn't necessarily love it, he also wants to focus on the season and the Knicks' quest to repeat. However, one piece of drama remains before the season starts: The Oct. 19 deadline for Karl-Anthony Towns to pick up his $61 million player option for next season. Here is what that means: • If he declines the option, Towns will be in the final year of his contract (making $57.1 million this season) and would become an unrestricted free agent next summer without an extension. • If he picks up the option, he will be under contract for $61 million for the 2027-28 NBA season and cannot negotiate an extension with the Knicks until after the season. Towns will likely decline the option, allowing him and his agents to continue negotiating with the Knicks this season once New York management decides to (quietly) reopen those talks. The risk there for the Knicks is that without an extension, Towns can walk out the door for nothing as a free agent next summer. If he picks up the option and locks himself into the $61 million for next season, it almost unquestionably puts the Knicks into the second apron in a year, a line owner James Dolan said would be "suicidal" to cross, and it would force New York to consider trading him, either at the deadline or in the offseason. Towns doesn't want to leave New York, and it wants to keep him. As always, it's a question of money, but in the NBA, money = respect, so more emotion is tied to it. Towns feels he's earned that respect after two monster seasons with the Knicks and helping the team win its first title in 53 years. Towns, 30, is eligible for a four-year, $276 million contract extension, coming off an All-Star season in which he averaged 20.1 points and 11.9 rebounds per game while being central to their title run. Towns has been clear: He will take a discount off the max to stay in New York. The Knicks reportedly have offered four years, $200 million, or an average of $50 million per season. Towns has said the sides are not close. A league source not tied to these negotiations suggested to NBC Sports there should be a compromise around $225-$230 million—basically, an average salary at around what Towns will make this season. As long as Dolan refuses to enter the second apron, the Knicks are facing trouble, especially starting in the 2028-29 season. That's when a new extension for Jalen Brunson could start — and don't expect the same massive discount — as well as OG Anunoby. Josh Hart is in a similar situation to Towns and is extension-eligible right now, but those talks are on hold. Mikal Bridges is under contract for 28-29 at $38.9 million but also is extension eligible. Everyone will want to get paid after winning a title, it may not be that simple. That's all going to play out over the next couple of years, and be a talking point around a team trying to defend its title this season. As much as the Knicks management wants to avoid that. They aren't going to be able to avoid the rash of stories that will be written in the next week when Towns does — or more likely, does not — pick up his player option for next season.

stories.title: Michael Jordan’s thinking behind confusing NBC job — that ended after one season
stories.summary: Many were curious of Michael Jordan's broadcast future after his short stint as a “special on-air contributor” for NBC Sports’ NBA coverage in the 2025–26 season.
stories.detailText: Mike Tirico explains why Michael Jordan isn't back for another season of NBC Sports' NBA coverage. Many were curious of Michael Jordan’s broadcast future after his short stint as a “special on-air contributor” for NBC Sports’ NBA coverage in the 2025–26 season. The network aired one sit-down interview with NBC Sports’ play-by-play voice Mike Tirico and Jordan, entitled “MJ: Insights To Excellence,” that was spliced into five segments, lasting about three to four minutes apiece, which aired throughout the season — and an August report by Front Office Sports said Jordan was not expected to return to NBC. During Front Office Sports’s “Tuned In” summit in New York on Tuesday, Tirico explained that Jordan ultimately didn’t want to deal with the day-to-day of a broadcaster at this point in his life. NBC Sports’ play-by-play voice Mike Tirico interviews Michael Jordan as a “special on-air contributor” for NBC Sports’ NBA coverage in the 2025-26 season. X “I think Michael Jordan hadn’t been on TV for a long time for a reason,” Tirico said. “He likes being Michael Jordan. There’s an aura, even still, when he’s on camera, there’s an aura about Michael Jordan that is just different. “Sitting across from him, it’s just a different feel. And I think he is above the day-to-day conversation of ‘Hey, who’s the best point guard in the NBA right now? And who’s best this or the best that?’ “So I think in a controlled setting, talking about topics that he’s still passionate about with the sport, he loved it.” Tirico defended his sit-down with Jordan after some felt it was underwhelming because it was spread across an entire season and did not match the hype that came with the ballyhooed announcement. Michael Jordan as a “special on-air contributor” for NBC Sports’ NBA coverage in the 2025–26 season. X Mike Tirico talks before the game between the Portland Trail Blazers and the Philadelphia 76ers on March 3, 2025 at the Wells Fargo Center in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. NBAE via Getty Images “I love the fact that we did one interview and you can say what you want about it airing once or being spread out over our series of pregame shows during the year,” Tirico said. “It’s a year later and people are still talking about it and people are still asking about it, which is to me, all the reason that it was completely worth it. “And I will say, it was damn cool to hang with MJ and talk basketball and talk business and golf and all that other stuff. I don’t think he wants to be — if he wanted to be, we would all run to have him on every single day, but that’s just not what he wants to do, I think at this point in his career in life.” “We have an obligation to pay it forward. That’s part of what this is all about.” Watch Michael Jordan’s first conversation with Mike Tirico in the first edition of MJ: Insights To Excellence. pic.twitter.com/7tfzGm6SpM — NBA on NBC and Peacock (@NBAonNBC) October 22, 2025 Jordan, a six-time NBA champion and Hall of Famer, co-owns the NASCAR team, 23XI Racing, with current NASCAR Cup Series driver Denny Hamlin.

stories.summary: The Knicks won the championship and then seemingly forgot how to play basketball. Only, you know, it’s the preseason, so they might as well go 0-5 for all I care. Here’s the latest from the first half of a back-to-back series of games ending north of the border later today. Mike Brown On the competition […]
stories.detailText: NEW YORK, NY - OCTOBER 12: Karl-Anthony Towns #32 of the New York Knicks goes up for the rebound during the game against the Minnesota Timberwolves on October 12, 2026 at Madison Square Garden in New York City, New York. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. Mandatory Copyright Notice: Copyright 2026 NBAE (Photo by Nathaniel S. Butler/NBAE via Getty Images) | NBAE via Getty Images The Knicks won the championship and then seemingly forgot how to play basketball. Only, you know, it’s the preseason, so they might as well go 0-5 for all I care. Here’s the latest from the first half of a back-to-back series of games ending north of the border later today. "Trying to let the guys understand how important the process is what I'm all about right now." Mike Brown talks about he and the Knicks focusing on the process in the preseason: pic.twitter.com/9rS4Q3gBLQ — SNY Knicks (@sny_knicks) October 13, 2026 Mike Brown On the competition for the Knicks’ third-string center position: “They should all be on a roster this year. There’s no experiments, in my opinion. These guys are all legitimate NBA players. They’re all great guys and in some way, shape or form, I can see each of them contributing this way or that way and it’s not gonna be an easy decision.” On the quality of the Knicks’ centers in training camp: “I’ve been in a lot of training camps and collectively, this is probably — now when I say the best, I’m not saying the most talented — this is the best group of centers I’ve been around. All of them bring something different to the table.” On potentially playing Karl-Anthony Towns more minutes at power forward: “I’m not sure yet. There’s a chance he may play a little bit more at the four, but what does that equate to? Again, I’m not sure. He has a better feel, and I have a better feel of how to use him when he’s there because we have to make some adjustments to what we do. But I couldn’t give you an exact number.” On the mentality and energy required from the Knicks’ still-unknown, third-string center: “You hope that there’s a passion, an energy and a focus coming from that spot because, at times, a person can start; at times they can be the No. 2; and at times, they’ll be the No. 3, and with the minutes fluctuating, you’re gonna have to generate some internal energy at times to go play in a low-minute game, to sit there and maybe not play one or two games in a row, maybe three games in a row. So you look for that and then you just look for somebody that’s gonna play hard at the end of the day, try to do the things that you ask on both sides of the floor and can bring something a little different than the two guys in front of you bring.” On Andre Drummond’s defensive communication against Minnesota: “The blocks are great, but I’m not a huge shot-blocking guy. His communication right now is unbelievable. Usually your big is the one that sees everything out in front and so he’s usually your quarterback of your defense. A lot of bigs aren’t great talkers though. Like Draymond [Green] is one of the best in the league… and I thought Andre’s communication tonight – and it’s been good [so far] – but tonight it was off the charts.” On Drummond’s defensive performance against the Wolves and why it excites him: “The blocks are good, him defending the pick-and-roll the right way, being big, there are a lot of good things that he did, but just watching him, and more importantly listening to him, man that got me really excited.” On the development of Pacome Dadiet and Mohamed Diawara: “I thought [Dadiet] had a pretty good game. I thought he had a pretty good game the game before. … Both [Dadiet and Diawara] are long, they’re obviously young and they’re talented and I’m gonna keep coaching them and they’re gonna keep getting better.” On intentionally keeping the Knicks’ preseason offense simple to test their execution: “The truth of the matter is I’m kind of hamstringing our guys offensively. Real generic with what we’re running offensively because I want to see if they can execute when a team gets rhythm and they start denying or putting pressure on us because they know what’s coming. Can we execute our counters? Can we still get to our spots offensively and execute our actions? Can we play fast doing it? Those are little things I’m looking at offensively.” On prioritizing the process over results in the preseason: “For me, it’s more about the process, not necessarily the end result. Defensively, are we making sure we’re playing with next-play speed? And, for the most part, I thought we did. We had some breakdowns execution-wise in terms of what our assignments were, but those things can be cleaned up in time. We’ll keep watching film and keep drilling it and all that other stuff.” On his expectations for when things turn ugly in the regular season: “I want to see how we react when we lose 3 in a row or 4 in a row and you guys are on us and the fans are on us. Let’s see if we can keep trying to [have an upward trajectory] in tough times.” KAT, OG, Mikal, Josh & JB introduced at the Garden pic.twitter.com/8mtV71ESpe — New York Basketball (@NBA_NewYork) October 12, 2026 Jalen Brunson On Mike Brown’s personality and authenticity: “I feel like he’s always genuinely himself. He doesn’t really care what people say or think about him.” On his first meeting with Mike Brown and how the coach established a relationship with him: “Honestly, Day 1, he kind of set the tone. I remember, I said this like last year: He came down to Jersey in the summer, and [we] sat, had dinner, talked for two, two and a half, three hours, whatever, and just did not talk about basketball or what we were gonna do.” Josh Hart On Mike Brown’s personality: “He’s super chill. He’s more of a ‘Who Let the Dogs Out’ kind of guy.” Drummond bag work? pic.twitter.com/BoSsAg1jBi — New York Basketball (@NBA_NewYork) October 13, 2026 Andre Drummond On changing his free-throw approach after years of struggling at the line: “I feel like a lot of people have opinions about what a good free throw looks like, right? So over my career I’ve had different coaches and teams I played for that tried to help me adjust and make it easier for me. Obviously, the stuff they said in practice would work, but when I got in the game, I’d overthink it. So I just simplified it, did a routine I’ve done since a child, and shoot the same shot.” On simplifying his shooting routine and avoiding overthinking: “I simplified it and stopped listening to a bunch of people. Just shooting the same shot over and over again and not worrying about the results. Sometimes, in the past, I would get frustrated if I miss, and I would try to overcorrect. Then, it’s a domino effect and more and more misses, and then I’m frustrated and I’m out of whack.” On why free throws became a struggle throughout his life: “It’s not something I struggled with growing up. It was more so just having a bunch of people in my ear and not being able to focus on one thing.” Broadcasting for NBC from the Garden as the Knicks raise the banner Oct 20th: Carmelo Anthony pic.twitter.com/ExwFTR0fQ1 — New York Basketball (@NBA_NewYork) October 13, 2026 Carmelo Anthony On the Knicks’ upcoming championship banner ceremony and what it means to him: “It’s hard to put it into words, especially for me as somebody who’s been a part of that organization. I understand what it was like to have to build something over there, and for them to finally do that, it just makes that journey and those years finally mean something. “We didn’t win it, but now [Jalen Brunson] and them can kind of take that and elongate that and celebrate just the history of what everybody put in.” On the significance of raising the Knicks’ championship banner: “It’s validation and completion. Once we raise that up, we got it forever.” Reggie Miller On the Knicks postponing contract negotiations with Karl-Anthony Towns: “You hope behind closed doors the contract stuff doesn’t become an issue. I like the Knicks coming out publicly and saying we’re going to table discussions until a later date. That doesn’t mean they’re not going to negotiate. It basically means you guys [media] can’t ask the players about their contract situation.” On Towns’ contract situation potentially affecting the Knicks’ chances of repeating: “If they want to be successful and they want to have a chance to repeat, you’re going to need a healthy KAT, mentally. You don’t want him being a malcontent, worrying about his contract behind closed doors. Because when KAT is at his best and on board, they’re hard to beat. But if he’s worried about his contract situation . . . I think a deal will get done. It’s going to be between the 200 and the 277. So meet in the middle, sign it, and let’s move on.” On the Knicks’ championship chances and the improved Eastern Conference: “They have a great chance of repeating. The problem is the East has gotten so much better and now the Knicks will have a bullseye on their back every single game because they’re the champs. Every night they take the floor, they’ve got to play their best. That wasn’t the case the last few years.” LaMelo hits the three then had some words for the Knicks bench 😂 pic.twitter.com/rhkYwbxDF6 — Kyle Ingram (@SnapshotKyle) October 12, 2026 Chris Finch On LaMelo Ball’s shot selection after acquiring him from Charlotte: “It’s something we talked about coming in. He’s been pretty good, and then when you watch it every day, you see — OK, the one-legged thing, he kind of shoots it like that every time, really. Some are a little more exaggerated than others, so it’s not too unusual when you see it every day.” On Ball becoming more focused on playmaking with Minnesota: “He’s been deferential here. He’s not looking just to kind of shoot, shoot, shoot. Sometimes, we [the Wolves] forget how good of a scorer he can actually be. We’ve been asking him to be way more into play-making for us, and then the out-of-context shots, he hasn’t had many of those. “And the deep 3s, he makes them. No one complains about Steph [Curry’s] deep threes, [so we won’t complain about LaMelo’s]. And then he gives us a guy we can close the game with. You can put the ball in his hands, and he can make shots from different spots on then floor.” On the Timberwolves’ pursuit and acquisition of LaMelo Ball: “Of course a talent like that doesn’t often come available especially after the year [the Hornets] had. So when it picked up speed it was real exciting to think about, and it’s been pretty exciting to watch it play out in front of us.” On Ball’s personality and his chemistry with Anthony Edwards: “[LaMelo] is always in a great mood, always comes in smiling. He and Anthony have this shared quality that they’re really hard to stay mad at, and they do some things that you want to get mad at, but they have a reflective joy and I think that’s important. They tease the joy out of each other as practice goes along, so that kind of adds to the overall spirit of the group which we really needed. “We’ve referred to ourselves as a moody team at times. We’ve traded moodiness for giddiness, so we’re happy to get back to some sort of equilibrium.” Everything in preseason is fake including the fights pic.twitter.com/JYS6T4msT9 — New York Basketball (@NBA_NewYork) October 13, 2026

stories.title: Kyle Anderson speaks on Jamal Shead, Lil Wayne, and his place on the Raptors
stories.summary: The small forward brings his perspective on team spirit and his veteran role on the Raptors
stories.detailText: Kyle Anderson doesn’t want to ruffle any feathers. At least, that’s what Slo Mo, the 13 year NBA veteran, said during last Wednesday’s practice. “I don’t want to be like, ‘oh, I’m the old head. You gotta do it my way,’” said Anderson. The former Timberwolf understands that he’s from a different era of NBA players. “There’s a whole generation after me that came in,” said Anderson. “These guys are 22 years old. That’s crazy to me.” 33 year old Anderson is one of the Raptors’ latest additions to the roster, making his way from Minnesota to Ontario, and the forward seems to be embracing a mentor role on his new team, while not trying to make everyone see his way. “I don’t like to impose myself like that,” he said, speaking about the young players on the Raptors. “They want to come into my world, then yeah, you know, I’ll show you what I’m listening to,” Anderson explained, drawing the line at telling his teammates to “listen to this Jay-Z or [that they] gotta listen to this Lil Wayne. They gonna be looking at me like I’m crazy.” VANCOUVER, BRITISH COLUMBIA – OCTOBER 10: Kyle Anderson #13 of the Toronto Raptors reacts during the preseason game between Los Angeles Clippers and Toronto Raptors at Rogers Arena on October 10, 2026 in Vancouver, British Columbia. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Elizabeth Ruiz Ruiz/Getty Images) | Getty Images Asked about how he gelled with his younger peers on the Raptors, Anderson explained that “we spent, you know, more time, more time than NBA teams, usually… uh, spend together in the summer.” Even beforehand, the forward had kept his eyes on some of Toronto’s guards. “I always got like a group of young guys that I enjoy watching in the league,” he noted, “and Jamal, every time I would watch him, he was able to affect the game without scoring… I just enjoyed watching him, like how they played hard, played together, um, always like in the gaps in the passing lanes.” When asked about the type of role he might take on the Raptors, the veteran described a conversation with coach Darko Rajaković, where the coach described that Anderson “need[s] to be ready to play the 5… maybe handle the ball, you know, things like that… I’m comfortable there and I think the game is shifted to kind of a small ball 5 at times,” the player said. The Raptors have struggled publicly with depth at the centre position, and ESPN’s depth chart notes that behind Jakob Poeltl and Collin Murray-Boyles lies Trayce Jackson-Davis followed by Jamison Battle, with Kyle Anderson listed as a third string power forward. It seems that there may be situations in which Anderson is lining up at the pivot instead, however, with Rajaković potentially betting on Anderson’s combination of defensive prowess and experience. “I think he wants me to come in here and use my veteran experience, you know, help out,” said Anderson. “We have a young team, so help out the young guys. Just be there for them. It’s a long season.” Indeed. The 82 game stretch is a false finish line, with the Raptors likely to make the playoffs this season. Toronto will use Anderson’s depth and veteran presence to take its young core far, and Slo Mo seems happy to be along for the ride.

stories.summary: In a SEGABABA, NY travels to Toronto for a date with Kawhi and some former friends.
stories.detailText: NEW YORK, NY - APRIL 10: Karl-Anthony Towns #32 of the New York Knicks drives to the basket during the game against the Toronto Raptors on April 10, 2026 at Madison Square Garden in New York City, New York. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. Mandatory Copyright Notice: Copyright 2026 NBAE (Photo by Nathaniel S. Butler/NBAE via Getty Images) | NBAE via Getty Images The ramp-up to the regular season continues tonight when the World Champion Knicks travel to Scotiabank Arena to face the Raptors. Toronto has split its first two scrimmages, beating the Clippers and falling to Miami, while New York has dropped three straight. Tonight’s tilt will be a showcase for the reserves, as coach Mike Brown intends to sit his starters. It’s the second night of a back-to-back. How will their bench hold up while, we’re told, Toronto will get its first play from Kawhi Leonard? Methinks trouble be in the cards, prognostication fans. The two teams last met on April 10 at MSG. The good guys won 112-95. Captain Jalen Brunson dropped 29, Karl-Anthony Towns added 22 and 10. Scottie Barnes and Brandon (no longer with the team) Ingram each posted 15 for Toronto. New York has beaten the Raptors 13 straight times in the regular season! (Probably a good thing that tonight won’t count.) Last season was a positive step forward for the Toronto. Despite some poorly timed injuries, Darko Rajakovic’s club secured the fifth seed, finished 46-36, and were a top-five defense. Their offense was middle of the pack, a problem addressed with the offseason acquisition of Kawhi (celebrated pitchman) Leonard. Kawhi was their big move this summer. The blockbuster return of Kawhi Leonard (finalized in mid-September after an NBA investigation delayed a deal originally made inn June) sent Brandon Ingram, Gradey Dick, unprotected first-round picks in 2031 and 2033, second-rounders in 2030 and 2033, and a 2027 first-round swap to the Clippers. He then signed a two-year, $115 million extension. Beyond that, Toronto drafted forward Allen Graves 19th overall and guard Jaden Bradley 50th, added veteran forward Kyle Anderson on a one-year minimum, re-signed Alijah Martin, and extended guard Jamal Shead to a three-year, $24 million deal. They lost Sandro Mamukelashvili and Jonathan Mogbo in free agency. OAKAAKUYOAKs RJ Barrett and Immanuel Quickley remain key players in their program, as does Scottie Barnes. A serviceable, but aging, Jakob Poeltl anchors the paint with solid rebounding and rim protection. Leonard, making his preseason debut, will be an upgrade from Ingram, provided he stays healthy. We’re just as curious as you to see tonight’s starting lineup for New York. Last night, the club fell 122-104 to a Timberwolves team that was determined to pull on Superman’s cape under the bright lights of Broadway. Against the Raps, we should see extended time for Deuce McBride, Tyler Kolek, and Landry Shamet, and hopefully better play from Mohamed Diawara. As for the center battle, James Wiseman, Drew Eubanks, and Tony Bradley will have yet another opportunity to win over coach Brown. Prediction? Probably a loss, hoss. Enjoy the bonus basketball. Game Details Who: New York Knicks (0-3) at Toronto Raptors (1-1) Date: Tuesday, October 13, 2026 Time: 7:00 PM ET Place: Scotiabank Arena, Toronto, ON TV: MSG Follow: @ptknicksblog and bsky

stories.summary: The Washington Wizards are about to begin a new era led by forward AJ Dybantsa, Trae Young and Anthony Davis. Capital One Arena, their home venue, is also nearly done with a major renovation. And fans want a rebrand of the franchise. When teams are not particularly great on the court, field, ice, etc., I […]
stories.detailText: WASHINGTON, DC - SEPTEMBER 28: AJ Dybantsa #4 of the Washington Wizards poses for a portrait during Media Day at CareFirst Arena on September 28, 2026 in Washington, DC. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Scott Taetsch/Getty Images). | Getty Images The Washington Wizards are about to begin a new era led by forward AJ Dybantsa, Trae Young and Anthony Davis. Capital One Arena, their home venue, is also nearly done with a major renovation. And fans want a rebrand of the franchise. When teams are not particularly great on the court, field, ice, etc., I can see why fans want the logo, colors or even a team name to change. But it appears that what fans are clamoring for isn’t simply white noise. Monumental Sports & Entertainment is looking into this as well. According to Joshua Robbins of The Athletic, Monumental Sports & Entertainment executives are looking closely into the possibility of rebranding the team’s logos and/or color schemes. Here is a snippet from that piece regarding a possible rebrand happening when Capital One Arena’s renovations are complete. “There’s a commitment to doing the homework and the research and to doing it really, really effectively and not doing things in the moment, so I think a lot of this will be an evolving process,” [MSE Chief Commerical Officer Jim] Van Stone said. “(The) 2027-28 (season) is a big year for us because the building project will be completed. That’s a major element for us. Certainly, we will be in the mix of looking at uniform designs. … There’s an openness to that. Some of the long-term logos or other changes, probably a little bit of a longer runway. But I do think the feedback that we’re getting from fans puts us in a really good situation to evaluate all of that.” One thing Monumental Sports isn’t considering is renaming the team. So a return to the Washington Bullets is not happening. Though the Wizards have various alternates like every NBA team, their traditional red jerseys and white jerseys have largely remained the same since the 2011-12 season when Monumental Sports decided to change the color scheme to red, white and blue. What do you think about the possibility of a rebrand? Let us know in the comments below.

stories.title: Delaware Blue Coats hire Brad Jones as general manager
stories.summary: The Sixers have a new front-office boss for their G League affiliate.
stories.detailText: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - JANUARY 22: A view of the ball sitting on the Philadelphia 76ers logo on the court during a game against the Houston Rockets at Xfinity Mobile Arena on January 22, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Emilee Chinn/Getty Images) | Getty Images The NBA regular season is right around the corner, but it’s not the only level of basketball preparing for a new campaign. As the G League gears up for 2026-27, the Delaware Blue Coats are making a significant front-office change, hiring Brad Jones as their new general manager. ESPN’s Dave McMenamin was the first to report the news. The Delaware Blue Coats, the Philadelphia 76ers’ G League affiliate, are hiring Brad Jones as their next general manager, team sources told me and @krisrhim1 . Jones joins Delaware after working for the G League offices for the last eight years. — Dave McMenamin (@mcten) October 13, 2026 McMenamin reported that Jones was selected by Sixers President of Basketball Operations Mike Gansey and Executive Vice President of Basketball Operations Jameer Nelson. He will take over a role previously held by Ariana Andonian, who departed to become general manager of the WNBA’s Los Angeles Sparks. So, who is Jones? He began his career with the Orlando Magic, where he overlapped with Nelson during the latter’s playing days. Jones worked his way up from an internship to positions on the team’s video and player personnel staffs. Most recently, he has worked in the NBA G League’s New York offices, handling player contracts, transactions, basketball operations and league affairs. Between his past stop(s) and his work with the G League office, he’s well equipped to run this team. The Delaware Blue Coats’ roster is expected to feature several intriguing names this season, with two-way players Caleb Love and Rayan Rupert likely spending time in Delaware. The roster could become even more notable once NBA teams finalize their cuts, as players such as Tacko Fall, Saint Thomas and potentially Jameer Nelson Jr. could also join the fold. The Sixers also have a vacant two-way contract spot that they could fill in the coming weeks or months. With a new general manager in place and another season on the horizon, the Blue Coats appear well-positioned to remain one of the G League’s more compelling teams. Delaware has consistently served as an important developmental pipeline for the 76ers, helping players earn opportunities at the NBA level while providing meaningful minutes for young prospects. Players such as Justin Edwards and Adem Bona have logged stints with the Coats in the past. As roster decisions are finalized and training camps conclude, the Blue Coats’ roster picture will become clearer. Between established G League veterans, two-way players and potential additions following NBA cuts, there should be no shortage of storylines to follow once the season gets underway.

stories.title: Bucks Reacts Survey: Who should Milwaukee cut?
stories.summary: Jon Horst and the Milwaukee Bucks have some tough decisions to make to finalise the roster.
stories.detailText: MILWAUKEE, WISCONSIN - DECEMBER 03: Caris LeVert #8 of the Detroit Pistons shoots the ball against Kyle Kuzma #18 of the Milwaukee Bucks during the fourth quarter at Fiserv Forum on December 03, 2025 in Milwaukee, Wisconsin. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Patrick McDermott/Getty Images) | Getty Images Welcome to SB Nation Reacts, a survey of fans across the NBA. Throughout the year we ask questions of the most plugged-in Bucks fans and fans across the country. The elephant has been in the (locker) room all offseason and, despite anticipation of its removal, it remains. Of course, this particular elephant is which players won’t make the final roster. With no two-for-one trades in sight, the Bucks currently carrying 17 standard contracts, and NBA teams only able to roster a maximum of 15 standard contracts during the season, Jon Horst and his staff will likely have to make the very difficult decision to waive two players. And that decision has to come soon—rosters must be set by 4:00 p.m. CT on October 19. So, which approach should they take? Remove the dead wood One option for Horst is to rid the roster of veterans who aren’t in the Bucks’ long-term plans. While plenty of fans would like this to include Gary Trent Jr., Milwaukee already has too much dead money on its books, so more likely veteran cut candidates are Kyle Kuzma and Caris LeVert. As the oldest players on the roster, Kuzma and LeVert could be cut without impacting the Bucks much on the court. However, doing so would mean Milwaukee no longer has their very tradable expiring salaries—$20.3m for Kuzma, $14.8m for LeVert—which, attached to draft capital or players with upside, could net the Bucks a quality player come trade deadline (or draft capital if the Bucks took on longer-term “bad” salary). Bite the bullet on youth On the other end of the spectrum, Horst could opt to cut youth that, for one reason or another, doesn’t seem to have the place on the roster it once might’ve. In this line of thinking, Bogoljub Marković is a prime candidate as he’s both a developmental project and on an inexpensive four-year, $9.3m contract that includes a team option in the final year. Outside of Marković, the options are less obvious. Kasparas Jakučionis’ name has recently been floated in the comments, but it’s hard to envision that scenario playing out given how insistent the Bucks were on him being included in the Giannis trade. Kevin Porter Jr., on the other hand, returned to the Bucks by exercising his $5.4m player option (i.e., not by negotiating a new deal with the team), has a history of injury, and isn’t likely to bring much back in a trade. Plus, Milwaukee’s guard room is crowded . Of course, he is one of the most talented players on the roster, so cutting him wouldn’t come without risk. Take the easy way out Somewhere in between the veteran and youth options is Pete Nance. It’s fitting, too. At 26, he’s not really a prospect anymore—yes, Porter is also 26, but his upside far exceeds Nance’s—and with only 68 career games he’s not exactly an established veteran either. More conveniently, at least from a roster-trimming perspective, he’s on a non-guaranteed deal. Truthfully, cutting Nance would hurt. After all, he’s an ideal third-string big, who makes the right play, spaces the floor, and does no harm . But he’s the easiest first step to solve the Bucks’ roster dilemma and would potentially (likely?) return to the team on a two-way deal anyway. Beyond Nance, things get a little more complicated, but Jericho Sims is the next “easiest” cut. Like Nance, he’s not old—Sims will turn 28 on October 20—but he’s certainly not young either and, at this point, he is who he is. Moreover, he’s on a measly one-year, $2.8m deal. There you have it, three potential paths the Bucks could take to trim the roster to 15. Which strikes your fancy? Alternatively, you might want a combination of these—or something different entirely. If so, be sure to share your GM wheeling and dealing in the comments. Sign up here to participate in the weekly emailed surveys:

stories.title: V.J. Edgecombe joins Jaylen Brown's stream to showcase Sixers' chemistry
stories.summary: Jaylen Brown is using his Twitch stream to connect with his new Sixers teammates, starting with a visit from V.J. Edgecombe.
stories.detailText: V.J. Edgecombe joins Jaylen Brown's stream to showcase Sixers' chemistry originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia It didn’t take long for Jaylen Brown to bring one of his new Sixers teammates onto his Twitch stream. On October 9, just one day before Philadelphia faced Boston in a preseason matchup, V.J. Edgecombe joined Brown on the stream. Brown, who was making his first return to TD Garden since joining the Sixers, did not play in the game and reportedly watched from the locker room. Jaylen Brown reportedly decided to watch the 76ers-Celtics preseason game in the locker room in his return to Boston 🤔 The Sixers won’t play in Boston again until January 2027 👀 https://t.co/aSnyiLui8h — Bleacher Report (@BleacherReport) October 11, 2026 Although Brown’s return to Boston drew attention, his focus is already on building chemistry with his new teammates in Philadelphia. He recently spoke about his plans to bring more Sixers players onto his stream, explaining that several teammates had already expressed interest in joining him. “I can’t wait to introduce you to some of my teammates who have been hitting me up like ‘I want to be on the stream’ so I can’t wait to tap in, for y’all to tap in with some of them. “For the most part we’ve been vibing, man. Everything’s been smooth, we’ve just been getting acclimated.” Brown also explained why he sees streaming as an opportunity to connect with his teammates beyond basketball. “We ain’t gonna be on here doing nothing just letting you get to know us as human beings, being authentic, but also just building team chemistry. I think building chemistry is important for a team to be able to vibe in order to try to accomplish goals. I wasn’t as successful in my attempts of being able to get more guys on my previous team, so hopefully this team I’ll be able to be more successful in getting guys.” Jaylen Brown says he’ll try to get more Sixers teammates on stream compared to how it went in Boston: “I wasn’t as successful in my attempts in being able to get more guys on my previous team (on stream). I think it’s the uncomfortably streaming… like you say the wrong thing is taken out of context. I’m not sugarcoating nothing.” — Polymarket Hoops (@PolymarketHoops) October 10, 2026 Brown didn’t have to wait long to make good on that plan. Edgecombe soon joined the stream, giving the two an opportunity to get to know each other outside of the practice facility. VJ pulled up to Jaylen Brown’s livestream 🔥 (h/t @ohnohedidnt24) https://t.co/fn1LeqWVst — Sleeper76ers (@sleeper76ers) October 10, 2026 After briefly connecting with teammate Justin Edwards on FaceTime, Brown and Edgecombe turned their attention to getting to know each other better. Their conversation touched on Edgecombe’s upbringing in the Bahamas, his family and even a hypothetical question about which teammate he would choose to survive with on a deserted island. Edgecombe’s answer? Brown. It might seem like a small, lighthearted moment, but these are the kinds of interactions that can help teammates develop a connection away from the court. With the regular season still ahead, Brown is already taking steps toward the team chemistry he believes is essential to success. And if his Twitch stream is any indication, those connections are beginning to take shape. Edgecombe and Brown shared the court for the first time in the Sixers’ preseason opener against the Knicks on October 5. Just one game together was enough for Brown to come away impressed. View this post on Instagram A post shared by NBC Sports Philadelphia (@nbcsphilly) Their partnership is still taking shape, but Edgecombe already trusts Brown enough to pick him for a deserted island.
