stories.title: Bears DE Montez Sweat suspended two games for violating NFL's PED policy
stories.summary: The NFL has issued a two-game suspension to Bears defensive end Montez Sweat for violating the league's policy on performance-enhancing substances.
stories.detailText: Chicago Bears defensive end Montez Sweat has been suspended for two games without pay for violating the league's policy on performance-enhancing substances. Sweat, 30, will miss the Bears' Week 6 matchup at the Atlanta Falcons and Week 7 against the New England Patriots . He will be eligible for reinstatement on Friday, Oct. 23. Sweat's suspension comes two days after fellow Bears defensive end Dayo Odeyingbo exited the first half of Chicago's 31-7 loss to the Green Bay Packers with a quad injury and did not return. Coach Ben Johnson did not have an update on Odeyingbo's health Monday. Sweat has totaled seven tackles and two sacks over Chicago's first five games of the season. He led the Bears with 10 sacks last season. The Bears activated defensive end Shemar Turner off the physically unable to perform list Tuesday. Turner, a former second-round pick, has been back at practice since Sept. 23 and will take Sweat's spot on the 53-man roster. Turner was limited to five games during his rookie season and suffered a season-ending ACL tear on Oct. 26, 2025. He provides depth to a thin group at defensive end led by Austin Booker , who has a team-high four sacks. "I think with any of these guys that are coming off the PUP list, to think that any of them would be ready to go in there and play 50, 60, 70 plays in a game, I think that would be unrealistic to think," defensive coordinator Dennis Allen said last week. "With all of these guys, as we begin to get some of them back, I think the prudent action would be start to incorporate them in and yet don't expect them to be full-time players initially on."

stories.title: Packers sign CB Elijah Culp, release high-priced UDFA
stories.summary: Elijah Culp joins cornerback Domani Jackson on Green Bay’s practice squad
stories.detailText: (Photo by Nick Cammett/Diamond Images via Getty Images) | Diamond Images/Getty Images The Green Bay Packers announced on Tuesday that the team signed cornerback Elijah Culp, whom the team brought in on Monday for a tryout . There’s little info out there about Culp, but here’s what we wrote on him yesterday: Culp is an undrafted rookie who played for four different college programs over six seasons (Austin Peay, Troy, Charlotte and James Madison). He originally signed with the Arizona Cardinals, coached by Matt LaFleur’s brother, before signing with the Indianapolis Colts’ practice squad in late September. He was released by the Colts last week and previously had a workout with the New York Giants prior to signing with Indianapolis. Worth noting: Culp’s defensive coordinator in Arizona is Nick Rallis, who also served as the defensive coordinator under then-head coach Jonathan Gannon, now the Packers’ defensive coordinator. It’s possible that he has familiarity with the scheme. Green Bay decided to release guard Josh Gesky to make room for the addition of Culp. Gesky signed for $215,000 guaranteed after going undrafted, making him the second-highest paid UDFA in the Packers’ 2026 class behind only edge defender Nyjalik Kelly . Green Bay was already oversigned on the offensive line, as the team carried 15 players at the position between the 53-man roster and the 17-man practice squad — which led the NFL . Currently, here’s the breakdown of the Packers’ practice squad: QB: Kedon Slovis RB: Damon Bankston WR: Isaiah Neyor, Quincy Skinner Jr. and Coleman Owen TE: Drake Dabney OL: Dalton Cooper, Dillon Wade and Mekhi Becton DL: David Blay Jr. ED: Nyjalik Kelly and Arron Mosby LB: Jack Dingle CB: Domani Jackson and Elijah Culp S: Kahlef Hailassie K: Lenny Krieg (international exemption) Of the 17 players on the practice squad, only 7 of them were Packers at the end of training camp: Neyor, Dabney, Cooper, Wade, Kelly, Mosby and Jackson. The other 10 players were outside signings made by Green Bay. The fact that the Packers parted ways with Gesky is interesting, as the team has an open roster spot on the 53-man roster, and they’re expected to have another open spot once defensive lineman Javon Hargrave (Achilles) goes on the injured reserve for his season-ending injury. Green Bay could have easily moved up a practice squad player and added Culp without losing their rights to Gesky, if they wanted to, but elected to not go down that route.

stories.title: Sources: Rams release kicker Mevis after miscues in loss, sign Grupe from Jets
stories.summary: The Rams are releasing kicker Harrison Mevis and signing Blake Grupe off the Jets' practice squad, sources told NFL Network's Ian Rapoport and Mike Garafolo on Tuesday.
stories.detailText: LOS ANGELES -- The Rams are releasing kicker Harrison Mevis and signing Blake Grupe off the New York Jets ' practice squad, sources told NFL Network's Ian Rapoport and Mike Garafolo on Tuesday. The change comes after Mevis missed a 50-yard field goal attempt in the first quarter and had a 48-yard kick blocked in overtime that would have been the winner in Monday night's 37-34 loss to the Buffalo Bills . After the game, Rams coach Sean McVay said he would "evaluate everything" about the kicking unit. "In the kicking game, especially with our PAT, field goal, not even close to good enough," McVay said. "It cost us the game tonight." The Rams have had three blocked field goal attempts since the start of last season, tied for the most in the NFL, according to ESPN Research. Los Angeles has had 81 missed or blocked kicks under McVay (since 2017, including playoffs), which is third most in the league. Mevis was 5-for-9 on field goal attempts this season. Grupe started last season with the New Orleans Saints , going 18 of 26 on field goal attempts. After he was cut during the season, he signed with the Indianapolis Colts and made all 11 of his field goal attempts. The loss Monday night was just one of five games that special teams have cost the Rams since the start of last season. In Week 16 of the 2025 season against the Seattle Seahawks , the Rams allowed a 58-yard punt return touchdown in the fourth quarter, sparking a 16-point comeback. The next day, the Rams fired special teams coordinator Chase Blackburn after three seasons. The Rams hired Bubba Ventrone as special teams coordinator in January.

stories.title: Saints owner Gayle Benson: I won't accept this level of play as our standard
stories.summary: Seats are starting to heat up in New Orleans.
stories.detailText: {"unknownError":"There has been an error","expiredError":"This video has been expired due to copyright restrictions.","unavailableError":"This content is not yet available.","georestrictedError":"This content is not available in your location.","networkId":"169843","adManagerUrl":"https://mssl.fwmrm.net/libs/adm/6.51.0/AdManager.js","serverId":"https://29773.v.fwmrm.net/ad/g/1","profileId":"169843:nbcu_web_jwp_cs_moat_https","afid":"140315314","caid":"nbcs_nbc_pft_vikingsoffense_261012","csid":"nbcsports_embed_on_domain","sfid":"","adHocGroup":"","athlete":"","businessUnit":"NBC Sports","category":"","duration":"473573","event":"","externalAdvertiserId":"nbcs_nbc_pft_vikingsoffense_261012","genre":"News","guid":"nbc_pft_vikingsoffense_261012","league":"NFL","network":"","platform":"PC","playlist":"","show":"ProFootballTalk","sport":"Football","subtype":"","team":"Minnesota Vikings, New Orleans Saints","title": "Murray, Vikings offense turns in best game of year","datePublished":"","videoPageUrl": "https://www.nbcsports.com/watch/nfl/profootballtalk/minnesota-vikings-offense-looked-the-best-all-season-in-win-over-saints","availableDate":"2026-10-12T13:29:59Z","expirationDate":"","countries":""} Seats are starting to heat up in New Orleans. The Saints lost to the Vikings in Week 5 to fall to 1-4 on the season. The last three losses came in a row and all three came at the Superdome, including a Monday night drubbing at the hands of the Vikings on a night when the Saints celebrated the 20th anniversary of their post-Katrina return to the stadium. On Tuesday, owner Gayle Benson said that loss "truly disappointed me" during a speech at the Greater New Orleans Quarterback Club Luncheon that left no doubt about how disappointed she is with the team's performance in general. Benson said fans "are right to expect more than we have delivered" through the first five weeks of the season. “As the owner, the responsibility does start with me,” Benson said, via Rod Walker of NOLA.com. “I will not make excuses and I will not accept this level of performance as our standard. I am committed to making the decisions necessary to improving this team. Everyone on this organization understands the urgency. We must prepare better, execute consistently and correct mistakes that are costing us the games.” Benson didn't issue any ultimatums about a more acceptable standard of play, but she did vow to hold people accountable if the Saints are not able to right their ship in the coming weeks. “Kellen Moore and his coaches are responsible for preparing our players to perform," Benson said. "Mickey Loomis and our football staff are responsible for building a roster capable of sustained success. The players are responsible for their preparation and execution. I am responsible for holding this organization accountable.” Moore is in his second season as the head coach while Loomis has been the General Manager since 2002. The Saints are 7-15 since Moore was hired in 2025 and it sounds like that record will need to get a lot better in order for anyone to feel secure about returning in 2027.

stories.title: Alaric Jackson suspended 2 games for punching Bradley Chubb, per report
stories.summary: Rams offensive lineman Alaric Jackson has been suspended for punching Bradley Chubb, per a new report
stories.detailText: The NFL has suspended Los Angeles Rams offensive lineman Alaric Jackson two games, without pay, for punching Buffalo Bills pass rusher Bradley Chubb following Monday night’s game between the two teams, according to a new report from Aaron Wilson . After a chaotic game saw the Bills defeat the Rams by a final score of 37-34, players from both teams were gathering at midfield for the traditional post-game handshakes and jersey exchanges. Nearby, Buffalo quarterback Josh Allen was conducting an interview. But in the middle of it all a verbal exchange between Jackson and Chubb turned heated, and after Chubb initially walked away from Jackson, the Rams offensive lineman confronted him and then connected with Chubb on a quick right to the jaw that came seemingly out of nowhere. You can see that moment here: Alaric Jackson threw a punch at Bradley Chubb after Bills-Rams. pic.twitter.com/diJunklKBe — ESPN (@espn) October 13, 2026 Jackson had completed the jersey exchange and had a Bills shirt in his hand, as he walked down Chubb and the discussion escalated. After the incident, Chubb told the California Post that he just “chilled” after the punch: “It was a close game. And, you know, they always catch the second guy, so I let him swing and my teammates held me back and I just chilled.” The loss on Monday night dropped the Rams to 2-3 on the season. Los Angeles faces the Arizona Cardinals and the Las Vegas Raiders over the next two weeks of the season. Jackson was suspended for two games by the NFL in 2024 for violating the league’s personal conduct policy, following a lawsuit filed by a woman alleging he recorded her without her consent during a sexual encounter. He was also arrested on suspicion of felony domestic violence in June of 2026 and charged with conduct involving a person who “willfully inflicts physical or corporal injury resulting in a ‘traumatic condition’ on an intimate partner.” Ultimately, criminal charges were not filed and the matter was assigned to a pre-filing diversion program. Jackson was not suspended by the NFL as a result of that decision by the Los Angeles City Attorney’s Office.

stories.title: Steelers Week 5 grades: Offense has most complete performance of the year
stories.summary: Steelers Week 5 grades.
stories.detailText: (Photo by Joe Sargent/Getty Images) | Getty Images Don’t look now, but the Pittsburgh Steelers’ offense is getting hot. They scored a season-high 34 points against the Indianapolis Colts, and are averaging just over 30 points over their last three games. As we do each week, Joey Bray and I will hand out grades for the previous game’s performances, so let’s get into it. QB Aaron Rodgers Jarrett Bailey: Rodgers put up another solid performance against the Colts, finishing the day going 22-of-31 for 235 yards and three touchdowns. This marked his third straight game with three or more touchdown passes, tying a franchise record held by Terry Bradshaw and Ben Roethlisberger. He was decisive, he used the entire field, and he protected the ball – you can’t ask for much more than that. Grade: A- Joey Bray: Rodgers started this game with 11 consecutive completions. This game also marked the first time since December of 2021 that Rodgers has thrown for three or more touchdown passes in three consecutive contests. I was most impressed by how Rodgers moved around the pocket. The Colts’ pass rush is not very good, but Rodgers deserves some credit for the way he was able to maneuver the pocket in this one. You have to be impressed with the way Rodgers performed in this one. Grade: A RB Jaylen Warren Jarrett Bailey: Do you know who leads all running backs with at least 25 touches in total EPA over the last three weeks? Did you guess Jaylen Warren because the heading says Jaylen Warren and this is a Steelers site? Great job, you’re correct. Yes, Warren has been the most efficient running back with the ball in his hands for the last three weeks, and he had another career day against the Colts with 188 yards from scrimmage and two touchdowns. He’s turning into a superstar in real time. Grade: A+ Joey Bray: The Steelers running back is third in the NFL in scrimmage yards at his position, behind only Bijan Robinson and Jahmyr Gibbs. This was the third consecutive game of over 100 scrimmage yards for Warren, who has been the Steelers’ best player this season. As we head into Week 6, Warren is averaging a whopping 5.9 yards per carry, behind only James Cook and Kenneth Walker. Warren’s efficiency this season has simply been out of this world. Grade: A+ Skill group Jarrett Bailey: It wasn’t the best day for DK Metcalf numbers wise (three catches, 12 yards) but he did have a key block on Jaylen Warren’s long touchdown reception. Germie Bernard also stepped in and caught six passes for 80 yards, while Pat Freiermuth added a pair of touchdowns. Overall, a strong day from the other skill players around Warren. Grade: B Joey Bray: Jaylen Warren was the best player on the field yesterday. Pat Freiermuth had a great game in which he scored a pair of touchdowns, moving him into a tie for the most receiving touchdowns by a tight end this season. Those performances alone carry this grade. The receiver room was lackluster, but was without Michael Pittman Jr., as well as Roman Wilson and Ben Skrownek who left with injuries in the first half. Germie Bernard led all receivers in yards and catches. Despite two early drops, the young receiver looked the part in his first real opportunity in the Steelers offense. With how Warren and Freiermuth played, it’s hard to be that upset with the lackluster receiver room. The Bernard performance was also encouraging, which certainly helps their case. Grade: A Offensive line Jarrett Bailey : Aaron Rodgers was the least pressured quarterback in the league in Week 5. After being sacked five times against the Browns, that’s a complete 180 from the unit. Warren’s big day on the ground was also sprung from huge run lanes opened up. Easily the best day the offensive line has had all year, and the best Steelers’ offensive line single week in recent memory. Grade: A+ Joey Bray: This young Steelers offensive line is bound to have some growing pains, as we saw against Cleveland. However, performances like the one they had yesterday against Indianapolis make you confident in the future of their group. Rodgers was only sacked once, and the offensive line gave Rodgers enough time to slowly maneuver through the pocket even when there was pressure. We already discussed just how efficient Warren was with his 6.7 yards per carry in the contest. It was an overall clean game from an offensive line that is starting to trend up. Grade: A+ Secondary Jarrett Bailey: The secondary still has a good bit to clean up. Jaquan Brisker got beat a couple times, and there still appears to be too many miscommunications that lead to chunk plays. That said, Asante Samuel Jr. had a pair of really nice pass breakups to prevent touchdowns, and it was a much better performance than the one we saw in Week 5. Grade: C+ Joey Bray: You know what? The secondary ended up doing better than I thought given how limited they were this week, although I’m not certain how much credit to give them considering Colts Daniel Jones was incredibly inaccurate throwing the ball down the field. Asante Samuel Jr. posted one of the better games of his Steelers career with four passes defended. This group certainly could use a boost, but looked the part against what was an overall mediocre Colts passing attack. Grade: C Run defense Jarrett Bailey: The biggest surprise of the week for me was how good the Steeler’s run defense was without Derrick Harmon. Credit to Yahya Black, Sebastian Joseph-Day, and Gabriel Rubio for stepping up in their increased roles on Sunday, as well as Cam Heyward and Keeanu Benton, of course. Jonathan Taylor totaled just 45 yards – that’s a good day at the office. Grade: A Joey Bray: No Derrick Harmon? No problem. The Steelers seem to have Jonathan Taylor’s number. The star running back amassed just 45 yards on the ground with his 15 carries. The Colts only rushed for 66 yards as a team. After giving up several rushes of over 20 yards last week against Cleveland, this was a resounding response from the run defense. Grade: A+ Let us know what you think in the comments . Be sure to bookmark Behind the Steel Curtain for all the latest news, breakdowns, and more! Steelers Week 6 power rankings roundup: Is Pittsburgh gaining respect? stories.title: Browns place Raheim Sanders on IR, sign Audric Estime off Vikings practice squad
stories.summary: The Browns have made a couple of moves at running back and on the practice squad.
stories.detailText: The Browns have made a couple of moves at running back and on the practice squad. Cleveland announced the club has placed running back Raheim Sanders (hip) on injured reserve. As a corresponding move, the club has signed running back Audric Estime to the 53-man roster off of Minnesota’s practice squad. Sanders was injured in Sunday’s loss to the Jets. He served as the primary kick returner for Cleveland, averaging 29.3 yards per return. Estime appeared in seven games with one start for New Orleans last year, rushing for 198 yards with a touchdown. He caught 12 passes for 103 yards. He previously appeared in 13 games for Denver in 2024. Additionally, Cleveland signed tight end Devin Culp and guard Vershon Lee to the practice squad and released cornerback Myles Bryant and receiver James Proche II from the practice squad.

stories.title: Bears' Montez Sweat suspended two games for violating NFL PED policy
stories.summary: The Bears will be without Montez Sweat for the next two games after the defender was suspended. Here's what to know.
stories.detailText: Chicago Bears defensive end Montez Sweat has been suspended two games for violating the NFL's performance-enhancing substance policy, according to multiple reports. The 30-year-old will now miss the Bears' Week 6 contest against the Atlanta Falcons and the Week 7 matchup with the New England Patriots on "Thursday Night Football." He will be eligible to return in Week 8 when the Bears visit the Seattle Seahawks on "Monday Night Football" in Week 8. Sweat is in the penultimate year of a four-year, $98 million extension he signed with Chicago after the team acquired him from the Washington Commanders in 2023. The Bears traded a second-round pick in the 2024 NFL Draft to acquire Sweat in the midst of a career year that resulted in a Pro Bowl selection. He has two sacks in five games for the Bears this year, along with seven total tackles and four quarterback hits. In 2025, Sweat notched 10 sacks, 53 tackles and 18 quarterback hits in 17 games. This article originally appeared on USA TODAY: Bears' Montez Sweat suspended two games for violating NFL PED policy

stories.title: Rams vs. Bills snap counts: Tutu Atwell takes over WR3 role
stories.summary: Do the Rams finally have a plan for Tutu Atwell?
stories.detailText: Tutu Atwell played 32 snaps against the Buffalo Bills on Monday, the most he’s had in a game since Week 5 of last season and a clear indication of who Sean McVay likes the most right now as the Rams’ third receiver. Atwell was only targeted one time and caught a pass for four yards, but obviously McVay thinks L.A. has a chance to do some things differently with him in the lineup instead of Jordan Whittington or Konata Mumpfield. Those two receivers played a combined 17 snaps. And it was explosive plays that mattered. Rams-Bills explosive plays After another of what seems like countless special teams gaffes, the Los Angeles Rams let the Buffalo Bills gallop right past them for a 37-34 win on Monday Night Football at L.A.’s SoFi Stadium. The game proved to be an advertisement for today’s NFL, how explosive plays can either set or change the tone of the outcome. Although the Rams used a grinding offensive attack to methodically move down the field, accumulating 78 offensive plays and 33 first downs, they had only five explosives. They all came on pass plays, all in the the last half and overtime. Overall in 2026, L.A. sits 17th in explosive offensive plays. Conversely, the Bills played to form, 1st in NFL Explosive Play Rate. They had 10 offensive explosives on 57 offensive plays, mixed evenly between run and pass with an 11th coming in the return game. Th Bills didn’t drop any bombs on the L.A. defense, their big plays arose from identifying lanes and and open field running. Whether it’s patient quarterbacks when the Rams pass rush doesn’t get home or backs/receivers that get the ball in space, all can apply pressure to the limited athleticism of L.A.’s linebacker and safety units. The Rams defense is 25th in explosives allowed. Offensive and defensive explosive play rates: The Bills offense is very good pic.twitter.com/Dr7YFUrYSn — Sam Hoppen (@SamHoppen) October 13, 2026 Here the snap count review from Sunday, players their snap counts and percentage of play time in bold. Quarterback Matthew Stafford (82, 100%) Played well enough for the Rams to win, too bad the outcome wasn’t put in his hands completely on the overtime drive. Staff had been lights out in the fourth quarter, 11 of 13 for 119 yards, as the Rams posted 20 points. Last week vs. Philly, it was 13 of 17 for 149 yards and two scores. Running back Kyren Williams (60, 70%) The Rams offensive braintrust decided again, that 50+ passes was the path to victory, so Williams never got into a groove as a run threat. He was pointed out for a couple on nice pass blocking reps and made an amazing catch late. On the Rams final scoring drive with 30 seconds left in the game, L.A. had third and seven from the buffalo 10. Stafford threw behind Williams, who had circled out of the backfield and the running back reached a hand back and snatched it in. Blake Corum (22, 27%) Actually did some damage as a receiver, hauled in three of four targets and had very nice 34-yard catch and run at the end of third quarter that led to a score in the fourth. On the Rams first drive coming out of the half, he was wide open in the flat with an open field to the end zone, but Staff, under pressure, overthrew him. Wide receiver Puka Nacua (70, 85%) Hard to predict how bad this offense would be, if Nacua went out for a long term. His physicality at the catch point and ability to plow forward with yards after the catch is quite amazing. Week in, week out, just a stud. Davante Adams (60, 70%) This strikes me as the exact role that you can envision the older version of Adams in, as a complimentary WR#2. Adams route-running savvy is still top notch and can create separation, particularly near the goal line. There are times though, that he can mail it in running routes when not the primary target. Tutu Atwell (32, 39%) Second highest snap count going back to October of 2024. It’s not just fans, even the national broadcasters spoke of the need to get Atwell’s speed into the game and cited McVay as saying he wanted him as a bigger part of the offensive plan. He caught a single short out and ran a lot deep clear out routes, but was never targeted deep. Jordan Whittington (11, 13%) Basically invisible, subbing in for Atwell in running situations. Did tote five kickoffs for an average of just under 28 yards per, over the Rams season average of 25. Konata Mumpfield (6, 7%) Came into the game nicked up and was in and out, likely the same shoulder problem.. I guess the Rams figured that an injured Mumpfield was a better fit into the game plan than rookie CJ Daniels. Tight end Tyler Higbee (55, 67%) Sipping from the Fountain of Youth, Higbee’s playing his best football in years. The Rams are lining him up in the slot or outside at 44 percent clip and he’s responded with a catch rate of 80 percent, 14 of 20 receptions for first down and the highest depth of target for his whole career. Colby Parkinson (53, 65%) Obviously gutting through his injury, just two short targets in a Rams game plan where the passing offense was all underneath. Is going with a player of Parkinson’s talent level and limited by injuries, a better choice than giving your Round 2 draft pick some needed time on the field? This is one of the questions that needs to be asked when you start 2-3. Davis Allen (41, 50%) Made two outstanding clutch catches to go along with his usual blocking duties. Offensive line Alaric Jackson, Steve Avila, Coleman Shelton, Kevin Dotson, Warren McClendon (82, 100%) The run game was primarily between the tackles. Even though it wasn’t particularly effective, the big guys have generally done well run blocking, allowing the least amount of stuff/loss plays (34.8%) in the league. Throwing 50+ passes is exorbitant even for the pass-happy Rams, the line was pretty good pass blocking against an aggressive Buffalo blitz program, only allowing a 22 percent pressure rate. Next Gen Stats recorded the Rams with 4 of 12 passes completed under pressure. Special teams Sniff, sniff. That’s the tell tale odor of a dead animal in the wood pile. Placekicker Harrison Meevis is the first to go, but the smell lingers. Now, more importantly, what’s the plan to clean up the rest? same last year, i think, https://t.co/oPNL9lUpcH — Jim Youngblood 53 (@53_jim70721) October 13, 2026 Defensive line Kobie Turner (43, 67%) Aaron Donald (43, 67%) Braden Fiske (26, 41%) Poona Ford (29, 45%) Tyler Davis (21, 33%) Ty Hamilton (7, 11%) Not the best showing for this unit, Buffalo also uses a lot of three tight end formations and came in to run the football. They did, to the tune of 234 yards. The Bills never went away from what worked, even into overtime. Against a running QB, lane discipline is paramount and too often the Rams interior left huge gaps for Josh Allen to traverse. Edge Byron Young (55, 86%) Josaiah Stewart (53, 83%) Wesley Bailey (16, 25%) Desjuan Johnson (4, 6%) Quiet getting after the passer. For the game, Bills’ QB Josh Allen had nearly three seconds in time to pressure percentage on passes, even though he couldn’t get deep and had to take the underneath stuff. Stewart seemed to get locked up regularly by the opposing tackle and lost contain. Young was close to making a couple more sacks with backside pursuit, but couldn’t close the deal. Off-ball linebacker Nate Landman (57, 89%) Good on him to know that Bills RB James Cook has been a fumbler ( most in the NFL from last year on), the punch outs were big time plays. Landman has an old school, tough guy game between the tackles. However in space, he lacks move skills and is exploitable. In over his head in pursuit of more agile offensive players and certainly to spy active quarterbacks. Omar Speights (23, 36%) Trending down. Although his play time was up a few from last week, his total was the second lowest since early in his rookie year. 1st play of the game. He was hunting… https://t.co/YJXqUufd19 pic.twitter.com/HqYvgOOEqe — Cody Alexander (@The_Coach_A) October 13, 2026 Safety Quentin Lake (64, 100%) Kamren Curl (64, 100%) Kamren Kinchens (36, 56%) Jaylen McCollough (1, 2%) It’s easy to Monday morning quarterback, but Lake reportedly wasn’t able to practice all week with a bad hip and was a game day decision. I realize he’s a team leader and the Rams depth is thin, but you start and give every snap to a player not known for his athleticism and has a hip impairment against a team with high-end explosive play strength? He didn’t play up to par and was exploited. Curl had a nice tackle for loss, as did Kinchens. McCollough is still trending downwards. Cornerback Trent McDuffie (64, 100%) Jaylen Watson (64, 100%) Josh Wallace (34, 53%) What on earth was Watson thinking when he made that interception? Poor situational awareness to dance around like that, looked like he was trying to burn clock rather than find running lanes. At the first glance it didn’t mean much, but it did cost the Rams offense another two or three plays and an opportunity to put points on the board right before the half. L.A. has moved to more man (27.4%) as their primary coverage. On Monday night, coverage was pretty darn good, Bills QB Allen had to scramble on nearly 30 percent of his drop backs. The negative side to that was Allen had 107 yards rushing on those scrambles. Some of the penalties were a bit ticky-tack, but in today’s NFL there should be weekly reports on the tendencies of officiating crews and you have to adjust. It’s tougher sledding when playing a lot of man-type coverages. Every team's man/zone coverage split: pic.twitter.com/2BWEdrsZ5z — SūmerSports (@SumerSports) October 13, 2026 Moving on Another defeat snatched from the jaws of victory. The big story that seems to be expanding exponentially is of course, special teams. It lays at the feet of Rams head coach Sean McVay, his decisions and arrogance about the importance of them have come home to roost. Since 2021, McVay has a special teams -70.87 EPA (Expected Points Added) metric, worst in the NFL. It was -13.1 against Buffalo. As tough as the loss is to swallow, the Rams go on five-game run of lower rung teams, the easiest schedule in the NFL over that stretch from Week 6 to 11. Arizona Cardinals (twice) , Las Vegas Raiders, LA Chargers, and Washington Commanders. Winning out could reset the season at the bye week and get the team straightened out for the league’s hardest schedule down the stretch run. Today, Defensive-adjusted Value Over Average (DVOA) still gives the Rams a 58.2% likelihood of earning a wildcard berth in the playoffs. The fat lady is not singing, but fans sure do want her watching the Rams special teams.

stories.title: Dolphins claim WR Jared Wayne off of waivers
stories.summary: The Dolphins are making a change at wide receiver during their bye week.
stories.detailText: The Dolphins are making a change at wide receiver during their bye week. They announced that they have claimed Jared Wayne off of waivers from the Texans. Ryan Miller was waived to create room for Wayne on the roster in Miami. Wayne played in all five Texans games this season, but was the odd man out after the team acquired Marvin Harrison Jr. in a trade with the Cardinals. He had four catches for 65 yards and also saw time on special teams while with Houston. Wayne played in four games for the Texans over the previous two seasons. He had two catches for 20 yards in those contests. The Dolphins also announced that they have signed defensive lineman Jordan Jefferson to the practice squad and that they have released defensive lineman Mazi Smith in a corresponding move.

stories.title: Patriots sign running back Hassan Haskins, cornerback D’Shawn Jamison to practice squad
stories.summary: Outside linebacker Jose Ramirez was released in a corresponding move.
stories.detailText: CLEVELAND, OHIO - AUGUST 27: Hassan Haskins #26 of the New England Patriots returns a kickoff during the second quarter of a preseason game against the Cleveland Browns at Huntington Bank Field on August 27, 2026 in Cleveland, Ohio. (Photo by Nick Cammett/Diamond Images via Getty Images) | Diamond Images/Getty Images With TreVeyon Henderson expected to miss multiple weeks due to a high ankle sprain, a familiar face has returned to the ground game in Foxborough. The New England Patriots announced the addition of running back Hassan Haskins to the practice squad on Tuesday along with cornerback D’Shawn Jamison. Haskins, 26, had worked out and signed at Gillette Stadium ahead of the 2026 preseason opener. The 6-foot-2, 228-pound running back went on to be released as a vested veteran at the NFL’s 53-man roster deadline. He spent two weeks on the practice squad in September and has remained a free agent since then. Originally entering the NFL in the fourth round of the 2022 draft at No. 131 overall, Haskins made previous stops with the Tennessee Titans and Los Angeles Chargers. Through 44 career games, the former first-team All-Big Ten selection via the Michigan Wolverines stands with 76 carries for 229 yards, 18 catches for 119 yards, three touchdowns and one start. He has handled 371 snaps on offense, 683 snaps on special teams and now checks in as the fourth healthy back in the fold behind starter Rhamondre Stevenson, trade acquisition Corey Kiner and scout-teamer Lan Larison. Jamison, 27, joins Al’zillion Hamilton as the second cornerback on New England’s practice squad midway through October after the promotion of veteran Kindle Vildor. The 5-foot-9, 185-pound Texas Longhorns product went undrafted in 2023 and made his initial NFL tours with the San Francisco 49ers, Carolina Panthers and Pittsburgh Steelers. He spent the first month of the 2026 campaign on the practice squad of the Arizona Cardinals. Notching 10 tackles and one pass deflection, Jamison has appeared in 18 games while seeing 107 snaps on defense and 166 snaps on special teams. The corner’s career includes one start as well as three kickoff returns. The Patriots released outside linebacker Jose Ramirez to make room among the 17-man group. Ramirez, 27, had re-signed to New England’s practice squad last week after going through the wire unclaimed. The 6-foot-2, 252-pound edge rusher first arrived as the calendar turned to September and was called up to the 53-man roster three weeks later. In two games, he recorded one solo tackle across 30 snaps between defense and special teams before being waived . Entering the NFL in the sixth round of the 2023 draft at No. 196 overall, Ramirez made four appearances while a member of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. The former MAC Defensive Player of the Year out of Arizona, Riverside City College and Eastern Michigan spent last year with the CFL’s Hamilton Tiger-Cats on the way to reaching a futures agreement with the Philadelphia Eagles. Head coach Mike Vrabel’s 3-2 club moves forward with an open spot on the active roster and a full practice squad. The New York Jets visit Gillette Stadium on Sunday. The AFC East kickoff is set for 1 p.m. ET.

stories.title: Montez Sweat suspended 2 games
stories.summary: The Bears’ defense continues to suffer more bad news, this time losing one of their veteran defenders.
stories.detailText: The Chicago Bears suffered an additional setback to their 2026 season on October 13th when Pro Bowl defensive end Montez Sweat was suspended without pay for two games, per Ian Rapoport and others. #Bears edge Montez Sweat has been suspended for the club’s next two games without pay for violating the NFL’s Performance-Enhancing Substances Policy, per The NFL. pic.twitter.com/SQKCJDiMUN — Ian Rapoport (@RapSheet) October 13, 2026 Sweat is currently third on the team for pressures and sacks and fourth for tackles for a loss. He should be eligible to return on Friday, October 23rd—almost three years after the Bears traded for him. This means he will miss the matchups against the Atlanta Falcons (2-3) and the New England Patriots (3-2). The news comes after Sweat’s fellow defensive end Dayo Odeyingbo left the field during the defeat against the Packers with a quadriceps injury. Meanwhile, 2025 second-round draft pick Shemar Turner will be activated off the physically unable to perform list today to take Sweat’s spot on the 53-man roster. That leaves only nickleback Kyler Gordon still on the PUP and in his 21-day practice window.

stories.title: Chicago Bears Rome Odunze needs to be better, but the drop narrative is unfair
stories.summary: Another Sunday and another “drop” by Rome Odunze, or so fans say. A closer look at the Bears' third-year receiver here:
stories.detailText: GREEN BAY, WISCONSIN - OCTOBER 11: Rome Odunze #15 of the Chicago Bears leaves the field after a loss against the Green Bay Packers at Lambeau Field on October 11, 2026 in Green Bay, Wisconsin. (Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images) | Getty Images Let’s get this out of the way — Rome Odunze has not yet played like the #9 overall pick. He has played like a solid WR, but when you draft a WR in the top 10, you rightfully should expect him to become a top of the league player. Still, I think Rome is getting a bad deal by Chicago Bears fans. Sure, Rome has had some bad drops throughout his career, as well as contested catches that he should have come down with. However, I think that the narrative is clouding our judgement, and the “drops” decried by fans have not always been fairly characterized. Let’s acknowledge some of the egregious drops, as there have been a few. The first, and arguably worst was this drop against the Rams with a chance to go to the NFC Championship on the line. While the ball was thrown behind Rome, he needs to snatch this pass rather than let it travel to his body: There’ve been a lot of really bad Rome Odunze drops during his time with the Bears. The one right on his hands in the endzone against the Eagles is the freshest. This one against the Rams was the most costly. I don’t blame Ben Johnson for losing patience. pic.twitter.com/qnByY9eelK — All Things Chicago Sports (@things_sox) October 1, 2026 Another happened during the Week 3 game against the Philadelphia Eagles, where Odunze lost concentration in the end zone before he could secure the ball: Rome Odunze Was Wide Open, And He Drops It. Case Keenum Did Everything He Freaking Could On That Play, And It Should Have Been A Touchdown. 😭 pic.twitter.com/yF7cVX1a30 — SM Highlights (@SMHighlights1) September 29, 2026 There have been a few other legitimate dropped passes to gripe about, including one against the Patriots his rookie year that slipped straight through his hands on a comeback route. But I am here to say: step out of the echo chamber and into reality. Rome needs to be better, yes, but the narrative around his drops is getting out of hand. This was no more clear than on Sunday when Tyson Bagent airmailed a pass to Rome, where he remarkably got two hands on the ball, just for the CB covering him to get his hands in to break it up (please ignore this Twitter user’s silly analysis): 9th overall pick rome odunze is a B U S T #dabears this is a B U M on your screen pic.twitter.com/3zZrzaE3kP — James (@DaaaSweener) October 11, 2026 Calling this anything more than a highly difficult play broken up by a great defensive effort is just parroting a narrative. There are several other instances where the narrative parrots a drop after Odunze doesn’t secure a diving sideline catch 6” off the ground. And it’s not just that the drop narrative has gotten out of hand; it’s that we seem to forget that he has made contested catches throughout his career. Here are some of my favorites: HIGHLIGHT REEL CATCH FROM ROME ODUNZE pic.twitter.com/HLAoyk82WI — Harrison Graham (@HGrahamNFL) September 13, 2026 Here’s the tight copy on Caleb Williams’ 4th down throw to Rome Odunze. It’s a middle of the field Hi-Lo concept — that stretches to the boundary. pic.twitter.com/q0wuPfIJ8A — Matt Bowen (@MattBowen41) January 11, 2026 3. Bears Vs. Commanders Rome Odunze TD wiped by an illegal motion flag. Even the announcers said there was NOTHING there. Took 7 off the board for no reason. pic.twitter.com/7BHUe17sma — Bears Facts (@DaBearsTakeOver) April 14, 2026 Some Caleb Williams to Rome Odunze highlights for your enjoyment on this Thanksgiving morning pic.twitter.com/T5gfd5hAju — Bearsszn (@bearszn) November 28, 2024 Coming into the league, Rome’s identity was a contested catch specialist who might not be able to separate enough at the next level. While Rome needs to find consistency in contested catches, he continues to be one of the best in the league at creating separation: WR Separation Score vs TPRR 📊 — Carnell Tate building chemistry with Ward — Downs, Doubs, Odunze, Pickens prime targets for positive regression — MHJ in a league of his own pic.twitter.com/kDtxG8H22T — JClyde (@JClyyde) October 8, 2026 This chart shows that Rome Odunze is consistently getting open, at a similar rate to Drake London, Garrett Wilson, and Romeo Doubs, but isn’t seeing the same target share as others. Through five games, Rome has 17 receptions for 273 yards, giving him pace for 58 receptions and 928 yards. While these aren’t #9 overall pick numbers, they are far from unproductive. I am still confident that Rome can turn into an even better pro with time. Mind you that he has only played with Caleb Williams four times since Week 13 of last season, while two of those came after a return from injury for Odunze. Let’s practice patience and give him time and consistency with Caleb to figure it out.

stories.title: Detroit Lions WR Jameson Williams gets celebration fine rescinded
stories.summary: Detroit Lions WR Jameson Williams had his fines rescinded after a celebration crack down in Week 2.
stories.detailText: ORCHARD PARK, NEW YORK - SEPTEMBER 17: Jameson Williams #1 of the Detroit Lions looks on prior to the game against the Buffalo Bills at Highmark Stadium on September 17, 2026 in Orchard Park, New York. (Photo by Bryan M. Bennett/Getty Images) | Getty Images A few weeks ago, the Detroit Lions were hammered by the NFL with a load of fines for celebrations. In their Week 2 loss to the Buffalo Bills, several Lions players mimicked a smoking motion—resulting in the following fines: Amon-Ra St. Brown: $14,926 — Illegal celebration and vulgar acts Amon-Ra St. Brown: $14,926 — Illegal celebration and vulgar acts Amon-Ra St. Brown: $14,926 — Illegal celebration and vulgar acts Amon-Ra St. Brown: $14,926 — Illegal celebration and vulgar acts Penei Sewell: $14,926 — Illegal celebration and vulgar acts Jahmyr Gibbs: $14,926 — Illegal celebartion and vulgar acts Jameson Williams: $14,926 — Illegal celebration and vulgar acts Jameson Williams: $11,941 — Taunting On Tuesday, it was revealed that Williams appealed his two fines and won both of those appeals. According to Ian Rapoport, Williams argued that marijuana was legal in several states and therefore not an obscene gesture. As for the taunting penalty, the brief gesture he made, Williams argued, was not offensive. At this point, it isn’t clear if any of the other Lions players won their appeals, but St. Brown told reporters the in Week 3 that he was planning on appealing with the league. Appeals officer—and Hall of Fame linebacker—Derrick Brooks offered the following response to Williams’ appeal. “Although I rescinded this fine, please make every effort to celebrate with your teammates in the best professional manner possible.” This offseason, the NFL attempted to cut down on celebrations that referenced drugs or alcohol. In the same week the Lions got hit, players like 49ers fullback Kyle Juszczyk and Cowboys tight end Jake Ferguson were fined for their “chugging” celebrations. Since then, both of their fines have also been rescinded.

stories.title: Dolphins add Brady Cook to practice squad in bye week move
stories.summary: The Dolphins bring back quarterback Brady Cook.
stories.detailText: MIAMI GARDENS, FLORIDA - SEPTEMBER 27: Brady Cook #15 of the Miami Dolphins exits the field after warmups prior to an NFL football game against the Kansas City Chiefs at Hard Rock Stadium on September 27, 2026 in Miami Gardens, Florida. (Photo by Perry Knotts/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Miami Dolphins have signed quarterback Brady Cook to their practice squad, days after releasing their third-string passer from the active roster. The move comes following the team’s loss to the Cincinnati Bengals, dropping them to 0-5 on the year. The Dolphins released Cook from their 53-man roster on Saturday to make space for defensive tackle Kenneth Grant, who was activated off the injured reserve list. To make space on the practice squad for Cook, the Dolphins released running back Jarquez Hunter. The Dolphins traded for Hunter this summer, sending the Los Angeles Rams wide receiver Tutu Atwell in compensation. Hunter landed on the practice squad after the preseason and never made an appearance with Miami. A 2025 undrafted free agent out of Missouri, Cook spent his rookie season with the New York Jets. He appeared in five games, starting four of them, and threw for 739 yards on a 57.5 completion rate. He had two touchdown passes and seven passes intercepted. He recorded a 55.4 passer rating. Cook was cut by the Jets as part of the team’s roster cuts at the end of the preseason this year. He has not made an appearance since signing with the Dolphins. Miami’s quarterback room includes starter Malik Willis and backup Kyle McCord. Cook slides back in as the team’s third option at the position.

stories.title: Bears’ Montez Sweat suspended 2 games for PED violation
stories.summary: The Bears’ highest paid defensive player just failed a PED test.
stories.detailText: (Photo by David Jensen/Getty Images) | Getty Images Montez Sweat has had a rough year for an overachieving Chicago Bears defense to start the 2026 season. Sweat is expected to be the team’s best passer rusher an overall anchor on the defensive line, but he only has two solo tackles all year. Now Chicago is going to be without Sweat for the next two games after he failed a test for Performance Enhancing Drugs. The NFL suspended Sweat for two games on Tuesday for violating the league’s PED agreement, according to Chicago Tribune reporter Brad Biggs . That means the Bears will be without him for their Week 6 matchup with the Atlanta Falcons and their Week 7 Thursday Night Football showdown with the New England Patriots. Sweat has two sacks on the year for the Bears, and he’s been credited with seven total tackles and two solo tackles thus far. Sweat has the biggest cap hit on the Bears’ defense at more than $25 million this season. He recorded 10 sacks last year as Chicago reached the NFC Divisional Round of the playoffs. Will Caleb Williams be back before Sweat? The QB was questionable last week as he recovers from a hamstring strain . We’ll update this story as it develops.

stories.title: Jaguars put Anton Harrison on injured reserve
stories.summary: A report on Tuesday morning said Jaguars left tackle Anton Harrison is headed for arthroscopic knee surgery and that his timeline for return won't be known until the operation takes place.
stories.detailText: A report on Tuesday morning said Jaguars left tackle Anton Harrison is headed for arthroscopic knee surgery and that his timeline for return won't be known until the operation takes place. The Jaguars revealed on Tuesday afternoon he'll be out at least four games regardless of what's determined during surgery. Harrison was placed on injured reserve and that could be where he spends the rest of the season. Per Tuesday's report, one of the potential outcomes is that Harrison misses the rest of the season. Walker Little is set to replace Harrison against the Texans in London this week. The Jaguars have a bye in Week 7 and then face the Colts, Ravens and Titans. Jacksonville filled Harrison's roster spot with the previously reported signing safety Kaevon Merriweather off of their practice squad. They also announced that they have signed long snapper Jacob Bobenmoyer to the practice squad. Ross Matiscik was forced out of last Sunday's game with a shoulder injury and defensive tackle DaVon Hamilton was pressed into service in that role.

stories.title: Eagles pass rusher Jalyx Hunt (leg) unlikely vs. Panthers
stories.summary: Eagles pass rusher Jalyx Hunt, who sustained ankle and knee injuries last week, is not expected to play Sunday against the Carolina Panthers, DC Vic Fangio said.
stories.detailText: PHILADELPHIA -- It would be "pretty miraculous" for Eagles edge rusher Jalyx Hunt to play Sunday against the Carolina Panthers , defensive coordinator Vic Fangio said. Hunt sustained ankle and knee injuries on the final play of the first half against the Jacksonville Jaguars last week. His left leg got pinned under him and twisted awkwardly as he attempted to recover a loose ball following a fourth-down stop from teammate Zack Baun . Hunt stayed on the ground for some time before exiting with the assistance of trainers. "He's the kind of guy, he's going to be pushing the envelope and making the medical people clear him," Fangio said. "He's not going to be one of those guys that's going to be hesitant to come back." Fellow edge rusher Jonathan Greenard was not able to suit up against the Jaguars after testing his injured ankle pregame. Fangio said "hopefully he'll be able to go this week" when asked about Greenard's status for the Panthers game. The Eagles could be getting reinforcements on offense with receiver DeVonta Smith and running back Saquon Barkley on the mend from hamstring injuries. "I'm hopeful," coach Nick Sirianni said Monday. "I just think it's hard to tell you one thing and then it plays out differently because there's still a lot of time left for this game. But I'm hopeful that these -- I know how hard these guys work to get themselves back because it's killing them that they're not out there." The running back room in particular could use a boost with Tank Bigsby (abdomen) on injured reserve and Will Shipley expected to miss multiple weeks after suffering a partial plantar fascia tear during the Jaguars game, according to ESPN's Adam Schefter. The safety position is another to keep an eye on. Marcus Epps missed the Jacksonville game with a groin injury, and Michael Carter II exited Sunday with an abdominal injury and did not return.

stories.title: Bears' Montez Sweat suspended two games for performance-enhancing substance violation
stories.summary: The Bears will be without starting defensive end Montez Sweat for the next two games.
stories.detailText: The Bears will be without starting defensive end Montez Sweat for the next two games. The NFL announced today that Sweat is suspended without pay for two games for violating the NFL policy on performance-enhancing substances. Although the NFL does not disclose the specific reason when a player is suspended for a violation, a two-game suspension is typically the penalty for a first offense of a player testing positive for a stimulant, diuretic or masking agent. Players who test positive for anabolic steroids are typically suspended at least six games. Sweat will miss Sunday's game against the Falcons and the following Thursday night game against the Patriots. He will then be eligible to return Week 8 against the Seahawks on Monday Night Football. The 30-year-old Sweat, who arrived in a Chicago via trade from Washington during the 2023 season, has started all five games and played 69 percent of the Bears' defensive snaps this season. He has two sacks.

stories.title: Bills waive DB Anthony Kendall, plan to bring him back on practice squad
stories.summary: The Bills are making a change to their 53-man roster.
stories.detailText: The Bills are making a change to their 53-man roster. Buffalo is waiving defensive back Anthony Kendall, NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reports. The team intends to bring him back on the practice squad should he clear waivers. Kendall, 26, had not played in a game since 2023 before he appeared in last night’s victory over the Rams. He was on the field for 31 defensive snaps and 15 special teams snaps in the contest. Kendall has also spent time with the Titans, Ravens, and Browns in his career.

stories.title: Patriots Power Rankings, Week 6: Pats back in Top Ten!
stories.summary: Check out where the experts ranked the Patriots heading into Week 6
stories.detailText: Oct 11, 2026; Foxborough, Massachusetts, USA; New England Patriots fans pose for a photo during the second half in a game against the Las Vegas Raiders at Gillette Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Bob DeChiara-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect With two Yuge wins, the Patriots are officially on an upward streak. The experts have noticed. Nick Shook from NFL.com ridiculously had the Pats ranked 31st two weeks ago ahead of the Bills game, but has since acknowledged the Pats rising from the ashes. The rest of the other experts have as well. Nice to see New England back in the top 10 where it feels they belong. Coming to town this coming Sunday are the 2-3 New York Jets. Pats fans may take them lightly, but the organization can’t afford to. A loss puts both teams at 3-3, with the Jets moving to second place in the AFC East. No one wants that. Everyone knows how much extra weight division and conference games carry in the standings, precisely why this matchup matters. The Pats are operating on an over-stuffed injury report and depleted roster. Mike Vrabel, Josh McDaniels and Zak Kuhr made it work effectively last week. Wednesday the initial Week 6 injury report comes out, giving us a better idea of which players are available but I think the coaching staff can keep it duct-taped together for another week. Pats head into the new week favored by 7.5. Geno Smith has thrown zero interceptions so far this season, but I believe New England’s defense will find a way to disrupt his passing game. I see the Patriots winning and padding their divisional lead over New York. GO PATS!! AFC East: Buffalo Bills (4-1) at Las Vegas Raiders (3-2) New England Patriots (3-2) vs. New York Jets (2-3) Miami Dolphins (0-5) – Bye Week AFC Matchups: Kansas City Chiefs (4-0) vs. Los Angeles Chargers (0-5) Baltimore Ravens (4-1) at Cleveland Browns (3-2) Jacksonville Jaguars (4-1) vs. Houston Texans (1-4) Denver Broncos (3-2) vs. Seattle Seahawks (3-2) Pittsburgh Steelers (3-2) at Tampa Bay Buccaneers (1-4) Cincinnati Bengals (3-2) -Bye Week Indianapolis Colts (2-3) vs. Tennessee Titans (0-5) 6th – Nate Davis (USA Today): QB Drake Maye has seemingly captured his MVP-caliber form the past two weeks after a very rough September. Might he even go to another level given WR A.J. Brown could be back as soon as Sunday against the Jets? [+1] 7th – Vinnie Iyer (Sporting News): Drake Maye’s first three games: average of 195 passing yards per game, 1 touchdown to six interceptions, 72 total rushing yards. Maye’s past two games: average of 322 passing yards per game, 7 TDs to 1 INT, 79 total rushing yards. What’s the difference? Might just be playing easier pass defenses of Buffalo and Las Vegas . [+2] 7th – Ian Glendon (Full Press Coverage): The Patriots have completely changed their season in two weeks. Beating Buffalo was the attention-grabber, but crushing Las Vegas 45-17 was the confirmation. Drake Maye and the offense looked explosive, and New England suddenly has a real argument as one of the AFC’s most dangerous teams. The Jacksonville loss still exists, but it feels a lot farther away now . [+2] 9th – NFL Nation (ESPN): Biggest issue on defense: Cornerback depth. They played with only three healthy CBs on Sunday, as starters Christian Gonzalez (shoulder) and Carlton Davis III (neck) were inactive, and rookie backups Karon Prunty and Channing Canada were unavailable because of hamstring injuries. When fill-in starter Charles Woods left the game in the second half because of a shoulder injury, it further thinned a perilous CB situation, leaving just Marcus Jones and Kindle Vildor as available options. New England has allowed a 66% completion percentage this season, which ranks 25th in the NFL. — Mike Reiss [+5] 9th – Mike Florio (ProFootballTalk): The patriotic pigeons had a field day on Tom Brady’s statue . [+4] 10th – Conor Orr (SI): I don’t really care whether it was a designed play or not, but Efton Chism’s in-game backwards pass, which followed an unbelievable end zone grab the week prior against the Bills, ensures that the story of the NFL in 2026 cannot be written without Josh McDaniels and a white Patriots wide receiver shorter than six feet tall. Time is truly a flat circle . [+2] 10th – Nick Shook (NFL): It took one wild win over the Bills to return the Patriots to excellence. They detonated the Raiders on Sunday, with fantastic offensive performances by Drake Maye, Efton Chism III, Kyle Williams, DeMario Douglas — heck, just throw in every skill-position player. They all feasted in a game that saw New England finish with 536 yards of offense, pairing perfectly with a defense that put the clamps on Las Vegas early . [+8] 11th – Pete Prisco (CBS Sports): Drake Maye has righted things in a big way. He’s been on fire the past two weeks as the Pats have turned their season around . [+4] 11th – Frank Schwab (Yahoo! Sports): Drake Maye isn’t a bad QB. Go figure. After naysayers got their licks in during Maye’s three-game slump to start the season, which was an extension of his postseason issues, Maye has 643 passing yards, seven passing touchdowns, 79 rushing yards and a rushing score in his last two games. Those games came against the Bills and Raiders, who had one combined loss before facing New England. Stunning, but a 24-year-old QB who was one vote from winning MVP last season might still be good . [+2] 13th – Ralph Vacchiano (FOX Sports): The Patriots are such a different team when Drake Maye is playing like Drake Maye. In the first three games of the season, Maye threw just one touchdown pass with six interceptions and averaged 195 passing yards per contest. But in the last two games — both wins — he’s had seven touchdown passes, one interception with an impressive 321.5 passing yards per game. And with him rolling, their running game was suddenly working, too. It’s no wonder that they made quick work of the upstart Raiders. And with the Jets and Dolphins coming up in their next three games, they’ve got a shot to get on a little bit of a roll now, too. Stat To Know : The Patriots averaged 12 points per game in Weeks 1-3, ranking 31st in the NFL. In Weeks 4-5, they averaged a league-best 37 points per game . [+2] AVG RANK: 9.3 [+3.6]

stories.title: Ravens release WR Chris Moore
stories.summary: The Ravens made a change at wide receiver on Tuesday.
stories.detailText: The Ravens made a change at wide receiver on Tuesday. They announced that they have released Chris Moore from their 53-man roster. There was no corresponding move, but the Ravens could get rookie wideout Ja'Kobi Lane back from injured reserve this week. Lane injured his wrist in Week 1, so he became eligible to return after Sunday's game and head coach Jesse Minter said he could play against the Browns in Week 6. Moore had three catches for 63 yards and a touchdown in four appearances this season. He was on the practice squad to open the season and could be headed back there if he remains in the team's plans.

stories.title: NFL suspends Bears DE Montez Sweat 2 games for violating the league's PED policy
stories.summary: The Bears have upcoming games against the Atlanta Falcons and New England Patriots in Weeks 6 and 7.
stories.detailText: The NFL has suspended Chicago Bears defensive end Montez Sweat two games for violating the league's policy on performance-enhancing drugs. The league announced the suspension on Tuesday. It did not provide details on what Sweat allegedly did to violate the policy. The Bears have upcoming games against the Atlanta Falcons and New England Patriots in Weeks 6 and 7. Sweat is a former Pro Bowler who's in his fourth season with the Bears since joining the team via a midseason trade from the Washington Commanders in 2023. He led the Bears in sacks with 10 in 2025. Join or create a Yahoo Fantasy Basketball league for the 2026-27 NBA season Sweat has been a full-time NFL starter since joining the league with Washington as a first-round pick in the 2019 draft. He missed just one game over the last four seasons. In five games this season, Sweat has 2 sacks, 4 quarterback hits and 7 tackles, including 4 tackles for loss. His tackle pace has him on a trajectory for the lowest output of his career. The Bears are coming off their worst defensive performance of the season, a 31-7 loss to the rival Packers in which Green Bay tallied 428 total yards, including 358 passing yards. The loss was the first in three games for the Bears without quarterback Caleb Williams, who's been sidelined with a hamstring injury sustained in Week 2. It's not clear when Williams will be able to return. He's not been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Falcons. The Bears are 3-2, in a tie with the Packers and Lions behind the 5-0 Vikings in the NFC North.

stories.title: Micah Parsons: "Jayden Daniels probably cost Dan Quinn his job"
stories.summary: Packers LB minces no words about QB's role in clock disaster.
stories.detailText: {"unknownError":"There has been an error","expiredError":"This video has been expired due to copyright restrictions.","unavailableError":"This content is not yet available.","georestrictedError":"This content is not available in your location.","networkId":"169843","adManagerUrl":"https://mssl.fwmrm.net/libs/adm/6.51.0/AdManager.js","serverId":"https://29773.v.fwmrm.net/ad/g/1","profileId":"169843:nbcu_web_jwp_cs_moat_https","afid":"140315314","caid":"nbcs_nbc_pft_wshblame_261013","csid":"nbcsports_embed_on_domain","sfid":"","adHocGroup":"","athlete":"","businessUnit":"NBC Sports","category":"","duration":"368101","event":"","externalAdvertiserId":"nbcs_nbc_pft_wshblame_261013","genre":"News, Trending","guid":"nbc_pft_wshblame_261013","league":"NFL","network":"","platform":"PC","playlist":"","show":"ProFootballTalk","sport":"Football","subtype":"","team":"Washington Commanders","title": "Did some Commanders not know game could be a tie?","datePublished":"","videoPageUrl": "https://www.nbcsports.com/watch/nfl/profootballtalk/is-it-possible-that-some-commanders-didnt-know-game-could-end-in-tie","availableDate":"2026-10-13T12:44:04Z","expirationDate":"","countries":""} Micah Parsons still isn't ready to play after last year's knee injury, but he still knows how to mix things up. Parsons recently said on his podcast, The Edge with Micah Parsons , that quarterback Jayden Daniels is to blame for the game-clock clusterfudge at the end of overtime in the Giants-Commanders game. "Jayden Daniels probably cost my man Dan Quinn his job , to be honest with you," Parsons said, via Nicki Jhabvala of The Athletic . "To be honest with you. And, like, I'm a big Jayden Daniels fan. But the reality is, he probably cost a lot of people their jobs this past weekend. . . . "All respectfully, we get coached so much on these situations that, like, I'm a defensive player, and this shit's programmed to me. I even know what to do in those situations. There's no way I'm taking a sack with 14 seconds left and no timeouts. . . . And, mind you, it'd be different if Jayden Daniels was a rookie. This is your third year. This is your third year. You've been to the NFC Championship game. You've been in big moments before. And to me, like even after a sack, you're casually getting up." Parsons made it clear that, in his view, quarterbacks are expected to always know what's going on. "This is your job, bro," Parsons said. "This is your job to be prepared to understand the game and understand situations. That's in your job profile. And you're telling me, 'Oh, we're gonna want to pay this guy eventually $6000000? This cannot happen. . . . I'm a big JD5 fan, but that's inexcusable, bro." Parsons said that the Packers work on situational football "every day," What happened at the end of the Giants-Commanders game should have required no discussion, frankly. "This is a lack of preparation, a lack of mentality, and a lack of urgency," Parsons said. "That just can't happen." Parsons isn't wrong. The fact that it did happen raises plenty of questions about the level of preparation and attention to detail, as created by the coaching staff. It speaks to potential cultural flaws, perhaps one in which Daniels hasn't been challenged or held as accountable as he could have or should have been, given his standing in the organization. It would be a lot easier to make sense of all of this if the Commanders had recorded and preserved the relevant communications. And Daniels surely will face even more questions on this topic the next time he speaks to reporters. The fact that the outcome was so bizarre, so jarring, and so downright surreal becomes a horrible moment for everyone involved. As to the ultimate consequences, Parsons hit the nail on the head — Daniels's failure to take charge of the situation in the moment will probably cost Quinn his job. But Daniels will continue to be the starting quarterback because, even if he made an inexcusable mistake as to one of the easiest parts of the job, he does the hard parts better than most of his peers.

stories.title: Free agent OL Jamaree Salyer visits the Cardinals
stories.summary: The Cardinals spent time with a possible veteran addition to their offensive line on Tuesday.
stories.detailText: The Cardinals spent time with a possible veteran addition to their offensive line on Tuesday. Jeremy Fowler of ESPN reports that Jamaree Salyer visited with the team. Salyer was a 2022 sixth-round pick of the Chargers and he moved on to the Dolphins as a free agent this offseason. Salyer went on injured reserve with a knee injury over the summer and Miami released him off of that list in August. Per Fowler, Salyer had arthroscopic surgery on his knee and has been cleared to play. Salyer made 31 starts for the Chargers over his first two seasons and saw time at both tackle and guard.

stories.title: Brian Schottenheimer report card: Todd Bowles dominates Cowboys head coach in week 5
stories.summary: The seat may be getting hot for Brian Schottenheimer.
stories.detailText: Mandatory Credit: Kevin Jairaj-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect It was bound to happen, we just did not think it would come in Week 5 against the 0-4 Tampa Bay Buccaneers. For the first time this season, despite a 2-2 start, play-caller Brian Schottenheimer was absolutely dominated on game day. If you’re unfamiliar with Todd Bowles defenses, it all relies on exotic blitz looks and simulated pressure. That’s exactly what the Cowboys offense saw on Thursday night, and they never came up with an answer on how to beat it. In the first half, the Cowboys offense had some offensive success, but struggled to get into third and manageable, leading to far too many third-and-longs. That played right into Bowles hands, as he was able to mix up blitz looks to scheme pressure on quarterback Dak Prescott. In the first half, the route concepts the Cowboys were calling against the Buccaneers blitz looks left a lot to be desired. The Cowboys faced far too many 3rd and 7+ and that led to far too many long developing routes. In most cases against heavy pressure, you’d love to have a few receivers at or past the sticks, and safety valves to get the ball out to with a chance to pick up the first down after the catch (Javonte Williams was fantastic in pass protection). That was nonexistent for most of the night leading to a lot of incompletions, tight window throws, and some errant throws from Dak Prescott. With the scheme making it hard on the Cowboys passing and running game, we saw a season high in punts (three) and only converting on four of 10 third downs in their 24-16 loss. Even with the schematic issues in the Cowboys week five loss, they had an opportunity to win the game, but two dropped passes resulting in interceptions, along with a KaVontae Turpin fumble on the Cowboys second possession of the second half, killed any momentum and hope of the Cowboys winning the game. It’s unfair we ask the offense to be near perfect week in-and-week out, but with the way the defense has played over the last year-and-a-half, they will need to be. For a coach that has been in the league calling plays for 20 years, he needs to be better. It was very disappointing to see Bowles out-coach Schottenheimer at the rate that he did on Thursday night, and the conversation would have been just as loud if the Cowboys were able to pull off the comeback. With the division still wide open, Schottenheimer has to consider making changes on the offensive side of the ball. A few to consider would be cutting into Jake Ferguson’s reps, considering more route concepts and play calls that target the middle of the field, and using a bit more of Tyler Goodson in the underneath passing game (did not receive a carry or target in week five) to get some quick, easy completions with a more explosive runner after the catch. While it sounds like there are changes coming to the defensive side of the ball, Schottenheimer should not be cleared of criticism, even with the offensive performing at a very high-level for four out of the Cowboys five games so far in 2026. Play-Calling F Fourth-Down Decisions N/A The Cowboys only went for it on one fourth down in week five. An incompletion on a rushed throw from Prescott was the result. All other fourth downs were six plus yards and given the Cowboys struggles on offense, the decision to go would have been way too risky. Timeout Usage N/A Team Preparation F It was all pretty ugly. What grade would you give to Brian Schottenheimer on Sunday?

stories.title: Steelers Week 6 power rankings roundup: Is Pittsburgh gaining respect?
stories.summary: Pittsburgh Steelers Week 6 power rankings roundup.
stories.detailText: (Photo by Lauren Leigh Bacho/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Pittsburgh Steelers got back on track with a huge win over the Indianapolis Colts, 34-22 in Week 5. Quarterback Aaron Rodgers tossed three touchdowns for the third consecutive game. Running back Jaylen Warren had a touchdown reception of 80 yards and a touchdown run of 50 yards in the contest. It was the third straight game in which the star back had recorded over 100 scrimmage yards. Without further ado, it’s time for our weekly look around the internet to see where various media outlets place the Steelers among the rest of the NFL in this week’s power rankings roundup. FOX Sports: No.17 (No. 22 Last Week) “The Steelers are the most Jekyll and Hyde team in the NFL, which is why I have been all over the Power Rankings map with them. They are on a win-one, lose-one pace. But more than that, they seem to alternate between looking awful and looking terrific. They were back to mostly terrific against the Colts on Sunday. Aaron Rodgers had the offense humming, and he got a big-time performance from underrated RB Jaylen Warren, too.” – Ralph Vacchiano The Athletic: No.16 (No.20 last week) “Even if this season hasn’t gone exactly as Aaron Rodgers imagined (at least based on the moments of frustration between him and Mike McCarthy), Rodgers continues to climb the record books. In an impressive win over the Colts, Rodgers surpassed Peyton Manning for the third-most all-time touchdown passes, including the playoffs (582).” – Chad Graff and Josh Kendall CBS Sports: No.13 (No. 21 last week) “At 3-2, the offense showed some life against the Colts. The running game with Jaylen Warren really led them to victory.” – Pete Prisco Pro Football Talk: No.12 (No. 14 last week) The Steelers are in a three way tie for 12th on the PFT NFL power rankings with the Browns and Bengals. “They’re second in the list because they beat the Bengals.” – Mike Florio NFL.com: No.22 (No.25 last week) “Pittsburgh is becoming an every-other-week team, producing offensive explosions in odd-numbered weeks and struggling in even weeks. While that’s a path destined for a near-.500 record, perhaps Sunday’s output vs. Indianapolis was an example of a group recovering from a tough loss and applying the lessons learned. It was certainly encouraging to see the Steelers finally lean on Jaylen Warren. That’s a method that will produce consistent success, regardless of week number.” – Nick Shook Yahoo! Sports: No.17 (No. 21 last week) “Aaron Rodgers’ stat line isn’t perfect. His 59.8 completion percentage is the worst of his career as a starter. So is his 88.9 passer rating. But what he’s doing at his age has been approached only by Tom Brady.” “Not counting Brady, whose production in his 40s is an extreme outlier, no quarterback in his age-43 season (Rodgers turns 43 in December) has ever had more than 952 passing yards or six touchdowns in a season. Their teams combined for two wins in their starts, and both were from Vinny Testaverde in 2007. Testaverde had a bad 65.8 passer rating that season. Rodgers already has 1,234 yards, 10 touchdowns and the Steelers have won three of his starts, more than every other quarterback at his age combined, other than Brady.” “Whatever happens the rest of this season, Rodgers’ season is already historic for his age.” – Frank Schwab USA Today: No.17 (No.19 last week) “Maybe they need to rethink the timeshare approach with RB Jaylen Warren, who’s produced 490 yards from scrimmage on 61 touches over the past three weeks as the primary backfield option.” – Nate Davis ESPN: No.20 (No. 20 last week) “The Steelers’ secondary has been in flux since Joey Porter Jr. began the hold-in during training camp that ultimately ended with his trade to the Cowboys. As a result, the Steelers’ secondary has been plagued with inconsistent play and busted coverages. Porter’s absence and departure, coupled with Jamel Dean’s ankle injury, forced rookie Daylen Everette into more action. And Asante Samuel Jr. hasn’t replicated his training camp performance. At safety, starter DeShon Elliott unexpectedly began the season on IR while still recovering from his 2025 knee injury, and free agent acquisition Jaquan Brisker has underperformed. Rookie Robert Spears-Jennings has shown promise, but he’s still young” – Brooke Pryor Most media outlets seem to be catching on to what many Steelers fans already know, that being they’re a very week-to-week team. It truly is anyone’s guess what version of the Steelers shows up on any given Sunday. Although the Colts clearly have issues, Pittsburgh was able to comfortably beat them while their offense continued to show signs of growth. Perhaps the Steelers can earn more trust from us and the rest of the internet with a road win over undrafted free agent quarterback Jalon Daniels and the Tampa Bay Buccaneers this weekend. Let us know what you think in the comments . Be sure to bookmark Behind the Steel Curtain for all the latest news, breakdowns, and more! stories.title: One wide receiver most fits the bill for a Chiefs midseason trade
stories.summary: There is one receiver with trade rumors swirling that could revamp his career in Kansas City.
stories.detailText: (Photo by Justin Edmonds/Getty Images) | Getty Images The latest addition to the Kansas City Chiefs wide receiver room — signing Justin Watson to the practice squad — may not have been the flashy signing Chiefs Kingdom expected, but it also may not be the only new face in the group this season. The season-long injury to wide receiver Tyquan Thornton (dislocated ankle) puts the team in position to look at ways to improve the position. We expect the Cheetah, Tyreek Hill, to return to the Chiefs this season , but there are no guarantees. If a significant move is to be made, it could be a trade. It wouldn’t be the first time general manager Brett Veach has traded for a wide receiver midseason. 2022: Traded a compensatory third-round pick and a sixth-round pick for Kadarius Toney 2023: Traded a future sixth-round pick for Mecole Hardman 2024: Traded a fifth-round pick for DeAndre Hopkins So who could Kansas City get via trade? The NFL Trade Deadline is November 10th, less than a month from today. The rumors are starting to swirl, and according to NFL Insider Jordan Schultz , a receiver on the (3-2) Cleveland Browns could be available. “Jerry Jeudy… the Browns clearly like the young receiver group they have and are building… Jeudy made some big plays in Thursday night’s win over [the Pittsburgh Steelers ], but then only played 24 snaps on Sunday, even with (KC Concepcion) leaving early with a concussion.” “It’s pretty well-known around the league that Jeudy is available, but my understanding is that Cleveland would like something in that early-third-to-fourth range; I’m just not sure they’ll be able to get it.” Jerry Jeudy Six years ago, Jeudy was the 15th overall pick of the Denver Broncos in the 2020 NFL Draft, which is the first criterion that stands out about trading for him. Whether it was Toney or Hopkins, or even wide receiver Josh Gordon in 2021, Veach has targeted former high-end talents or former first-round picks when the organization has no prior history with them. However, there are some ties to the Chiefs: Wide receivers coach Chad O’Shea coached Jeudy for two seasons in Cleveland, including a Pro Bowl campaign in 2024 in which Jeudy racked up 1,229 yards on 90 receptions. It’s the only Pro Bowl season of Jeudy’s career. This season, Jeudy has been buried in the rotation and has only caught eight passes for 81 yards. However, he has shown he can make plays downfield in Cleveland. Over the 2024 and 2025 seasons, Jeudy caught 12 passes thrown 20 or more yards downfield, for 438 yards and four touchdowns, according to Pro Football Focus . Jeudy is a volatile playmaker; he had 19 drops between the 2024 and 2025 campaigns. If Cleveland is motivated to find draft compensation for Jeudy’s talents, the Chiefs are a strong fit based on Jeudy’s pedigree, the ties to O’Shea and what he brings to the offense. If Kansas City can send a Day 3 pick for the 27-year-old wideout, it could be a strong option to replenish the Chiefs’ playmaking for this season and the future without taking a huge risk. He is signed through the 2027 season, with a $13.4 million cap hit next year. Editor’s Note: Jeudy’s contract includes a nearly $23 million non-guaranteed option bonus next season. Financially, a team would likely be motivated to get out of that contract before using his services in 2027. Do you like the idea of Kansas City trading for Jeudy? Let us know in the comments.
