stories.title: On Arch Manning’s maddening inconsistency
stories.summary: From Dr. Manning to Mr. Swoopes and back again.
stories.detailText: DALLAS, TEXAS - OCTOBER 10: Arch Manning #16 of the Texas Longhorns stands on the sideline during a game against the Oklahoma Sooners at Cotton Bowl on October 10, 2026 in Dallas, Texas. (Photo by Stacy Revere/Getty Images) | Getty Images From play to play, there are two versions of Texas Longhorns senior quarterback Arch Manning. Dr. Manning is capable of seeing the field and delivering highlight-reel plays that justify his longtime perception as a potential top pick in the NFL Draft, like his 41-yard touchdown pass to junior wide receiver Cam Coleman on Saturday in the Cotton Bowl after climbing the pocket and resetting his feet to make the delivery. Arch Manning evades the rush and finds Cam Coleman for a 41 Yard TD🤘 (Via: ABC) pic.twitter.com/iTuxH0FYdJ — PFF College (@PFF_College) October 10, 2026 Or Dr. Manning’s 42-yard completion to Coleman, an inch-perfect delivery between two defenders. ARCH MANNING TO CAM COLEMAN DEEP BLURRR pic.twitter.com/Wa5wkwn6Gr — wok (@wokdior) October 10, 2026 Or ripping a 34-yard throw to junior wide receiver Ryan Wingo down the seam for a touchdown, a pass made on time and in rhythm. ARCH MANNING TO RYAN WINGO TOUCHDOWN ARCH IS FINDING HIS GROOVE pic.twitter.com/b1M0bAOeGF — ClutchWire (@ClutchWireHQ) October 10, 2026 And then there’s Mr. Swoopes, Dr. Manning’s counterpart who struggles with processing, pocket presence, and accuracy, the quarterback wracked by indecision about when to run or pass who has three illegal forward passes in the last three games. While Dr. Manning has elite arm strength, Mr. Swoopes lacks arm talent and struggles to make the same type of improvisational, off-platform deliveries that defined the high-end talent possessed by Quinn Ewers. Mr. Swoopes is more of an athlete trying to play quarterback who makes mistakes like floating a duck into the defense on the run that turns into a touchdown back in his face. ARCH MANNING TOUCHDOWN PASS TO THE DEFENSE pic.twitter.com/nz7czGREEb — wok (@wokdior) October 10, 2026 Mr. Swoopes has breakdowns in footwork, decision making, and ball placement that result in a late-game interception thrown off his back foot and inside into the defender’s leverage instead of safely out of bounds. ARCH MANNING THROWS A COSTLY INTERCEPTION WITH 20 SECONDS LEFT!! pic.twitter.com/Hq9o38IUzf — ESPN (@espn) October 10, 2026 Mr. Swoopes hitches in a clean pocket until he’s on the back of his center, floating his throwing lanes closed and taking a sack that leads to a blocked punt touchdown. Mr. Swoopes lacks his stinger, turning his athleticism into indecision to limit off-schedule success. Mr. Swoopes lacks the freedom or comfort level to change plays at the line of scrimmage, leading to look-back calls from the sideline that can force wasted timeouts. “I think that he’s processing fine,” Sarkisian said on Monday. But is fine the standard for Manning as a fourth-year player who is in his second season as the starter? “I think if you took the name off the back of his jersey, and you said, ‘Here’s Joe Smith playing quarterback at the University of Texas, and here’s a guy who’s beaten four top 10 ranked teams in his last 13 starts,’ we’d be praising the guy, but the expectations are high for him. He understands that the expectations are high for all of us, so we’ve got to we got to put our nose back to the grind and get back to work,” Sarkisian said. What about assessing the totality of Manning’s performance against the Sooners, which included those three big throws, but was arguably defined by the two crushing interceptions that led to 10 points. “I hate it for him. He has two interceptions in the fourth quarter of that game when, quite frankly, I thought he played pretty good up until that point, and that’s the frustrating part, but that’s the level of consistency that’s needed,” Sarkisian said. It’s the type of consistency that’s lacking as the quarterback veers from Dr. Manning to Mr. Swoopes. The Texas head coach and his staff aren’t helping enough, either. Manning simply hasn’t developed enough during his four years in Austin, an indictment of Sarkisian, AJ Milwee, and Mike Bimonte as quarterbacks coaches exacerbated by the lack of development from Ewers during his own time on the Forty Acres, high-profile failures that are threatening to become a trend. Why hasn’t the game slowed down enough for Manning? Why is he having breakdowns in his footwork? Why is his pocket presence a continued issue? Why is he visibly indecisive when he has space to run? In retrospect, perhaps the greatest misconception surrounding Manning is that his last name endowed a certain level of the football intelligence and processing speed possessed by his uncles, producing a player with all the best attributes of his uncles and grandfather. Instead, Manning often looks like an athlete constrained by a scheme in which he’s been told not to scramble and rarely receives opportunities to execute designed runs. Last year, Manning ran for 519 yards and 10 touchdowns, including 32 scrambles for 349 yards and another 31 designed runs. This year, Manning has yet to record his first rushing touchdown, had three of his five designed runs on the season called against Oklahoma, and started looking much less decisive after getting reprimanded for scrambling too much in the UTSA game, contributing to those three illegal forward passes. Through the air, the type of pass plays that Sarkisian is calling are part of the problem, from a lack of hot reads against the blitzes that SEC opponents have frequently employed to the other missing parts of the quick game, highlighted by the utter absence of the screen game that was so threatening to opponents before Manning took over the starting role. Last year, Manning’s average depth of target careened from 20.2 against Florida as the Texas quarterback took a beating while trying to lead a comeback to four yards against Oklahoma when Sarkisian allowed him to operate in an efficient, game-manager role that played an important part in the victory. This year, Sarkisian apparently forgot that lesson because Manning’s average depth of target was at 10.7 yards on Saturday. Just an OU guy’s opinion here… Sark needs to call more quick game. They run too many deep route concepts. I get he wants to push it down the field & produce explosives but it’s tough on Arch & the OL. Need to get their athletes the ball quicker in space. Also…get TE involved. https://t.co/ll4FPD9F3D — Gabe Ikard (@GabeIkard) October 13, 2026 The problem with trying to get the ball to the tight ends more in the passing game? There’s no evidence that’s a real possibility . As for Dr. Manning and Mr. Swoopes, there’s a growing sense that they will return to Texas for a fifth season, but given Manning’s lack of development so far, the Horns may simply be stuck with an unanticipated package deal.

stories.title: Bengals TE Tanner Hudson to miss rest of season with torn pectoral
stories.summary: The Bengals have lost a member of their tight end corps for the rest of the season.
stories.detailText: The Bengals have lost a member of their tight end corps for the rest of the season. Tight end Tanner Hudson's agent told Charlie Clifford of WLWT that Hudson is out for the year due to a torn pectoral. The injury occurred during the Bengals' win over the Dolphins in Week 5. Hudson caught a two-yard touchdown pass in the 31-24 win and had three catches for 14 yards overall. He had four catches for 19 yards in the first four weeks of the season. Hudson is in his fourth season with the Bengals and is set to be a free agent in 2027. Mike Gesicki, Erick All, Drew Sample, and Jack Endries are the team's remaining tight ends.

teamStories.summary: After getting praised by the media a week ago, the tune surrounding Las Vegas is much different this time around
teamStories.detailText: (Photo by Winslow Townson/Getty Images) | Getty Images The media was singing the Las Vegas Raiders’ praises last week . However, it’s a much different tune in the Week 6 NFL Power Rankings roundup after a 45-17 blowout loss to the New England Patriots . Sports Illustrated 16. Las Vegas Raiders Last week: 10 While I’m not overreacting at all to the Fernando Mendoza appearance at the end of the Patriots blowout, I do wonder if three straight losses at least generates some conversation. Something tells me the Raiders are dug in on this, but .500 after six weeks will change a lot of minds. — Conor Orr Klint Kubiak called Kirk Cousins the Raiders’ starter during the head coach’s press conference on Monday, putting a brief halt to the questions about when Mendoza will take over under center. However, Orr is correct that if the Silver and Black lose to the 4-1 Buffalo Bills this Sunday, those conversations are really going to heat up. Does that mean the rookie’s first start will be behind a shaky offensive line against a Los Angeles Rams defensive line that features two future first-ballot Hall of Famers in Week 7? Granted, Myles Garrett may not return from injured reserve by the end of the month, which could change the situation. But the following week against the New York Jets feels like the sweet spot, unless Las Vegas pulls off an upset or two before the trip to the Big Apple. Bleacher Report 18. Las Vegas Raiders Last week: 10 Even after consecutive losses, the Las Vegas Raiders are sitting at 3-2. Most Raiders fans would have taken that sort of start to the season, given the option to do so in August. However, things feel a lot different after a blowout loss to the New England Patriots than they felt following last week’s close loss to the rival Chiefs. Playing across the country with a less-than-100-percent Ashton Jeanty certainly didn’t help Las Vegas. However, the Raiders’ defense looked legitimately bad for the first time this season, and the lack of wide-receiver depth was glaring as Las Vegas tried to keep pace with Drake Maye and Co. Fernando Mendoza made his 2026 debut after the game got out of hand on Sunday. While Kirk Cousins wasn’t benched for performance reasons, calls for Mendoza will intensify if Las Vegas has many more team performances like the one it had in Week 5. — Kristopher Knox Knox has pretty much the same take as Orr and me on the Mendoza-Cousins situation. The hot start to the season might have temporarily altered the timeline for the No. 1 pick’s first start. However, if the postseason goes back to being an afterthought, it’s probably time to see what the kid is made of. ESPN 17. Las Vegas Raiders Last week: 11 Biggest issue on defense: Growing pains in the secondary are showing Rookie cornerback Hezekiah Masses had a strong start, being named the AFC’s Defensive Player of the Week after the Raiders’ Week 2 win over the Chargers. But Masses has allowed nine catches, 155 yards, two touchdowns and a 60% completion rate the past three games. Against the Patriots, the Raiders’ young trio of defensive backs — Masses, rookie safety Treydan Stukes and second-year cornerback Darien Porter — all struggled. Porter gave up a 49-yard reception to wide receiver Kyle Williams. Stukes gave up three catches for 59 yards, including a 35-yard touchdown in the first quarter. — Ryan McFadden It’s interesting to me that the young defensive backs are getting called out here. Don’t get me wrong, Masses has struggled over the last three weeks, and Stukes had a bad game in New England. But whether you use Pro Football Focus or Next Gen Stats , Eric Stokes has given up the most yards in coverage (209 or 205) and the second-highest completion percentage (62.5% or 56.0%) of the corners who have at least 10 coverage snaps. Also, Taron Johnson is third in yards (132 or 168) and is first in completion percentage (68.4% or 68.2%). Yes, Porter gave up a 49-yard catch to the Patriots. However, he’s yielded three completions on nine targets (33.3%) for 61 yards, per PFF, or four receptions on 11 targets (36.4%) for 86 yards, per NGS. So, that one play accounts for about 80% or 57.0% of the production he’s allowed so far this season. Also, the play the second-year pro was beaten on in New England was a Cover 0 call where he had to cover a deep over route while the Patriots had max protection to give Drake Maye all day to throw. On top of that, he had two PBUs last Sunday. Sure, Stokes and Johnson have been on the field more than any of the young guys mentioned, which leads to the higher volume stats. But the point here is that the entire secondary is struggling right now, not just the first- and second-year defensive backs. Additionally, Rob Leonard has to shoulder a good portion of the blame since his play-calling has become predictable and put the defense in bad spots over the last three weeks. The Athletic 17. Las Vegas Raiders Last week: 13 Who have you beaten? Dolphins, Chargers, Saints The Raiders were exposed Sunday after a strong start to the season, largely on the back of wins over bad teams. But this trip to New England revealed a lot of flaws for Klint Kubiak and company. The defense was a total mess, allowing six touchdowns on 10 real drives. — Chad Graff, Josh Kendall I stand by what I said at the beginning of the season: the Raiders shouldn’t apologize for beating bad teams a year after being the worst team in the league. However, when it comes to them being legitimate playoff contenders in 2026, this is where the 3-2 record gets misleading. Vegas’ best win right now is against a 1-4 New Orleans Saints team that has lost its last two games by multiple possessions and a combined 31 points. That takes the air out of the “Saints are better than their record indicates” argument, and the 0-5 Miami Dolphins and 0-5 Los Angeles Chargers aren’t doing the Raiders any favors with how they’ve played over the last five weeks. NFL.com 19. Las Vegas Raiders Last week: 12 The Raiders finally became the overmatched team we expected to see in 2026. Las Vegas’ defense couldn’t stop a nosebleed on Sunday, surrendering over 500 yards of offense to a unit that seemed lost just two weeks prior. An inability to protect Kirk Cousins (plus a continued lack of production from the ground game) prevented the offense from keeping up in a blowout loss. It’s certainly not time to consider benching Cousins for Fernando Mendoza, but the Raiders have officially encountered their first pothole and will need to divert accordingly in order to sustain the momentum built by a strong start. — Nick Shook Shook kind of alludes to this: a two-game skid is the first significant adversity Kubiak has faced as a head coach. How will he get his team to respond? We’ll find out on Sunday. It may be doom and gloom right now, but if the Silver and Black can pull off an upset against the Bills, I’ll turn to my friend Michael Corleone for the appropriate response.

teamStories.title: 2026 NFL Power Rankings: How all 32 teams stack up for Week 6
teamStories.summary: How does every NFL team stack up heading into Week 6? We made our 1-32 list and picked the biggest defensive problem for every team.
teamStories.detailText: NFL teams are averaging 23.3 points in the 2026 season . Though some of those points have come from defensive touchdowns and one punt return TD from the Vikings, it's mostly an indicator that offenses are getting into scoring territory a lot . So why are defenses struggling so much? In addition to our updated 1-32 rankings, we asked our NFL Nation reporters to pick out the biggest defensive issue for each team. From secondary depth to third-down defense, what is causing each team to falter? To form the list, our power panel of more than a dozen NFL analysts evaluates how all 32 teams stack up against one another. Here are a few highlights from this week's rankings: The Patriots have returned to the top 10 after back-to-back wins over the Bills and Raiders. Sunday's win was catalyzed by another strong performance from quarterback Drake Maye , who led the team to its most points (45) and yards (536) in a game since 2021. The Patriots could continue their hot streak with matchups against the Jets and Dolphins in two of the next three weeks. The Packers are also climbing back up our list after two losses in their first three games. Green Bay entered Sunday's matchup against Chicago as 1.5-point underdogs, but it completely dominated the Bears to avenge its wild-card loss last season. Quarterback Jordan Love 's 367 passing yards were the second most by any QB in Bears-Packers series history, per ESPN Research. The bottom three teams in our rankings (Chargers, Titans and Dolphins) are all 0-5. It's the fifth time since the 1970 merger that three teams from the same conference have started a season with that record, per ESPN Research. Los Angeles had the most excruciating loss of the bunch this past weekend, blowing a seven-point lead with nine minutes left against the Broncos . Let's get into the full list, starting with the same No. 1 team from last week. Previous rankings: Week 2 | Week 3 | Week 4 | Week 5 Jump to a team: ARI | ATL | BAL | BUF | CAR | CHI | CIN CLE | DAL | DEN | DET | GB | HOU | IND JAX | KC | LAC | LAR | LV | MIA | MIN NE | NO | NYG | NYJ | PHI | PIT | SF SEA | TB | TEN | WSH 1. San Francisco 49ers (5-0) Week 5 result: Beat the Seahawks 32-29 Week 5 ranking: 1 Biggest issue on defense: Third-down efficiency Under new coordinator Raheem Morris , the Niners rank fifth in yards per play allowed (4.7) and have limited big plays as well as any team in the league. But they have struggled to get off the field consistently. The Niners rank 20th in third-down defense, giving up a first down on 40.8% of their opportunities. As a result, their defense has been on the field for 31 minutes, 12 seconds per game, which ranks 23rd in the NFL. -- Nick Wagoner 2. Kansas City Chiefs (4-0) Week 5 result: Bye Week 5 ranking: 2 Biggest issue on defense: Not enough sacks The Chiefs can generate pressure on the quarterback, whether it's via Chris Jones , George Karlaftis or rookie R Mason Thomas . But they have one of the biggest statistical anomalies of the 2026 season: zero sacks in the first month. Before their bye week , they couldn't put Raiders QB Kirk Cousins on the turf despite a season-high 21 pressures. If the Chiefs can start collecting sacks, their defense could be a top unit in the second half of the season. -- Nate Taylor 3. Buffalo Bills (4-1) Week 5 result: Beat the Rams 37-34 (OT) Week 5 ranking: 4 Biggest issue on defense: Letting offenses off the hook The Bills haven't had much issue pushing offenses backward on first down. But opponents have had far too much success extending drives in second-and-long and third-and-long situations. Plenty of this has to do with the Bills' dwindling cornerback depth, but that's hardly an excuse for how C.J. Stroud , Jared Goff , Drake Maye and Matthew Stafford completed 74.6% of their passes for 558 yards and five touchdowns (posting a 80.8 QBR) on second downs against the Bills. -- Nick Suss 4. Seattle Seahawks (3-2) Week 5 result: Lost to the 49ers 32-29 Week 5 ranking: 3 Biggest issue on defense: Not enough stops in the red zone The biggest problem for the Seahawks' defense might actually be their offense; the 44 points they've given up off turnovers is tied for most in the NFL. You have to look hard to find a true weakness with a unit that ranks second in both defensive EPA and ESPN's defensive efficiency metric, but the Seahawks are 27th in opponent red zone efficiency (75%) and tied for last in opponent goal-to-go efficiency (100%). Granted, they haven't allowed offenses to get that far down the field often -- only 12 times inside their 20 (tied for fifth fewest) and seven times inside their 10 (tied for seventh fewest). -- Brady Henderson 5. Jacksonville Jaguars (4-1) Week 5 result: Beat the Eagles 19-17 Week 5 ranking: 5 Biggest issue on defense: Getting sacks from the edge It's nitpicky, considering the Jaguars are No. 1 in run defense and second in scoring defense, but they could do a better job of getting sacks from their edge rushers. Their 80 QB pressures are tied for sixth and 11 sacks rank ninth, but edge rushers Josh Hines-Allen and Travon Walker have only 3.5 sacks combined. They each had 1.5 sacks in the season opener against the Browns but a combined half sack since (Walker on Sunday). Both are a large part of the run defense (63.8 yards per game) by setting the edge, but their sack production needs to increase. -- Michael DiRocco 6. Minnesota Vikings (5-0) Week 5 result: Beat the Saints 23-13 Week 5 ranking: 9 Biggest issue on defense: Depth not tested yet It's not easy to find a negative indicator from a defense that has been the league's best this season, based on NFL Next Gen Stats' expected point average. But because the Vikings have been almost entirely healthy, their depth at multiple positions is untested. In fact, eight defensive players have been on the field for at least 80% of the snaps. That doesn't mean the backups would falter in more prominent roles. It's just hard to judge based on game reps. -- Kevin Seifert 7. Baltimore Ravens (4-1) Week 5 result: Beat the Falcons 30-23 (OT) Week 5 ranking: 6 Biggest issue on defense: Getting stops on third down The Ravens are allowing teams to convert 41.5% of their third downs, which ranks 20th in the NFL. It's frustrating because Baltimore seems to be winning on the early downs before giving up a big play on third down. Opposing quarterbacks are averaging 8.7 yards per attempt on third down, the fifth highest in the league. The Ravens gave up nine third-down conversions Sunday, which are the most they've given up in a game in two seasons. "It obviously feels a lot better fixing those mistakes with a win," safety Kyle Hamilton said. "I might be a little too cynical or critical, but we can be better." -- Jamison Hensley 8. Los Angeles Rams (2-3) Week 5 result: Lost to the Bills 37-34 (OT) Week 5 ranking: 7 Biggest issue on defense: Missing Myles Garrett The Rams' defense has been inconsistent at times, and it has only eight sacks this season (tied for sixth fewest in the NFL). But Los Angeles should get more sack production once the reigning Defensive Player of the Year is back on the field. Garrett, who had knee surgery in mid-September , is eligible to return to practice this week. Rams coach Sean McVay said the team is unlikely to open Garrett's 21-day practice window this week, but the pass rusher is making "good progress." -- Sarah Barshop 9. New England Patriots (3-2) Week 5 result: Beat the Raiders 45-17 Week 5 ranking: 14 Biggest issue on defense: Cornerback depth They played with only three healthy CBs on Sunday, as starters Christian Gonzalez ( shoulder ) and Carlton Davis III ( neck ) were inactive, and rookie backups Karon Prunty and Channing Canada were unavailable because of hamstring injuries. When fill-in starter Charles Woods left the game in the second half because of a shoulder injury, it further thinned a perilous CB situation, leaving just Marcus Jones and Kindle Vildor as available options. New England has allowed a 66% completion rate this season, which ranks 25th in the NFL. -- Mike Reiss 10. Denver Broncos (3-2) Week 5 result: Beat the Chargers 23-17 Week 5 ranking: 10 Biggest issue on defense: Missed tackles For a defense that continues to flash its teeth when the Broncos really need it -- they gave the offense the ball in Chargers territory on four of their five scoring drives Sunday, including three in the fourth quarter -- missed tackles continue to plague the group. From an astounding 19 missed tackles in the season opener to three missed tackles on Chargers running back Kimani Vidal 's 42-yard touchdown run Sunday, Denver could get back to elite status if it cleans up its tackling. After giving up the second-fewest yards per game last season (278.2), the Broncos rank 22nd in 2026 (347.4). -- Jeff Legwold 11. Detroit Lions (3-2) Week 5 result: Beat the Cardinals 45-21 Week 5 ranking: 16 Biggest issue on defense: A depleted secondary Defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard was under fire after Detroit gave up at least 30 points in three of its first four games, though the Lions enjoyed a much better performance Sunday before heading into their bye week. The biggest struggles have been in the secondary, as they've given up a league-high 1,487 passing yards. It should be noted that the Lions entered the season without Pro Bowl safeties Brian Branch and Kerby Joseph . And they're missing safety Thomas Harper and defensive back Avonte Maddox , who are on injured reserve. Branch should return for Week 7 after being sidelined since December because of a torn Achilles . -- Eric Woodyard 12. Cincinnati Bengals (3-2) Week 5 result: Beat the Dolphins 31-24 Week 5 ranking: 15 Biggest issue on defense: Stopping big runs It has been boom or bust for Cincinnati's run defense. Though it has been good in spots, it has given up far too many big plays. The Bengals lead the NFL in giving up 21 carries of 10 or more yards, per ESPN Research. Seventeen of those have come the past three weeks. Even in Week 5, the Bengals surrendered 217 rushing yards, including 80 yards over expectation, per NFL Next Gen Stats. Improving the run defense will be crucial with the Bengals set to face Derrick Henry and the Ravens after the upcoming bye week. -- Ben Baby 13. Chicago Bears (3-2) Week 5 result: Lost to the Packers 31-7 Week 5 ranking: 8 Biggest issue on defense: The secondary is more problematic than the pass rush The Bears' preseason belief that their secondary would be the strength of the defense has gone out the window. That unit allowed Green Bay quarterback Jordan Love to complete six passes for 25-plus yards and has been trending down since a shootout with the Panthers in Week 1. Rookie defensive backs Dillon Thieneman and Malik Muhammad II will understandably experience growing pains, but the play of veteran cornerbacks Jaylon Johnson (77.3% of targets thrown into his coverage have been caught) and Tyrique Stevenson Sr . (allowing a 140.7 passer rating when targeted) is a major cause for concern. -- Courtney Cronin 14. Green Bay Packers (3-2) Week 5 result: Beat the Bears 31-7 Week 5 ranking: 23 Biggest issue on defense: Injuries to the front seven In back-to-back weeks, the Packers lost linebacker Edgerrin Cooper and defensive tackle Javon Hargrave to season-ending Achilles injuries . Cooper was their best linebacker; Hargrave their most experienced defensive lineman. And who knows when edge rusher Micah Parsons will play? He hasn't practiced since last year's torn ACL in Week 15. While they've struggled to get off the field on third down and they've been gashed on the ground a couple of times, the biggest issues are injuries and the corresponding absences of key players such as Cooper and Parsons. -- Rob Demovsky 15. Dallas Cowboys (2-3) Week 5 result: Lost to the Buccaneers 24-16 Week 5 ranking: 12 Biggest issue on defense: Everything? How do you pick just one issue when it comes to the Cowboys? They are giving up 27.2 points per game, which ranks 26th in the NFL. They are giving up 168.4 rushing yards per game, which is last in the league. They have recorded only five sacks and do not have an interception this season. Opposing quarterbacks are completing 72.3% of their passes. Through five games, new coordinator Christian Parker's defense might not be worse than it was under Matt Eberflus last season. But it is at least the same and a big reason why Dallas is 2-3. -- Todd Archer 16. Philadelphia Eagles (2-3) Week 5 result: Lost to the Jaguars 19-17 Week 5 ranking: 13 Biggest issue on defense: Fourth-quarter effectiveness There have been stretches in games, including Sunday, when coordinator Vic Fangio's unit looks as dominant as advertised. But the closing quarter has not been kind. Philly is last in opponent yards (648), 31st in touchdowns allowed (six) and 30th in opponent success rate (52.5%) in the final frame. The struggle is almost certainly linked to how much the defense is on the field, working opposite an Eagles offense that leads the league in three-and-outs (20). This defense is tied for the second-most snaps (332) in the NFL and will continue to wear down if that amount of usage continues. -- Tim McManus 17. Las Vegas Raiders (3-2) Week 5 result: Lost to the Patriots 45-17 Week 5 ranking: 11 Biggest issue on defense: Growing pains in the secondary are showing Rookie cornerback Hezekiah Masses had a strong start, being named the AFC's Defensive Player of the Week after the Raiders' Week 2 win over the Chargers . But Masses has allowed nine catches, 155 yards, two touchdowns and a 60% completion rate the past three games. Against the Patriots, the Raiders' young trio of defensive backs -- Masses, rookie safety Treydan Stukes and second-year cornerback Darien Porter -- all struggled. Porter gave up a 49-yard reception to wide receiver Kyle Williams . Stukes gave up three catches for 59 yards, including a 35-yard touchdown in the first quarter. -- Ryan McFadden 18. Carolina Panthers (2-2) Week 5 result: Bye Week 5 ranking: 18 Biggest issue on defense: Starting cornerbacks on IR With Jaycee Horn ( quad ) and Mike Jackson ( groin ) on IR, the Panthers enter Week 6 with rookie Will Lee III and special teams ace Akayleb Evans penciled in as their starting cornerbacks. In their Week 4 win over the Lions , Evans allowed 12 catches for 208 yards and a touchdown (on 16 targets), according to NFL Next Gen Stats. Lee had a better outing (four catches allowed for 47 yards on seven targets). The Panthers could use some help at the position or a significant switch-up in the starting lineup. Chau Smith-Wade , a 2024 fifth-round pick, is an option. -- Mike Kaye 19. New York Giants (3-1-1) Week 5 result: Tied the Commanders 27-27 Week 5 ranking: 17 Biggest issue on defense: Interior defensive line depth The Giants are thin on the interior of their defensive line, so it's no wonder they are ranked 25th in run defense (127.6 rushing yards allowed per game), and 30th in yards allowed per carry (5.19). On the Commanders' first two long touchdown runs Sunday, starting defensive linemen DJ Reader and Shelby Harris were off the field, replaced by Darius Alexander and CJ Okoye . New York is going to need to find a more palatable rotation. -- Jordan Raanan 20. Pittsburgh Steelers (3-2) Week 5 result: Beat the Colts 34-22 Week 5 ranking: 20 Biggest issue on defense: Lack of secondary depth The Steelers' secondary has been in flux since Joey Porter Jr . began the hold-in during training camp that ultimately ended with his trade to the Cowboys . As a result, the Steelers' secondary has been plagued with inconsistent play and busted coverages. Porter's absence and departure, coupled with Jamel Dean 's ankle injury, forced rookie Daylen Everette into more action. And Asante Samuel Jr . hasn't replicated his training camp performance. At safety, starter DeShon Elliott unexpectedly began the season on IR while still recovering from his 2025 knee injury , and free agent acquisition Jaquan Brisker has underperformed. Rookie Robert Spears-Jennings has shown promise, but he's still young. -- Brooke Pryor 21. Houston Texans (1-4) Week 5 result: Beat the Titans 26-3 Week 5 ranking: 24 Biggest issue on defense: Health at all three levels The Texans have dealt with injuries to key players. Pro Bowl linebacker Azeez Al-Shaair sat out time because of a groin injury. Nickelback Jalen Pitre just sustained a shoulder injury against the Titans, defensive tackle Kayden McDonald was on IR because of a quad injury to start the season, and linebacker Henry To'oTo'o landed on IR after Week 1 because of a shoulder injury . That has factored into their defense giving up 234 passing yards per game (23rd). Overall, Houston is tied for 15th in scoring defense (22.4 per game) after ranking second last season (17.4). -- DJ Bien-Aime 22. Atlanta Falcons (2-3) Week 5 result: Lost to the Ravens 30-23 (OT) Week 5 ranking: 25 Biggest issue on defense: Not enough takeaways The Falcons have made great improvements against the run compared to last season. And Atlanta's pass rush has been better than expected despite the loss of edge rushers Jalon Walker ( torn ACL ) and James Pearce Jr . ( suspension ). But the Falcons' secondary has been banged up, with top cornerback A.J. Terrell Jr. ( groin ) on injured reserve and replacement C.J. Henderson (groin) being injured in Sunday's loss. Atlanta has only one interception this season; 27 teams have more. Coach Kevin Stefanski has preached winning the turnover battle, which means the Falcons need to generate more takeaway opportunities. -- Marc Raimondi 23. Cleveland Browns (3-2) Week 5 result: Lost to the Jets 17-12 Week 5 ranking: 19 Biggest issue on defense: Run defense The Browns' defense rebounded after giving up 34 points to the Jaguars in Week 1 , but the inability to stop the run has been a consistent theme this season. Cleveland is giving up 4.5 yards per attempt, the ninth-worst mark in the NFL. And its success rate on opponent rushes (52.8%) is the second-worst mark in the league. Tackling has been an issue; opponents are averaging 2.53 yards after contact per rush, which ranks 30th. -- Daniel Oyefusi 24. Indianapolis Colts (2-3) Week 5 result: Lost to the Steelers 34-22 Week 5 ranking: 22 Biggest issue on defense: Poor tackling The Colts have a litany of issues on defense, but tackling is a fundamental problem that affects many areas. Consider: They rank 28th in yards allowed after contact (482). That showed up repeatedly Sunday, including on a 50-yard touchdown run from Steelers running back Jaylen Warren . It's not a coincidence the Colts are 31st in the league in yards allowed per play (6.2). Most responsible for this issue are the team's underwhelming linebackers. -- Stephen Holder 25. New York Jets (2-3) Week 5 result: Beat the Browns 17-12 Week 5 ranking: 26 Biggest issue on defense: Interceptions are rare The frequency is roughly the same as a term in the House of Representatives: every two years. The Jets have intercepted only one pass in the past 22 games, with safety Minkah Fitzpatrick ending a historic 20-game drought in last week's loss to the Bears . On Sunday, he had a chance to make it two games in a row, but he dropped a would-be pick. The Jets are playing more zone than man-to-man this season, which makes the low total even more perplexing. The Cowboys are the only team with zero interceptions. -- Rich Cimini 26. New Orleans Saints (1-4) Week 5 result: Lost to the Vikings 23-13 Week 5 ranking: 21 Biggest issue on defense: Interior defensive line The Saints' defensive line has been confusing this season. Their depth issues started when Bryan Bresee sustained a torn ACL in training camp , yet rookie second-round pick Christen Miller has barely been on the field. That lack of depth showed up Sunday, when two defensive linemen were inactive due to sickness and the team allowed a 100-yard rusher for the second straight game. The Saints rank 30th in rushing yards allowed and haven't had much of an interior pass rush this season. -- Katherine Terrell 27. Tampa Bay Buccaneers (1-4) Week 5 result: Beat the Cowboys 24-16 Week 5 ranking: 30 Biggest issue on defense: Inconsistency You don't know who or what you're going to get with the Bucs right now. Take inside linebacker Alex Anzalone , who struggled mightily early in the season but was a standout Thursday night with his game-sealing interception. There was a reason he was tested so many times by Dak Prescott over the middle. When the offense doesn't turn the ball over, and the defense can get some takeaways of its own, the Bucs can make enough plays to win games. The key is doing it on a play-by-play and week-to-week basis. -- Jenna Laine 28. Washington Commanders (1-3-1) Week 5 result: Tied the Giants 27-27 (OT) Week 5 ranking: 27 Biggest issue on defense: Performing in the second half The Commanders are last in second-half points allowed per game (19) and 28th in second-half yards allowed per game (151.2). They have given up 20 or more points after halftime in each of the past four games, which includes a blown two-touchdown lead Sunday. One big issue has been a lack of pressure. Washington ranks 28th in sacks per dropback in the second half. Their secondary has played better, but it lacks playmakers. That issue, combined with little pressure, is why the Commanders are allowing a 53.1 third-down conversion rate after halftime. -- John Keim 29. Arizona Cardinals (1-4) Week 5 result: Lost to the Lions 45-21 Week 5 ranking: 29 Biggest issue on defense: Defending the pass The alternative answer was everything, and though that might sound hyperbolic, it's not far from the truth. Arizona is giving up a league-high 32.4 points per game and has the second-worst point differential in the NFL (minus-54). But the core of the Cardinals' defensive issues are coming against the pass. Arizona is giving up a league-worst 8.5 net yards per attempt and 236.8 passing yards per game (25th in the NFL). And when it comes time to stop touchdown passes, the Cardinals continue to struggle, with opposing quarterbacks completing 10.1% of their passes for touchdowns (the highest rate in the NFL). -- Josh Weinfuss 30. Los Angeles Chargers (0-5) Week 5 result: Lost to the Broncos 23-17 Week 5 ranking: 28 Biggest issue on defense: Allowing points in short-field situations According to defensive coordinator Chris O'Leary, a key emphasis for the Chargers during practice last week was the defense needing to rise up against a "sudden change opportunity." But they gave up points three times in four post-turnover possessions Sunday (a touchdown and two field goals) and the fourth was a missed field goal attempt. It's not an easy task; with the offense giving away a league-high 13 turnovers, short fields are becoming common. -- Anthony Gharib 31. Tennessee Titans (0-5) Week 5 result: Lost to the Texans 26-3 Week 5 ranking: 31 Biggest issue on defense: Poor communication on the back end Coach Robert Saleh's scheme has been tough for the secondary to grasp so far. That has been shown on some blown coverages leading to touchdowns this season. Some of it has been as simple as identifying which receiver is No. 1 on a particular side of the formation. Other times, it has been miscommunication in telling one of the defensive backs where to go in his deep part of the zone. Saleh has preached how it will take time for his players to master his scheme, but the clock is ticking as the losses keep accumulating. -- Turron Davenport 32. Miami Dolphins (0-5) Week 5 result: Lost to the Bengals 31-24 Week 5 ranking: 32 Biggest issue on defense: Rushing the passer It took the Dolphins until the first snap of their fourth game of the season to record their first sack; they have the NFL's second-worst sack rate. Their issues pressuring opposing quarterbacks has compounded into easy completions -- Miami ranks last in both opposing QBR and completion percentage. Going into the season, the Dolphins were thin at pass rusher behind Chop Robinson , but the 2024 first-round pick also started slow. With one of the NFL's youngest secondaries, Miami will continue to struggle against the pass until it can impact opposing QBs more consistently. -- Marcel Louis-Jacques

teamStories.title: Recruiting firm's Brian Flores memo contains racial stereotypes, lawyers say
teamStories.summary: A recruiting report on Brian Flores has examples of what his lawyers say are racial stereotypes that NFL teams use when evaluating Black coaching candidates.
teamStories.detailText: A recruiting firm's report on Brian Flores contains multiple examples of what his lawyers say are racial stereotypes that NFL teams use when evaluating Black coaching candidates. The memo from recruiter Korn Ferry, prepared for the Las Vegas Raiders during one of their recent coaching searches, was unsealed Tuesday as part of Flores' discrimination lawsuit against the NFL and three of its teams. "The recently unsealed documents demonstrate two unfortunate, but unsurprising, realities," Flores attorney Douglas H. Wigdor told Front Office Sports, which also published a copy of the Korn Ferry memo. "First, that Mr. Flores' decision to hold the league and its teams accountable for systemic race discrimination has been met with unlawful retaliation. Second, discrimination continues to play a significant role in the hiring process for NFL Head Coaches, as evidenced by the fact that the candidate profile prepared for the Raiders leans heavily on racial stereotypes." In its memo to the Raiders, Korn Ferry presented the headline "Brian Flores -- Strengths and Weaknesses" above two corresponding columns. One of the "strengths" listed by Korn Ferry said that Flores is: "Polished and a good presenter despite growing up in Brownsville, Brooklyn (same as Mike Tyson). He was able to build a strong friendship with a billionaire's son which gave him opportunities to socialize and learn how to build relationships with white-collar and upper-class individuals." Some of Flores' "weaknesses," according to Korn Ferry, are: • "He can fool you with his polish upwards. Has little people skills, lacks self-awareness and can sometimes exhibit erratic behavior. Tua's [Tagovailoa's] statements have opened the narrative that Brian was 'pessimistic and adversarial' and his style 'shattered his confidence.' • "Chip on his shoulder -- can be a dictator with players, coaches, and can even be difficult with ownership. His personality is unpredictable -- not sure who is going to show up. Failed in how he hires coordinators and staff because he doesn't give second chances or see efforts to improve." • "Needs someone strong at the top to reign [sic] in some of his worst behavior. He once threatened violence to his GM and made irrational demands during an ownership meeting. One long-time senior team executive said, 'He may have changed since, but he was the worst hiring decision we've ever made.' Another President of a club refused to talk about him." Flores attorney Michael Willemin told Front Office Sports that the report portrays Flores as an "angry Black man." Willemin cited the "polish upwards" reference as a racial stereotype that diminishes Flores' intelligence as a Black man. Willemin also pointed to the final item in the "weaknesses" column -- "Ongoing litigation may be a distraction" -- as evidence of leaguewide retaliation against Flores because of the lawsuit. Flores, who is Black, sued the NFL, Denver Broncos , New York Giants and Houston Texans in February 2022, alleging the league was "rife with racism" regarding its hiring practices when it comes to Black coaches. He was later joined in the lawsuit by fellow Black coaches Steve Wilks and Ray Horton. Flores, who was fired as head coach of the Miami Dolphins shortly before the suit was filed, is now the Minnesota Vikings ' defensive coordinator. He interviewed with the Broncos in 2019 and the Giants and Texans in 2022. Tagovailoa, who was cited in the "Weaknesses" column, played his first two NFL seasons with the Flores-coached Dolphins in 2020 and 2021. The veteran quarterback called Flores a "terrible person" in 2024 and said he began to believe he didn't belong in the NFL under Flores. Flores responded in August 2024 that he wished Tagovailoa well and acknowledged that he had "done a lot of reflecting on the situation, reflecting on the situation and communication."
